# MAG 7 Daily
> **4.4 gigawatts is the planned scale of Amazon's AI campus on a retired coal plant.**

**What You Need to Know:** 4.4 gigawatts is the planned scale of Amazon's AI campus on a retired coal plant. The Information's visit this week puts that campus on the old Homer City site in Pennsylvania coal country, a project few other cloud builders can finance the same way. The rest of the day is a Bogotá cloud zone switched on, a warning from Meta's AI chief, and a fight over who may read a phone screen.

### Top News
**4.4 gigawatts on a retired Pennsylvania coal plant: The Information**
The Information visited an Amazon data-center project this week near the economically depressed borough of Homer City, on a site that once held a 2-gigawatt coal-fired plant. The old plant employed thousands and released coal dust and arsenic. The project is described as gas-fired power into 36 buildings for the AI of Anthropic or others, the kind of site few companies can marshal resources for as readily as Amazon. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/amazon-plays-long-expensive-data-center-game-neoclouds)

**AWS activates first Colombian cloud zone in Bogotá: Telecompaper**
Amazon Web Services has activated its first Local Zone in Bogotá, bringing cloud infrastructure closer to Colombian users for applications that need single-digit millisecond latency. The facility is designed for real-time gaming, live video streaming, medical imaging and financial transaction processing. Source: [telecompaper.com](https://www.telecompaper.com/news/aws-activates-first-colombian-cloud-zone-in-bogota--1589682)

**Meta AI chief says superintelligence is coming: Calcalist**
Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang says AI systems could soon surpass human intelligence across almost every field and eventually improve themselves at a pace people cannot control, and that next year will be critical. He pointed to a reported proof of the Riemann Hypothesis — a problem he said occupied leading mathematicians for about 150 years, and a harder intellectual challenge, in his telling, than the atomic bomb he grew up beside in Los Alamos — and compared it with OpenAI's o3 model solving hard AIME problems in December 2024. He said coding, cybersecurity and limited-oversight task systems have advanced, with the remaining barriers in specialist knowledge, infrastructure, experimentation and data, and that AI could outperform human specialists in AI research, biological research, weapons development and economics. Maintaining control over unrestricted self-improvement, or over systems potentially 1,000 times more capable than humans, would be difficult, he said; he rejected the idea that superintelligence is inevitable and said society should not hand control to machines. Source: [calcalistech.com](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/hked2tbjqx) · [convergence-now.com](https://www.convergence-now.com/artificial-intelligence/meta-ai-chief-alexandr-wang-warns-superintelligence-is-coming-why-human-control-could-be-the-biggest-challenge/) · [aa.com.tr](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/science-technology/meta-ai-chief-says-superintelligence-is-coming-warns-next-year-will-be-critical/4134281)

**Protesters enter Meta's Delhi offices: The Verge**
Members of India's opposition Congress party protested outside Meta's offices in Delhi on Friday, and in a video shared by CNN they appear to have entered the building. The party's youth wing is demanding that Meta restore accounts of party leaders and has warned of more protests. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1039732/protesters-storm-meta-offices-in-india)

**Siri layoffs spared newer AI systems: MacRumors**
Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says Apple's recent Siri layoffs hit people working on the assistant's older infrastructure, not its newer AI systems, and that employees have yet to notice a major change in how Apple operates. Inside Craig Federighi's software engineering organization, an internal release calendar labeled A through G ties work to software versions; depending on the release, the roadmap for a major operating-system update is largely set by late summer or early fall of the year before, which Gurman says leaves little room to answer rivals that ship far more often than Apple's annual cycle. He also described Siri as slow, thinly tied to third-party apps, and worse at dictation. A more advanced Apple AI agent is not expected before late 2027; multistep control of Apple's own apps is expected in December, with third-party app support in 2027. Gurman said Apple's privacy reputation and deeper platform access could still help it compete as rival agents collect preferences and connected accounts. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/22/siri-layoffs-spared-newer-ai-systems/)

### Company Desk
**Samsung and Google set a December 10 US launch for AI glasses: UC Today**
Samsung says its intelligent eyewear, built with Google, will launch in the US on December 10, after pre-orders that opened on November 12, with Gemini, real-time translation, messaging, navigation, visual assistance and image capture. Cortney Harding, founder and CEO of Friends With Holograms, told UC Today the capabilities are not fully new, but that wearability and a deep tie to Google's own workplace tools set the glasses apart from Meta and Snap for companies already on Google Workspace. She expects office workers, not industrial crews, among the earliest users — the design is lightweight and not rugged, with what she called a good battery life — and pointed to translation, plus a Samsung scenario in which a wearer captures a whiteboard, asks Gemini to summarise it, and saves the notes to Samsung Notes. Gemini alone is not the deciding feature, she said; the larger step would be letting a company attach its own internal models, which she expects over time. Person recognition, she added, stays contentious unless it is a clear double opt-in in a controlled setting. Source: [uctoday.com](https://uctoday.com/are-samsung-and-googles-ai-glasses-ready-for-work)

**Bessent refuses to rule out Huang's return to Nvidia: Financial Times**
US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent has refused to rule out Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, saying it depends where the buck stops, as President Trump calls for the former chief's reinstatement. The Financial Times reported the comments against the still-open question of whether Huang comes back. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/91b7a3a6-8ac5-4327-ad03-6d951f287346?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

### Also Today
**MacBook Neo put on an annual cycle, Gurman says: MacRumors**
Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says Apple has put the MacBook Neo on an annual cycle like the Air and Pro, with a spring model code-named J701 moving from the A18 Pro and 8GB of memory to the A19 Pro and 12GB, frequent color refreshes, and a target at the low end of the Windows PC and Chromebook markets, while an iPhone 18, an iPhone 18e, an entry-level iPad and a MacBook Air are also aimed at about February or March, and an iPhone Air 2 plus new iPad Air and iPad Pro models a little later. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/23/macbook-neo-new-colors-every-year/) · [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/22/new-apple-products-february-or-march/)

**Nvidia-backed Firmus considers a $1.5 billion bond: Bloomberg**
Nvidia-backed Firmus Grid is considering about $1.5 billion in a bond offering as part of a larger debt financing, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg, after the company shelved an initial public offering last month. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-23/nvidia-backed-ai-company-firmus-mulls-1-5-billion-bond-offering)

**AWS is said to be weighing a Jabil arrangement: Newsquawk**
Business Insider reports that AWS is evaluating a potential deal with contract manufacturer Jabil that could save $300 million a year, a savings estimate rather than a stated deal value. Source: [newsquawk.com](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/aws-amzn-is-said-to-be-evaluating-a-potential-deal-with-jabil-jbl-that-could-save-usd-300mln-annually-business-insider-reports)

**iPhone Duo face unlock works in light, not in the dark: Bloomberg**
Mark Gurman, in a hands-on note, says iPhone Duo face unlock works in the light and fails in the dark, does not support Apple Pay, and that Touch ID on the Duo has been fully usable for him and is not a dealbreaker. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-11-22/apple-s-ai-agent-war-early-2027-product-plans-and-iphone-duo-face-unlock-review?accessToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzb3VyY2UiOiJTdWJzY3JpYmVyR2lmdGVkQXJ0aWNsZSIsImlhdCI6MTc5NTM1OTY0NCwiZXhwIjoxNzk1OTY0NDQ0LCJhcnRpY2xlSWQiOiJUT1dTQzFLSUpIOEwwMCIsImJjb25uZWN0SWQiOiJDNEVEQ0FFMUZBMDU0MEJFQTI0QTlGMjExQzFFOTA4MCJ9.jkEPTJXvP-oTyib7UR52QrKc8e6MQs5W0qfWIEz5aCw)

**Google's Mirror Dimension, a fake internet for agents: The Indian Express**
The Indian Express describes Google's Mirror Dimension as a fake internet built to train the company's AI agents. Source: [indianexpress.com](https://indianexpress.com/article/technology/artificial-intelligence/google-mirror-dimension-explained-fake-internet-ai-agents-10975011/)

### The Counterpoint
**A project that could become a park, while Nvidia-financed rivals hang on: The Information**
The Homer City campus is still a project a reporter toured, written up as what could become one of the largest AI power parks in the country, not as a park already delivering that power. The same piece says smaller cloud providers, which Nvidia has propped up financially, are trying to hang on — so the number that decides Amazon's lead is how much of the planned campus is actually online, against rivals that already have a chipmaker's money behind them. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/amazon-plays-long-expensive-data-center-game-neoclouds)

### The Thread: The screen an assistant can still read
On 20 November, Signal president Meredith Whittaker announced protections that stop Apple's Siri and Google's Gemini from reading chats displayed on a phone. On iPhones running iOS 27 or later, Signal 8.37 or later enables the block by default, under Settings, Privacy, Block Siri AI. That control also blocks screenshots and screen recordings in the app and hides Signal content in the App Switcher. If the app blocks a screenshot, a prompt offers ten minutes with protection off, and during that interval Siri may scan the visible chat. On Android the build is Signal 8.35.1. Screen security switches on the first time the app detects an assistant trying to read the screen, or a user can enable it in advance under Settings, Privacy, App security, Screen security. Turn it off through Signal's prompt and the app restores it after 90 days; turn it off manually in Settings and Signal says it will leave that choice alone. Active protection on Android also blocks screenshots and obscures the conversation in the recent-apps view. Microsoft met this problem earlier: in May 2025 Signal introduced screenshot blocking on Windows 11 to keep Recall from saving images of conversations. For macOS 27, Signal says it cannot provide equivalent screenshot blocking and recommends adding Signal under System Settings, Siri, Excluded Apps.

Those version lines sit on one mechanism. End-to-end encryption protects a Signal message only while it travels. Once the recipient opens the thread, the phone must show the words. An assistant that can see the screen can read the same words, without intercepting the message or obtaining a key. In a group chat, one person's assistant can capture lines written by several other people who never chose that assistant. Google's guide to Gemini screen actions says that with Intelligent Screen Context enabled, Gemini can infer when to use what is visible, and Google provides controls for screen text and screenshots. Apple's guide lists onscreen awareness among Siri's capabilities on compatible iPhones. Whittaker says engineers spent months identifying routes they could verify, and that other routes may exist, so a developer still cannot give users a complete account of what an assistant can reach. Signal is asking Apple, Google and Microsoft to document those routes and to let developers exclude an app's content across screens, notifications, files and software interfaces.

Apple's phone block does not follow the user to the Mac, so a person who shut Siri out of the mobile app still has to exclude Signal on the desktop or leave proactive access in place. Google's screen-aware Gemini hits a stop inside this app once Signal detects the read, unless the user opts out in the way the app has said it will remember. Microsoft's earlier desktop rule is the template the phones now follow: the price of keeping an assistant off the conversation is that an ordinary screenshot is treated as a leak. What changes is the limit of a privacy promise that used to stop at encryption. Apple, Google and Microsoft can still ship assistants that see a screen; users of this one app can refuse that sight; and nobody in a group thread can treat another member's assistant settings as someone else's problem. The step Whittaker wants from the three platform owners is a documented exclusion that covers every route an assistant uses. Source: [linkedin.com](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/signal-now-blocks-siri-gemini-from-reading-private-htgee)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Forty-eight Lambda calls now share one GPU model, so Amazon hosts inference without a cluster.**

**What You Need to Know:** Forty-eight concurrent Lambda invocations can now share one model in GPU memory, so Amazon runs event-driven inference without the customer operating a cluster. California has widened a Nvidia chip-sales inquiry to possible criminal violations of state law. Oakley Meta glasses are on sale in the Philippines, Amazon is closing in on Decart, and a Siri settlement has a per-phone payout range.

### Top News
**AWS Lambda runs GPU inference, forty-eight calls to a model: InfoQ**
AWS has added GPU support to Lambda: event functions on Lambda Managed Instances can run on EC2 G-series instances — G4dn, G5, G6, G6f, Gr6, Gr6f and G6e at launch — as container images, triggered by the same event sources as any other function. The feature is generally available in commercial regions where both Managed Instances and those G-series instances exist, priced at the EC2 On-Demand rate plus a 9.75 percent management fee and $0.20 per million requests. A capacity provider lists allowed instance types, the VPC and a vCPU ceiling; Lambda picks the newest generation with capacity and falls back when newer ones are short. Publishing a version provisions environments, downloads the weights and warms the engine before the first event; Seekable OCI lazy loading can cut environment start time by up to 70 percent. Launch limits include container images up to 32 GB, 32 GB of ephemeral storage, 2 to 32 GB of memory, 3 to 48 GB of accelerator memory, 15,000 vCPUs per capacity provider, and a timeout of up to 90 minutes for asynchronous and event-source mapping invocations. AWS ships five GPU base images — CUDA only, CuPy, PyTorch, vLLM and SGLang — and the two inference servers need no handler code. Source: [infoq.com](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-lambda-gpu-managed-instances/)

**Oakley Meta AI glasses go on sale in the Philippines: Speed**
The Oakley Meta Performance AI collection has debuted in the Philippines, starting at P38,295, at select Oakley and G-Force stores. The HSTN, for everyday wear, has a 12MP camera, video up to 3K, slow-motion and hyperlapse, open-ear speakers, an IPX4 rating, and a charging case that can provide up to 48 hours on the go. The Vanguard, for high-intensity sport, adds an ultrawide 12MP camera, video stabilization, Oakley’s Three-Point Fit with three interchangeable nose pads, and an IP67 rating, with 6 hours of continuous audio, 9 hours of daily use, and a case that adds 36 hours. Both include Meta AI with Strava and Garmin integration and 32GB of storage, enough for over 500 photos or more than 100 30-second videos. Source: [speed.ph](https://www.speed.ph/oakley-meta-ai-glasses-arrive-in-the-philippines-start-at-p38295/)

**California Nvidia probe looks at possible criminal violations: Bloomberg**
California’s probe into whether Nvidia illegally sold advanced chips to China and misled investors about that conduct is also looking at potential criminal violations of state law. Bloomberg reported that the criminal angle raises the stakes for the chipmaker. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-21/california-nvidia-probe-covers-potential-criminal-law-violations)

**Amazon closes in on a $7.5 billion Decart deal: Financial Times**
Amazon is nearing a deal to buy Decart, an AI start-up, for $7.5 billion, the Financial Times reported. The FT said the acquisition would help AWS compete with Nvidia in the race for computing power. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/dc7749dc-0f40-44a6-80bc-7f747d383616?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

**Siri AI settlement points to at least $61 per eligible iPhone: MacRumors**
Apple agreed in May to pay $250 million to settle a U.S. class action over Siri AI’s delayed launch, and MacRumors reported that claims remain open on the settlement website. Lawyers said in a court document this week that claimants will likely receive at least $61 per eligible iPhone, up to a maximum of $95, unless claims jump. Eligible claimants are U.S. residents who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 16, 16e, 16 Plus, 16 Pro or 16 Pro Max in the U.S., other than for resale, between June 10, 2024 and March 29, 2025. Apple denies the allegations and agreed to the settlement to avoid the costs and risks of a trial. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/21/apple-siri-ai-settlement-payment-amount/)

### Company Desk
**Experian and H&R Block arrive in Google Search: Digital Trends**
Experian, already in the Gemini app, has arrived in Search so people in the US can check a credit rating and shop for a personal loan, and H&R Block is in Search for tax calculations and refund estimates. Grocery Connected Apps were already available; these credit and tax tools are the new piece, and connecting an app is optional once a Google account is signed in. In the coming weeks, Angi and Thumbtack will also let users link accounts to Search. Source: [digitaltrends.com](https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-connected-apps-groceries/)

**Microsoft’s final Outlook report cites tests that missed the bug: GeekWire**
Microsoft says the bug behind last week’s global Outlook outage hit only newer servers in a key part of its network, and tests run on older ones missed it. The final report lists 13 fixes, including steps to keep a failure in one part of the world from spreading. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/microsofts-final-outlook-outage-report-details-testing-gaps-and-safeguards-that-backfired/)

**Tesla seeks a pollution-limit increase near a Fremont school: The Mercury News**
Tesla wants to raise a pollution limit nearly 60-fold near a Fremont elementary school. Parents are fighting the permit request. Source: [mercurynews.com](https://www.mercurynews.com/2026/11/21/tesla-fremont-factory-emissions-permit/)

### Also Today
**US officials describe an MSS campaign to acquire advanced AI chips: Techmeme**
Current and former officials from the US and other countries describe the Chinese spy agency MSS’s campaign to help Chinese companies acquire advanced AI chips, the New York Times reported. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Techmeme/status/2124397883705475098)

**Workers and the public oppose Amazon’s data-centre build: Financial Times**
Amazon’s plans for rapid data-centre expansion face opposition from the public and from its own employees, the Financial Times reported. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/d194e93b-8d3c-42eb-85dd-46d58c4f2a80?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

**Meta ads arrive in AWS Quick: Amazon Web Services**
Meta ads are now available in AWS Quick, Amazon Web Services said. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/meta-ads-is-now-available-in-aws-quick/)

**Nvidia nears a deal for diffusion startup Inception: The Information**
Nvidia is close to paying more than $500 million for Inception, a diffusion AI startup with just over 30 employees that had raised $50 million, The Information reported. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/theinformation/status/2124261594527936587)

**Amazon puts a Council warning on shipping labels: The Verge**
Amazon is putting labels on shipments claiming the New York City Council could add up to $5 to any Amazon order, while fighting a Delivery Protection Act that would effectively ban the third-party delivery arrangements it uses, The Verge reported. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1039564/amazon-nyc-council-packages-shipping-label)

**Nvidia’s board still will not rehire Jensen Huang: The Information**
Days after resigning, Jensen Huang said Tuesday he would be open to taking the job back, the board is still refusing to rehire him, President Trump on Friday said Nvidia should give him the job, and a letter purports to carry 10,263 employee signatures, about a quarter of the workforce, The Information reported. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/can-jensen-return)

**Three of four large districts push back on Google’s AI-or-Search line: Fortune**
Three of America’s four largest school districts are pushing back after Google told schools to accept AI or lose Search, Fortune reported. Source: [fortune.com](https://fortune.com/2026/11/21/google-search-ai-overviews-schools-chicago-nyc-los-angeles-miami/)

**Microsoft puts GPT-6.2 Sol in Copilot worldwide: Startup Fortune**
Microsoft is putting OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Sol in Copilot worldwide as its MAI models push in, Startup Fortune reported. Source: [startupfortune.com](https://startupfortune.com/microsoft-puts-openais-gpt-62-sol-in-copilot-worldwide-as-mai-models-push-in/)

### The Counterpoint
**The GPU function still waits on a zero quota and a cold publish: InfoQ**
Classmethod’s Akaike tried every accelerated instance type in us-east-1 and found 37 of 81 accepted, all G-family; P-family, G7, Inferentia, Trainium and the Graviton-based g5g were refused, as were zip packages. A PyTorch benchmark ran about 66 times faster on the L4 than on that instance’s CPU, but neither Terraform nor the Cloud Control provider knew AcceleratorConfig yet, and the GPU vCPU quota in a fresh account is zero — a g6.xlarge has 4 vCPUs, so the default three instances need a quota of 12. A second test put Gemma 4 E2B on one g6.2xlarge through the vLLM image, with Google’s 4-bit QAT weights and a speculative-decoding drafter in a 9 GB image: 417 calls succeeded, at roughly 130 tokens a second for a single request and 3,400 to 3,600 at full concurrency, after 484 seconds from publish to an active version. Source: [infoq.com](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-lambda-gpu-managed-instances/)

### The Thread: Search’s slower quarter, Meta’s larger bill
Up to $145 billion is the 2026 capital spending Meta has committed, and advertising is the business that has to earn it back. Yahoo Finance, citing the company’s results, says advertising was 98 percent of total revenue in the third quarter of 2026. Daily active users across the family of apps stood at 3.64 billion and were still growing. Ad revenue rose 25.9 percent year over year to $63.1 billion in that quarter. Average price per ad increased 14 percent, and impressions rose 10 percent.

The same piece sets that ad revenue just slightly below what Alphabet’s Google Search generated in the third quarter, and it says Search is growing at a much slower pace. That comparison is the shared ground. Both companies sell attention to advertisers. Only one of them, in this account, has turned free cash flow negative and paused share buybacks in order to fund the build. The article says spending is likely to be much higher next year. Susan Li, chief financial officer, said Meta is leveraging AI to make it easier for businesses to manage campaigns, develop creative, and act on performance opportunities. The piece adds that better recommendations drive engagement, engagement produces data on interests, and that data draws advertisers, with revenue then pushed back into the technology stack. Outside the ad line, Meta sells AI tools to small businesses and enterprises, has said it can sell excess compute to outside customers at premium prices, and offers a Muse personal agent that can bring subscription sales and a share of commerce revenue. Those lines are immaterial right now.

The dependency runs through the advertiser, not through a joint product. Alphabet’s Search business is the yardstick, so a slower Search growth rate is Alphabet’s number, not a cost Meta can hand it. Meta’s number is whether price and impressions keep rising once cash that used to repurchase shares is going into data centers instead. The article’s test is narrow on purpose. A thriving ad segment is the evidence it wants that the infrastructure spend is showing up in core operations. Tool sales, outside compute, and Muse are not, in its telling, large enough to answer the question.

The consequence splits. Meta is exposed if the ad gains stall, because the piece already describes cash flow turned negative and buybacks stopped, with a higher outlay still ahead. Alphabet is exposed differently: Search remains the slightly larger ad business in the quarter being compared, so Alphabet does not need Meta’s build to work in order to hold that position, but it does compete for the same campaign budget Li says Meta is making easier to run. Neither company gets a date in the article for the next set of figures. The deciding read is whether ad price and impressions repeat this quarter’s direction, and whether anything outside advertising stops being too small to matter. Source: [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/mark-zuckerberg-meta-platforms-pouring-043101493.html)

### On the Calendar
Claims in the Siri AI settlement can be submitted until December 21. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/21/apple-siri-ai-settlement-payment-amount/)

A final approval hearing in that settlement is scheduled for February 24, 2027. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/21/apple-siri-ai-settlement-payment-amount/)

Apple is opening an upgraded store at The Oracle in Reading in December, after closing the Festival Place store in Basingstoke. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/21/apple-store-in-uk-permanently-closing-today/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **YouTube is preparing to pay three billion dollars to settle school addiction claims.**

**What You Need to Know:** YouTube is preparing to pay $3 billion to thousands of school districts over claims that its addictive design harmed kids, in a deal Bloomberg sources described to The Verge as agreed in principle, with new safeguards for teens. The Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia’s accounting, on top of the difficulties that followed Jensen Huang’s resignation. Apple is putting daily limits on server-side Siri AI and Apple Intelligence in iOS 27.3, with higher allowances tied to iCloud+ plans.

### Top News
**YouTube prepares a $3 billion school-district settlement over addictive design: The Verge**
YouTube is preparing to pay $3 billion to thousands of school districts to settle claims that its addictive design harmed kids, The Verge reported, citing Bloomberg. Sources told Bloomberg that YouTube reached the agreement in principle, and that the deal would also include new safeguards for teens. The settlement would let Google avoid a wave of cases. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/streaming/1039096/youtube-social-media-addiction-school-districts-settlement)

**SEC opens an accounting probe as Nvidia deals with Huang’s exit: Financial Times**
The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia’s accounting, the Financial Times reported. The paper said the probe adds to difficulties facing the chip group after Jensen Huang’s resignation. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/9b28ed72-aac4-4291-9734-bf60b66645ab?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

**iOS 27.3 meters Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, then sells a higher cap: Mashable**
Apple is putting daily limits on server-side Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features with iOS 27.3, while basic Siri requests keep working after the advanced allowance is used up. Mashable, citing Apple, said the capped categories are separate: image tools including Clean Up, Extend, Spatial Reframing and Image Playground; AFM Cloud and AFM Cloud Pro models in Shortcuts; and third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute. Limits sit on the Apple Account and apply across iPhone, Mac and Apple TV. A limit prompt reads “Daily Request Limit Reached” and “You can continue with basic requests,” with a button to raise the cap through iCloud+. Apple’s published multipliers, as Mashable laid them out: the 50GB plan at $0.99 a month adds nothing; 200GB at $2.99 is up to 2x; 2TB at $9.99 is up to 5x; 6TB at $29.99 is up to 10x; 12TB at $59.99 is up to 20x. People already on an eligible plan get the increase inside that subscription. Limits reset at about midnight in the user’s time zone; travelers reset around midnight in the central time zone of the Apple Account’s country or region; a Family Sharing group resets around midnight in the plan purchaser’s time zone; someone not signed in resets about 24 hours after first use of that category that day. Unused allowance does not roll over. Source: [mashable.com](https://mashable.com/tech/ios-27-3-apple-intelligence-siri-ai-usage-limits-what-to-know)

**Google drops the desktop Search button and pins Gemini to the homepage: Startup Fortune**
Google began rolling out a redesigned desktop homepage on Thursday, November 19, 2026, Robby Stein, VP of Search, said on X. The Google Search button beside I’m Feeling Lucky is gone. Under the box sit Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm; shattered.io identified the image tool as Nano Banana. A collapsible sidebar holds Gemini chat history and tasks, a New chat control, and, per Engadget’s account in Startup Fortune, AI and ordinary search history, with each entry reopening in AI Mode. Pressing Enter still runs an ordinary search. Stein said: “People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done, and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress and continuing to explore the web.” The rollout is global, though 9to5Google noted availability may vary by account and device. Stein’s announcement covers the desktop homepage, not phone users or the Google app. Earlier server-side tests, including one for signed-out users, let file analysis and brainstorming work without an account while image generation needed a sign-in. Source: [startupfortune.com](https://startupfortune.com/google-drops-the-search-button-from-its-desktop-homepage-and-adds-a-gemini-chat-sidebar/)

**Google and Penn State describe a memory log so one model’s harness can teach the next: eu.36kr.com**
A paper from Google and Pennsylvania State University, reported by 36kr, proposes Continual Recursive Self-Improvement built on Self-Improvement Memory. The memory is a structured log of harness changes — prompts, tools and interception rules — not a rewrite of model weights. Each change stores a rationale and the code touched, predicted outcomes, observed outcomes, and the evaluation context of model and dataset. The account says a harness evolved on Claude Opus scored lower on Gemini than Gemini’s own starting harness, because the new model kept the result and lost the reason. In the cross-model test described, a harness evolved by Claude Opus 5.5, packaged with that memory, was handed to Gemini 3.8 Flash to keep optimizing. Source: [eu.36kr.com](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4078984519750789)

### Company Desk
**AWS Quick builds a business flow from a chat and runs several agents on one prompt: Amazon Web Services**
AWS Quick’s new release lets someone describe a process in chat and have Quick build a flow that orchestrates agents, skills and tools with access to structured data, knowledge and apps. Deterministic steps are there to make workflows consistent and verifiable, including longer-running workflows and large data volumes. The updated web app puts attention items and a daily briefing on the home screen, adds desktop agents and skills, and keeps work running after the tab closes. Multi-agent orchestration has several specialized agents work one request at the same time and combine what they find into one response. Quick can connect to Meta ads and Amplitude. Skills can be saved from the web app. Configurable content-safety and sensitive-information controls apply to user prompts. Language support adds Japanese, German, Chinese in Simplified and Traditional, and Vietnamese. In the finance example, a flow drafts a Microsoft Excel summary to a shared Space and tells the team in Slack that the draft is ready. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/new-in-aws-quick-more-capable-flows-an-updated-web-experience-and-agents-that-work-together/)

### The Counterpoint
**Three billion dollars is still an in-principle number: The Verge**
The figure that has to become a filing is the same $3 billion. Bloomberg’s sources, as The Verge reported them, said YouTube reached an agreement in principle, not that a court has entered a judgment or that the districts have been paid. Until that principle is a completed settlement, the wave of cases the deal is meant to avoid is still the live docket, and the teen safeguards travel with the unsigned deal rather than with a ruling. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/streaming/1039096/youtube-social-media-addiction-school-districts-settlement)

### The Thread: The cart, and the door that shuts
Google’s November 20, 2026 post put grocery ordering inside Search and the Gemini app for users in the United States, naming Albertsons, Safeway, Shaw’s and Target. Albertsons, Safeway and Shaw’s are banners of Albertsons Companies. In the published Target example, a request for a quick brunch returns product cards, and the first bakery card is Favorite Day Petite Butter Croissants at $6.49, sold by Target, rated 4.8 stars from 32 reviews. A follow-up that begins with [@Target](https://x.com/Target) asks for two bagels and cream cheese, strawberries, croissants, cold brew and juice, for pickup. The confirmation adds two Thomas Everything Bagels in an 18oz six-count pack at $3.99 each, quantity two, $7.98, and two Philadelphia Original cream cheese tubs at $4.19 each, quantity two, $8.38, plus Fresh Strawberries, Butter Croissants, Good & Gather Cold Brew Coffee and Tropicana Pure Premium pulp-free orange juice, for pickup at a store named Nashville West in Nashville, Tennessee. The cart panel shows a subtotal of $37.49 for 8 items. Google says the apps help build an order and check out, powered by the Universal Commerce Protocol, the open standard it linked to a January announcement. The same post says Experian, already live on the Gemini app, is rolling into Search so U.S. users can check a credit rating and shop for a personal loan; that H&R Block can calculate taxes and estimate refunds from Search; and that links to Angi and Thumbtack accounts in Search arrive in the coming weeks, for jobs from a leaky faucet to last-minute decorations.

Amazon is closing the other door on its own store. Mezha and The Register reported that Amazon is blocking shopping bots on its main site while AWS Marketplace opens to agent purchases. Google is letting a conversation assemble a retailer’s cart inside Search. Amazon is keeping outside agents off the flagship site and allowing agent buying on the cloud marketplace instead.

The shared dependency is the last step of a purchase: who is allowed to turn a suggestion into an order, and on whose system the cart lives. Google’s protocol is the pipe it wants agents and merchants to share, dropped onto the page people already open, next to a chat sidebar that keeps the thread. Amazon’s block keeps third-party agents away from the catalogue, the reviews and the fulfillment on the main site, and points permitted agent spending at infrastructure the company already bills as cloud. One assistant is being invited into the grocer’s cart. The other company’s store is being reserved for shoppers Amazon is willing to serve itself.

For Alphabet, a holiday list, a credit check, a tax estimate and, within weeks, a home-services booking can start in Search, so the retailer’s app is no longer the only front door to its own inventory. For Amazon, an outside shopping agent that cannot enter the main site has to stop, hand the task to a person, or buy through the marketplace path AWS is opening. The next marker Google actually dated in prose, not on a calendar, is those Angi and Thumbtack links, described as arriving in the coming weeks. Source: [ppc.land](https://ppc.land/google-puts-target-and-albertsons-grocery-carts-inside-search-and-gemini/) Source: [mezha.net](https://mezha.net/eng/news/mezha-b5dc0024c454ba8e7ac4455d_amazon_blocks_shopping/) Source: [theregister.com](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/11/20/amazons-split-personality-aws-embraces-bot-commerce-while-main-site-enforces-bans/5311493)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Dozens of clicks become one Gemini prompt on a Mac, while your cursor stays free.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google’s Gemini app for Mac can now turn work that normally takes dozens of clicks into one prompt, running in a background window so the cursor stays free. Amazon will let agents put fixed-price Marketplace purchases on an AWS bill. Nvidia is in talks to buy a diffusion-model startup for at least $500 million, and two prepaid energy deals meant to provide $3 billion to Alphabet are paused.

### Top News
**Google Lets Gemini Control Mac Desktops: Silicon UK**
Google said computer use in the Gemini app for Mac is available starting today, so one prompt can run multi-step work across local files, desktop apps and the web. Gemini works inside an isolated background window with a live preview in the chat, and the main screen and cursor stay free. Google says the user chooses which apps Gemini can access, can watch every step, pause at any time, and approve key actions before they happen. Silicon UK reports the feature is initially in English in the United States and requires the Gemini desktop app plus a Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra subscription. Google’s examples include batch color-grading photos, pulling weights, dimensions and addresses from local PDFs into shipping quotes, building a Google Slides deck from dashboard screenshots, and staging resale listings from a folder of clothing photos. The same week, Google began a broader rollout of Tasks, which can carry out multi-step online jobs such as purchases and booking appointments. Source: [silicon.co.uk](https://www.silicon.co.uk/cloud/ai/gemini-macos-agent-632450) Source: [betanews.com](https://betanews.com/article/google-gemini-control-macos/)

**AWS Lets AgentCore Agents Buy Marketplace Products Through AWS Billing: Unite.AI**
Amazon said on November 19, 2026 that Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments can settle purchases from x402-enabled AWS Marketplace sellers through AWS Billing. Agents can buy software, APIs, data and content per request in US dollars, with the charge added to the developer’s AWS bill, and those purchases do not need a stablecoin wallet or an API key. A seller answers an unpaid call with HTTP 402 and a signed quote; if the session still has budget, AgentCore returns a payment token that Unite.AI says stays valid for about five minutes, and Marketplace rejects a quote whose price was altered. The first purchase from a seller creates an AWS Marketplace agreement; later purchases are tracked against it, recorded in CloudTrail and Cost Explorer, and settled before they appear on the monthly bill. A failed budget check leaves the developer uncharged. The sample separates roles so a session role can set a budget but cannot pay, while an agent role can pay but cannot create sessions, and Private Marketplace can limit the catalog. The documented walkthrough defaults to a $0.05 session budget and a $0.02 cap per request; in AWS’s test the agent compared two listings and completed one $0.01 payment. Source: [unite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/aws-lets-agentcore-agents-buy-marketplace-products-through-aws-billing/) Source: [superpowerdaily.com](https://superpowerdaily.com/posts/aws-lets-ai-agents-charge-pay-per-request-marketplace-purchases-to-cloud-bills)

**Nvidia Nears Acquisition of Diffusion AI Developer for More Than $500 Million: The Information**
Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire Inception, a two-year-old startup that builds diffusion large language models meant to run faster than the models behind ChatGPT and Claude, The Information reported, citing three people with knowledge of the discussions. One of those people said the proposed deal is worth at least $500 million, plus earnout awards for the new employees if they hit certain goals. That person said the models and the team are supposed to aid Nvidia’s Nemotron open-source models. The report describes the talks as still moving after Jensen Huang’s resignation as chief executive. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/nvidia-nears-acquisition-diffusion-ai-developer-500-million)

**Alphabet Energy Deals Delayed Amid Weak Muni Market: The Information**
Two prepaid energy deals that would provide $3 billion to Alphabet have been paused, The Information reported, citing Bloomberg. The briefing attributes the pause to muted investor demand and market shakiness, and to a slowdown in the municipal bond market. The deals are still expected to go ahead. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/alphabet-energy-deals-delayed-amid-weak-muni-market)

### Company Desk

WhatsApp is gradually rolling out a higher group-chat cap, 1,500 participants instead of 1,024. 9to5Mac reported the increase as a gradual rollout. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/19/whatsapp-is-raising-group-chat-limit-to-1500-participants/)

### Also Today

Pixalate said its OpenEPG module, announced in London on November 19, adds show, channel, genre and content rating to connected-TV bid requests on AWS RTB Fabric, mapping 770,000-plus U.S. streaming shows, including live sports, across 17,900-plus FAST and linear channels on eight platforms, with single-digit latency. **Google Announces $15M in Funding to Advance Water Stewardship in Iowa: River Cities' Reader**

**Google’s 3D emoji has wild Android spec requirements: 9to5Google**
9to5Google reported that Google has now published minimum Android specifications for the 3D emoji introduced on Pixel this year: 10GB of free space and 6GB of RAM. Source: [9to5google.com](https://9to5google.com/2026/11/19/android-3d-emoji-specs-requirements/)

**Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up: Ars Technica**
Ars Technica reported that Amazon is fighting the Delivery Protection Act with a homepage banner and an in-app pop-up, and said the company is using its shopping platform for political purposes. Source: [arstechnica.com](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/11/amazon-takes-its-fight-against-nyc-delivery-bill-to-shoppers-with-in-app-pop-up/)

**Announcing custom execution roles for AWS CloudFormation StackSets: Amazon Web Services**
CloudFormation StackSets can now take a customer template for the execution role in each member account instead of the default AdministratorAccess role, which also lets service-managed stack sets deploy nested stacks, macros and transforms; switching does not delete the default role. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/announcing-custom-execution-roles-for-aws-cloudformation-stacksets/)

### The Counterpoint
**Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac: TechCrunch**
The Mac that Gemini is now driving is still Apple’s, and Apple is tightening who else gets to drive it. TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, says the upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple told developers it planned additional controls so that this level of access requires very explicit user action. The same reporting says Apple is hiring a senior engineering manager to build an agent that browses, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, privately. Bloomberg’s account, as relayed by TechCrunch, is that Apple has eyed introducing that service as soon as the end of next year, and that progress remains in the early stages. TechCrunch asked Apple for more information and did not receive a response. The open question is whether those macOS 27.3 warnings and the explicit-consent control land before, or on top of, a third-party agent that needs broad access to apps, files and the web. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/apple-may-be-developing-its-own-ai-agent-that-runs-your-mac/)

### The Thread: The Mac an agent still has to rent
Nearly 1,000 organizations were running Devin on macOS within six weeks of launch, Cognition told Amazon in an architecture post. Devin could already draft Swift on Linux. Building, testing and signing an app for iPhone, iPad or Mac still required Apple hardware and macOS, and Devin Cloud did not offer that until a couple of months ago. Sessions had run only on Linux and Windows virtual machines. Without Xcode, the agent depended on a customer’s continuous-integration system or that customer’s own Mac fleet. A clean compile still does not show behavior. The post’s example is an iPhone game that should resume where the player paused: the agent has to play, pause, quit, relaunch and confirm the saved state.

Amazon’s answer is EC2 Mac. Each instance is a physical Mac mini or Mac Studio attached to the Nitro System, so Cognition runs Apple’s Virtualization framework as it would on a Mac it owned. Dedicated Hosts come through the EC2 API rather than a shipping dock. The fleet is in six AWS Regions. A fresh macOS virtual machine starts in under a minute, which Cognition estimates is 15 to 20 times faster than a customer setting up a Mac host. Each Dedicated Host has a 24-hour minimum allocation, so the life of a session is split from the life of the host. Where capacity is not already reserved, an Auto Scaling group allocates and releases hosts. On each host, a Cognition manager boots guest VMs from images Cognition prepares. A disk keeps the session’s work so an idle session does not hold a VM. Network rules follow the session. A live view and an accessibility tree from accessibility-cli let both the user and Devin see and operate the app.

The shared limit is Apple’s license. The macOS Software License Agreement allows up to two additional copies of macOS in virtual environments on each Mac, and macOS enforces that cap, so each bare-metal host runs two isolated Devin workspaces. Idle sessions release those VMs, and one host can serve more than one session in a day. Apple is the only legal hardware and the only OS that can sign the app and run the iOS Simulator. Amazon is the API, the regions, the virtual private cloud and the EBS boot volume that make those Macs look like other EC2 instances. Cognition wrote the agent. Neither of the other two did.

What changes is who has to own the machine. A customer no longer keeps a private fleet just so an agent can open the simulator before it hands back a merge-ready change. Cognition can start a clean guest, with Xcode tools and the simulator, and return the host to later work the same day. Apple’s license still bounds how many copies sit on one computer at once. Amazon’s host minimum still means the bill works only if many short sessions share a machine. The post names no further launch date. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/ai-coding-agents-on-amazon-ec2-mac-how-cognition-scales-devin-for-macos/)

### On the Calendar
Pixalate chief executive Jalal Nasir and chief technology officer Amin Bandeali will present the OpenEPG module with AWS at re:Invent 2026 in Las Vegas, November 30 through December 4. Source: [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/media-advertising/articles/pixalate-launches-openepg-db-amazon-035000473.html)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Moonshot scrapped a $150 million Nvidia chip rental after a new U.S. rule.**

**What You Need to Know:** Moonshot AI scrapped a $150 million rental of Nvidia Blackwell chips in an Indonesian data center after the U.S. restricted remote access to advanced chips. Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon for coding and long tasks, and New York, Los Angeles and Chicago are weighing a break with Google Search. Amazon opened a shared cache for self-hosted models, and Disney put AWS inside three Star Wars robots.

### Top News
**China’s Moonshot AI Scraps $150 Million Deal to Access Nvidia Chips in Indonesia: The Information**
Moonshot AI, the Beijing developer of the Kimi models, has scrapped a $150 million deal to reach Nvidia Blackwell chips through a data center in Indonesia, after the U.S. this week announced a rule restricting Chinese companies from accessing advanced chips remotely, two people with direct knowledge told The Information. Moonshot had signed with a Southeast Asian neocloud to rent a sizable cluster of Blackwell Ultra B300 chips, with access starting as early as next year. The B300 is barred from sale to China. Remote rental from data centers outside China had been the workaround; the Commerce Department rule released this week closed it. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/chinas-moonshot-ai-scraps-150-million-deal-access-nvidia-chips-indonesia)

**Gemini 4 Neon: Google's new $3 AI model for coding: DNE Africa**
After shipping Gemini 4 Hydrogen for speed, Google on Wednesday released Gemini 4 Neon, placed between Hydrogen and Carbon and aimed at coding, analysis, science and long agent tasks. Google priced it at $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 per million cached inputs and $15 per million output tokens, with a context window of up to 1 million tokens across text, PDFs, charts, audio and video, and four thinking levels. Google said Neon scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, third overall, and ranked first on that firm’s coding-agent index; InfoWorld reported a coding-agent score of 58.6, plus 65.2 percent on Terminal-Bench 4.1, and dev.ua reported SWE-sweep rising from 12.8 percent in a base shell to 39.0 percent in Antigravity without a model change. Google said a task at the default high setting costs 32 percent less than on Gemini 4 Carbon, and quoted Glean saying Neon matched Carbon’s quality at three times the speed. It replaces Argon for Google AI Pro, $19.99 a month in the U.S.; free users and AI Plus, at $4.99 a month, do not get it, and DNE Africa said Google’s benchmarks have not been independently replicated. Source: [africa.dailynewsegypt.com](https://africa.dailynewsegypt.com/gemini-4-neon-launch/) · [dev.ua](https://dev.ua/en/news/google-gemini-4-neon-1795081523) · [infoworld.com](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4250618/google-launches-gemini-4-neon-touting-lower-costs-for-complex-ai-coding-tasks.html) · [notebookcheck.net](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Gemini-4-Neon-replaces-Argon-for-Google-AI-Pro-subscribers.1454281.0.html) · [digitaltrends.com](https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-says-gemini-4-neon-can-hang-with-claude-opus-5-5-and-gpt-6-2-sol-for-less/)

**The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search: The Verge**
New York, Los Angeles and Chicago schools are considering alternatives to Google after the company said that, starting next year, schools cannot turn off Gemini-powered features without also losing Search, The Verge reported, citing The New York Times. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools that turn off Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search.” New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders responded harshly, The Verge said. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1037151/school-districts-ditching-google) · [gizmodo.com](https://gizmodo.com/nyc-la-and-chicago-school-districts-all-discussing-alternatives-to-ai-pilled-google-2000842174)

**Announcing distributed KV caching for self-hosted LLMs with Amazon ElastiCache: Amazon Web Services**
Amazon said distributed KV caching is generally available on ElastiCache for Valkey, a shared cache beside a GPU fleet that stores key-value state computed during prefill. Amazon said it cuts self-hosted inference cost by up to 40 percent and time to first token by up to 80 percent. Existing engines, including vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM, connect through the open-source LMCache connector with a configuration change and no code changes. In Amazon’s account of tests on B300 GPUs, prefill takes seconds for a 32K-token prompt, tens of seconds for 100K tokens and minutes past 250K; coding-agent traces from SemiAnalysis and TraceLab show more than 95 percent of prompt tokens sit in prefixes already processed. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/announcing-distributed-kv-caching-for-self-hosted-llms-with-amazon-elasticache/)

**At All Hands, Nvidia Interim CEO Tried To Reassure Employees, Prevent Talent Loss: The Information**
At Nvidia’s all-hands on Wednesday, interim CEO Colette Kress tried to steady employees and limit a talent exodus, people present told The Information. She said they can expect pay raises and more equity at the end of this year. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/hands-nvidia-interim-ceo-tried-reassure-employees-prevent-talent-loss)

### Company Desk
**You turned off Gemini history? Google still keeps everything for two months: Korben**
Korben reported that turning Gemini history off does not stop Google keeping the chats for two months. Tech Times reported that AI Mode temporary threads have launched with no stated retention, and that Gemini chats are now kept two months. ### The Thread: Scripted aliens, two robot suppliers
In 1963 Disney opened the Enchanted Tiki Room on audio-animatronics locked to one script. On Wednesday Disney and Amazon described three Anzellan robots — Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a and Jibu Bre’a — that react to guests, to the workshop and to each other, with the cloud side on AWS.

Kyle Laughlin, senior vice president of Walt Disney Imagineering research and development, technology and engineering, told The Hollywood Reporter the Amazon work goes back more than a decade, from Disney+ into daily Imagineering. The species was in The Rise of Skywalker and in the 2026 film The Mandalorian and Grogu. BigGo Finance said these three were created with Lucasfilm for this project, and that the build took just a few months. Vilo leads. Kado is a droid mechanic who wants attention. Jibu, his twin, is shy. They mix English — Galactic Basic, in the story — with Anzellan, and they pick from a large bank of lines recorded in advance.

Concealed cameras and microphones read the scene. Samira Panah Bakhtiar, AWS general manager for telecommunications, media, entertainment, games, advertising and sports, said each figure tracks three streams at once: the guests in front of it, the workshop, and the other two characters. A fast model handles an instant move, such as eye contact. Larger models shape a longer exchange. Imagineers wrote every action and every line. The model chooses inside that script and does not write new words on the spot. AWS engineers used the coding tool Kiro to turn the ideas into software, and people approved the code. Imagineers also used Amazon Bedrock, which can call foundation models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta by task. Bakhtiar said the cloud tools shortened the path from concept to a working system by orders of magnitude compared with not using them.

Nobody drives the figures from backstage. What they do changes with how many people are present and with whether those people are children or adults. A birthday badge or a particular Star Wars shirt can become the topic. Laughlin said guests want meetings that feel genuine, and that today’s audio-animatronics are scripted in how that meeting happens. BigGo said the three are expected at a Disney park after the conference showing.

Disney is not doing the robot work with one supplier. BigGo reported a robotics partnership with Nvidia, including Olaf from Frozen as a walking robot at Disneyland Paris and at Hong Kong Disneyland, and a guide robot under consideration for a Disneyland parking lot. Laughlin described characters from a single franchise moving and talking together, and he indicated the pattern is meant to spread past Star Wars.

Amazon is supplying the cloud, Kiro and the model switcher for lines a person still wrote. Nvidia already has walking characters in two Disney parks, and a parking-lot guide still on the table. Meta is not building the bodies, but its models are on the Bedrock menu, so the reasoning step need not be an Amazon model. The guest hears a recorded line. The new piece is which company’s software picks it, in the room, with no one behind the curtain. # MAG 7 Daily
> **NVIDIA's Vera rack links 192 CPUs for science at over 200 terabytes a second.**

**What You Need to Know:** NVIDIA's Vera rack links 192 CPUs for science at over 200 terabytes a second. The liquid-cooled platform is NVIDIA's first fully custom data-center CPU system, aimed at climate modeling, molecular dynamics and other scientific work that does not run on GPUs. Microsoft, at Ignite, put Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot and described Copilot as the new operating system for work.

### Top News
**NVIDIA unveils Vera CPU rack-scale platform for HPC: Engineering.com**
NVIDIA announced the Vera CPU rack-scale platform, pairing its first fully custom data-center CPU with Quantum-X800 InfiniBand for climate modeling, molecular dynamics and other scientific workloads that are not accelerated on GPUs. The liquid-cooled rack brings together 192 Vera CPUs and delivers more than 200 TB/s of aggregate peak memory bandwidth. Each Vera CPU has 88 custom Olympus cores and 176 threads, with serviceable SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X memory delivering up to 1.2 TB/s; the rack holds about 300 TB of memory and 1 petabyte of storage in an MGX design that reuses NVL72 chassis, power and cooling, with eight CPUs, NVMe storage and management in each 1U tray. Quantum-X800 connects the system, and SHARP in-network computing is meant to cut the time processors spend coordinating. HPC SDK 26.11 is available now, including a public beta of a next-generation Fortran compiler so existing Fortran programs can run faster on NVIDIA platforms without a rewrite, and Vera racks are expected from Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro beginning in early 2027. Source: [engineering.com](https://www.engineering.com/nvidia-unveils-vera-cpu-rack-scale-platform-for-hpc/)

**Microsoft puts Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot: Digital Trends**
At Ignite 2026, Microsoft made Word, Excel and PowerPoint generally available inside Copilot, and chief executive Satya Nadella described Copilot as the new operating system for work. Files created there stay editable in the corresponding Office apps, and Microsoft 365's security and compliance controls cover them. Autopilot, in the Frontier early-access program, is a cloud agent meant to take ongoing work such as email and calendar catch-up once permissions are granted; each agent gets its own identity, administrators can revoke access, activity is recorded, and some actions can require human approval. Work IQ draws on company email, meetings, files and relationships. Microsoft 365 holds roughly 19.5 exabytes of customer business data, Jared Spataro wrote, and Home — merging Chat and Cowork, with Auto routing a request to a model — is the interface he says the workday will start in; Today, a private-preview scan of mail, calendar and Teams, can draft replies. Copilot Code, which builds dashboards and apps from plain language, moves to general availability in December. Digitimes reported that Microsoft also unveiled in-house coding and cybersecurity models it says come close to OpenAI and Anthropic models at a fraction of the cost. Estimates of employee time saved are calculated with a model rather than measured directly, Digital Trends reported. Source: [digitaltrends.com](https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/microsoft-wants-copilot-to-be-your-new-workspace-with-word-excel-and-powerpoint-built-in/) · [siliconangle.com](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/18/at-ignite-2026-microsoft-reinvents-copilot-as-the-autonomous-engine-of-enterprise-work/) · [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261118VL218/microsoft-copilot-coding-security-operating-system-2026.html) · [startupfortune.com](https://startupfortune.com/microsoft-puts-word-excel-and-powerpoint-inside-copilot-and-calls-it-a-new-os-for-work/)

**Nvidia's board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang: The Information**
Hours after Jensen Huang posted that he would return as chief executive if the board decided that was in the interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America, chair Harvey Jones said on Tuesday's earnings call that the board does not intend to reinstate him. Jones added that the exit followed disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms. The Information reported that the affairs — with a subordinate and a business partner — were the cause, not concerns about possible chip smuggling into China. Huang's morning statement said he had made serious mistakes in his personal life and would cooperate with the board's independent investigation. Apple said developers' proceeds on eligible app and in-app sales have been adjusted in four countries for new taxes: Botswana's 14 percent value-added tax, a 3 percent significant-economic-presence tax in Cameroon, a 3 percent SEP tax in Côte d'Ivoire, and Rwanda's 18 percent VAT. In Botswana and Rwanda, the Paid Applications Agreement will state that Apple collects and remits applicable taxes, and a Software-as-a-Service attribute is now available for the App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating and Boosting categories. From December 3, developers on automatic pricing will see app and in-app prices change in five countries for tax and foreign-exchange moves; prices will not change in a base storefront, for auto-renewable subscriptions, or where developers set prices manually. From January 1, 2027, those SaaS and related categories become subject to California sales and use tax; U.S. storefront prices are shown excluding tax, so displayed prices stay put, developer proceeds stay the same, and the total a customer pays, including tax, may rise. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/17/apple-announces-app-store-price-changes-in-multiple-countries-new-california-tax-rules/) · [mezha.net](https://mezha.net/eng/news/mezha-deee179be8de3520163c23b5_apple_announces_app/)

### The Counterpoint
**NVIDIA's own tests, and a forecast labeled projected: Engineering.com**
The speed claim that has to survive a customer's benchmark is still NVIDIA's. In NVIDIA's tests, Vera delivered 1.9 times the performance and 2.4 times the performance per watt of x86 systems on one OpenFOAM case, the motorBike Large airflow simulation. On the open-source Weather Research and Forecasting model, the gains NVIDIA cites are projected: 1.6 times the performance and 2 times the energy efficiency versus x86. Those four multiples, not the core count, are the numbers that decide whether the rack changes a climate or airflow run before a buyer has it. Source: [engineering.com](https://www.engineering.com/nvidia-unveils-vera-cpu-rack-scale-platform-for-hpc/)

### The Thread: The revenue under an open chair
Nvidia's third-quarter revenue was $115.8 billion, up 103 percent from a year earlier, including $107.6 billion from the data-center business, interim chief executive Colette Kress said on Tuesday's earnings call. The company raised its forecast for next fiscal year's revenue growth to about 75 percent, from 70 percent. Yesterday the open question on this spending cycle was whether guidance would move; that raise is the move. Kress spent 13 years at Microsoft earlier in her career. She said customers, suppliers and employees remain behind the company, called the transition business as usual, and ended the call with "We've got this."

Amazon's founder answered the vacancy from outside the building the same day. Jeff Bezos, now co-chief executive of the AI engineering startup Prometheus, said at Semafor's Silicon Valley and the World event that if Nvidia does not bring Jensen back he would not hire an outsider. Nvidia is too complicated, he said. Outside chief executives at complex companies, he added, have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding, and he would treat that hire as a last resort. He said Blue Origin is using Prometheus tools on two projects. When Semafor raised his 2021 handoff of Amazon to Andy Jassy, the longtime insider who built AWS, Bezos called the comparison a poor one. There has never been a more carefully planned transition, he said, and he did not know enough about Nvidia's board meetings to say whether Huang should return. He called Huang a remarkable founder who deserves admiration and respect no matter what. Asked about his own calendar, he described running Prometheus as nirvana.

Huang had already pointed inward. In a Bloomberg interview recorded October 14 he said he hoped his successor was already inside the company. He was chief executive for 33 years. Harvey Jones, the longtime director named Nvidia's first board chair last week, said the search will include internal and external candidates, that the board wants a permanent chief executive quickly, and that it will not rush the pick. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker asked the board to leave open a return. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives wrote in a Sunday note that talk of a comeback is ridiculous.

What changes is who is allowed to carry the book those three companies already touch. Amazon's own handoff, the one Bezos refused as a template, put the person who built its cloud in the chair, and he is now telling Nvidia's directors that an outsider is a last resort even while their search still lists external names. Microsoft is not bidding for the job; it is the company that trained the interim who just signed the higher growth forecast and told customers the quarter was ordinary. Nvidia's candidates, inside or out, inherit a data-center franchise whose interim steward came from that Microsoft career and whose most famous outside adviser built Amazon by promoting from within. Investors who want the former chief executive kept in play are asking the chair to hold a door he has framed as a search. Customers heard the interim say the company still has it. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/jeff-bezos-has-some-advice-for-nvidias-board-on-its-ceo-search/)

From January 1, 2027, specified app categories become subject to California sales and use tax. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/17/apple-announces-app-store-price-changes-in-multiple-countries-new-california-tax-rules/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **More than 50,000 CUDA cores define Nvidia’s Rubin HPC for science, shipping in 2028.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia used Supercomputing 2026 to unveil Rubin HPC, a GPU it says carries more than 50,000 CUDA cores and will ship in 2028 for scientific simulation. The current Rubin tops out at 28,672 CUDA cores. A Commerce Department license rule on remote chip access, a new Nvidia board committee, and an Apple memory contract sit beside that roadmap.

### Top News
**Nvidia unveils Rubin HPC with more than 50,000 CUDA cores: AI Weekly**
Nvidia used Supercomputing 2026 to tee up Rubin HPC, a GPU with more than 50,000 CUDA cores that it says will accelerate agentic workflows and simulation for scientists, engineers, and analysts working with large data sets. The current Rubin tops out at 28,672 CUDA cores. Nvidia is framing the part as a balanced design, pairing more compute with faster node-to-node movement over NVLink 7, which retains the 3.6 TB/s of per-GPU bandwidth already shipping on NVLink 6. Tom’s Hardware reports the design likely reuses a four-die layout similar to Rubin Ultra, linked by NVLink-C2C. Nvidia says Rubin HPC will arrive sometime in 2028. Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and HPC, said faster simulation means faster discovery. Source: [aiweekly.co](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/nvidia-unveils-rubin-hpc-gpu-with-over-50000-cuda-cores-at-sc26-shipping-2028)

**US requires licenses for some Nvidia chip sales, and curbs remote access: Bloomberg Technology**
The Trump administration moved to restrict foreign countries from giving Chinese companies remote access to advanced AI chips and servers, amid scrutiny of semiconductor export controls following an alleged Nvidia espionage scandal. Several Southeast Asian nations, along with Brazil, will need a US government license to purchase advanced AI chips from Nvidia and other American manufacturers, according to an interim rule released by the US Commerce Department. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2026-11-17/us-moves-to-curb-china-s-remote-access-to-nvidia-s-chips-video) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2026-11-17/breaking-down-the-us-move-to-curb-remote-access-to-chips-video)

**Nvidia’s board adds an export-control committee: NVIDIA Newsroom**
Nvidia’s board established a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee for board-level oversight of national security policies, export-control compliance, and global trade risk management. Director Suzanne Nora Johnson will chair it, with directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. The committee will meet at least quarterly, including with management and in executive session, and will retain independent outside experts in law, national security, and trade compliance. The existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report to the committee and to interim CEO Colette Kress on day-to-day operations. Chairman Harvey Jones said Nvidia has a responsibility to help safeguard national security while supporting continued innovation. The Financial Times reports the move comes as the company faces criticism in Washington over its ambition to increase revenues in China, after the US moved to cut off China’s access to Nvidia’s most powerful AI chips. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-of-directors-establishes-national-security-and-export-control-oversight-committee) · [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/aeacbf89-5511-4d1c-81c2-b4c227bdfceb?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

**Apple nears a four-to-five-year DRAM deal with Samsung: MacRumors**
Apple is close to signing a long-term DRAM supply agreement with Samsung, Korea’s Maeil Business Newspaper reported. The deal would run for four to five years from the first half of 2027, set a minimum supply volume, and leave prices to be finalized later based on market conditions. Apple usually favors short-term contracts and presses suppliers on price. It recently signed a similar deal with SK hynix on supplier-favorable terms as a worsening memory shortage pushes up component costs amid the AI data-center buildout. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/17/apple-rare-long-term-memory-deal-samsung/)

**Blackstone takes 75 percent of an AWS data-center portfolio: Telecompaper**
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust agreed to acquire a 75 percent majority interest in two joint ventures holding data-center assets leased to Amazon Web Services, its first investment since listing on the New York Stock Exchange. The transaction values the portfolio at approximately $5 billion. It covers 13 newly constructed powered-shell buildings across two AWS campuses in the United States, representing 647 MW of IT capacity. ### The Counterpoint
**Core count meets a 3 percent benchmark: AI Weekly**
Rubin HPC’s headline core count is the claim that has to survive procurement math. AI Weekly, citing the HPCG benchmark, says top supercomputers achieve only 3 percent of theoretical peak on sparse workloads, the benchmark most relevant to Rubin HPC’s target uses, and that two procurement cycles sit between this tease and silicon in 2028. The Vera CPU rack — 192 CPUs, about 300 TB of memory, and 1 PB of storage — arrives in early 2027, a full year before Rubin HPC ships. Source: [aiweekly.co](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/nvidia-unveils-rubin-hpc-gpu-with-over-50000-cuda-cores-at-sc26-shipping-2028)

### The Thread: A desk, a partner cloud, a chip raise
Nvidia, Alphabet, and Meta are each trying to place advanced compute where a shared queue is not the default. Nvidia’s DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit, already on sale at SC26, links four Spark units into 512 GB of memory and 20 TB of NVMe. Each node is a GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip with 128 GB of LPDDR5X, 6,144 CUDA cores, up to 1 PFLOP of FP4, a 140-watt thermal design power, and 273 GB/s of bandwidth. Twenty Arm cores split into 10 Cortex-X925 cores at up to 4 GHz and 10 Cortex-A725 cores at up to 2.8 GHz. ConnectX-7 joins each box to two neighbors in a ring, so the kit needs no separate switch. Nvidia says NVFP4 lets those four nodes run models of up to 700 billion parameters, a class it illustrates with DeepSeek V4.1. The Rubin Lab at the University of California, Berkeley, Nvidia says, received genomic results 15 times sooner than a workflow stuck in an 11-hour cluster queue. Berkeley’s Hartwig Group fine-tuned a 120-billion-parameter-class chemistry model on a single Spark using NVFP4.

The shared problem is who holds the machine, not who posts the largest core count. At the same conference, cuPhoton.xBeam cut Event Horizon Telescope analysis from one month to 8 minutes. KTH Royal Institute used Nemotron for Science to repair 81 percent of faulty molecular-dynamics simulations overnight; the toolkit includes Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model and the LitmusBench v0.2 dataset. TCBP-JOBS cut a design step from 12 weeks to 45 minutes. In Brussels, Google said select Gemini models are coming to Google Cloud Dedicated, operated by an independent local partner on isolated infrastructure. Select Gemini models already carry a commitment to process customer data in-region in the EU, and Gemini is already available with Google Distributed Cloud. In France, S3NS has made managed model serving generally available on PREMI3NS, so teams can deploy Mistral and Google open models, or their own, inside an environment S3NS operates. Confidential External Key Management is in preview, designed so customers or a local partner hold root keys outside Google while key operations run in a hardware-attested confidential-computing environment. A Telefónica partnership in Spain, also in preview, expands who can hold those keys. A Data Boundary framework for Switzerland is available today. A framework for the EU’s DORA act is planned for financial services.

What changes is the path, not a single delivered campus. A lab can develop on the four-node ring with Nvidia’s HPC SDK — GPU-accelerated C, C++, and Fortran plus MPI — then scale to larger Nvidia supercomputers; LAMMPS and NAMD are confirmed on the four-unit kit, and the community reports that GROMACS, OpenFOAM, and WRF also run. A European hospital or finance team can aim Gemini at a partner-operated cloud while key control is still partly a preview and Switzerland already has a mapped framework. Meta’s route is a custom memory program: a Korean outlet reports Samsung is developing HBM4E for Meta’s AI chips on a 2nm base die. Cassava Technologies is seeking to raise as much as $1 billion to buy Nvidia chips for African AI data centers, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg — a raise being sought, not a cluster switched on. The kit is the piece already on sale, through partners including Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, H3C, HP, Lenovo, MSI, and xFusion, and through the Nvidia Marketplace.
