# MAG 7 Daily
> **Forty Amazon Leo satellites were destroyed ten minutes after liftoff, delaying a thirty-eight-flight Vulcan order.**

**What You Need to Know:** A United Launch Alliance Vulcan failed about ten minutes after liftoff Sunday and destroyed 40 satellites for Amazon Leo, the joint venture’s first total mission failure since 2006 and the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon bought. Apple opened a U.S. health-AI study with OpenEvidence for up to 200,000 adults, with study data barred from model training. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Nvidia to shake up leadership and explain export-control compliance days after Jensen Huang’s ouster.

### Top News
**Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites in a ULA Vulcan launch failure: GeekWire**
United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan failed about ten minutes after lifting off from Cape Canaveral on Sunday and destroyed 40 satellites for Amazon’s Leo internet network, The Information and GeekWire reported. It was ULA’s first total mission failure since the Boeing–Lockheed Martin joint venture was formed in 2006, and the first of 38 Vulcan launches Amazon has purchased. ULA said it does not yet have specific data on what went wrong and will work with Amazon to return to flight as quickly as possible. Amazon had said a second Vulcan mission could fly within weeks; that flight now waits on the investigation. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-loses-40-leo-satellites-as-ula-vulcan-launch-failure-deals-setback-to-tech-giants-starlink-rival/) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/amazon-loses-40-leo-satellites-ula-rocket-failure)

**Apple launches a study of how people use AI for health: TechCrunch**
Apple opened the Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform, and a study app that answers health questions with linked, peer-reviewed citations. TechCrunch reported the company wants up to 200,000 participants, aged 21 and older, for more than 12 months; The Tech Outlook said eligible phones are Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone 15 Pro or later models running iOS 26 or later. Participants can rate answers and may share HealthKit types such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results. Apple said study data will not be used to train AI models; TechCrunch reported the data is anonymized before it goes to a secure third-party cloud and that OpenEvidence deletes query and response data after 24 hours. The app is available to download starting today. Sumbul Desai, Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said insights from the study should help build trusted tools as the technology evolves. TechCrunch noted that OpenAI said earlier this year users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/15/apple-launches-new-app-to-study-how-people-use-ai-for-health/) · [thetechoutlook.com](https://www.thetechoutlook.com/new-release/software-apps/apple-announces-the-launch-of-the-apple-health-ai-usage-study-to-evaluate-the-use-of-ai-for-health/) · [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1033355/apples-new-study-looks-to-improve-the-effectiveness-of-ai-health-tools)

**Bessent says Nvidia leadership needs a dramatic shakeup: Bloomberg**
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Nvidia to make a dramatic leadership shakeup and come clean about compliance with export controls on its AI chips, Bloomberg reported, days after the company ousted Jensen Huang. Colette Kress, the finance chief, is interim chief executive. The Information reported that confidantes are informally seeking to reinstate Huang, that others close to him say there is no official effort, and that Bessent is pushing the board to look outside. The Financial Times reported that Huang’s exit removes a vocal supporter of open AI systems, which it said boosts Anthropic and OpenAI. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-15/nvidia-s-ceo-search-draws-fire-with-bessent-s-call-for-shakeup) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/huang-weighs-nvidia-comeback-bessent-pushes-board-look-outside) · [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/418ca885-fbcf-4b9f-a8b9-2bd60b543fc5?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

### The Counterpoint
**Forty birds are not the constraint the FCC already wrote down: GeekWire**
Amazon Leo posted that risk comes with any launch, especially an inaugural mission, and that it believes ULA will learn and still deliver on long-term Vulcan plans. The Federal Communications Commission in June let Amazon keep deploying after it missed a July 30 deadline to have 1,616 satellites in service, but satellites that were not operational by then temporarily lose priority in key spectrum bands. Vulcan was the rocket slated to carry more than 1,500 of the 3,232 first-generation satellites, and the full fleet still faces a July 30, 2029 deadline. The number that decides the setback is how many birds are operational before that spectrum priority stays lost, not whether forty satellites are a large share of the paper constellation. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-loses-40-leo-satellites-as-ula-vulcan-launch-failure-deals-setback-to-tech-giants-starlink-rival/)

### The Thread: The ride above the satellite
Before this flight, Amazon had 396 Leo satellites up, flown on 14 missions since April 2025. The last success was in July, and it closed the Atlas 5 chapter: eight Leo missions on that older rocket, the last of them carrying 29 satellites. Vulcan was built to lift a heavier stack than that Atlas flight. Melissa Wuerl, Amazon Leo’s director of launch systems, had called it the program’s primary workhorse for the next several years. The network those satellites serve is based in Redmond and was formerly Project Kuiper. Amazon has said it still plans an initial commercial internet rollout this year.

The rocket that failed is a stack of other companies’ engines, which is why a ten-minute flight becomes a multi-firm investigation even when only one of the seven owns the payload. Sunday’s mission was Vulcan’s fifth, the vehicle’s first since a January 2024 debut to fly with six solid boosters, and the first Vulcan flight in nine months. Those Northrop Grumman boosters had thrown nozzle failures on the second flight, in October 2024, and again on a national-security mission in February. Both of those flights still reached orbit, but the Space Force paused Vulcan national-security launches after February. ULA flew this mission with an improved nozzle. The first stage is powered by two BE-4 engines from Blue Origin in Kent, Washington. ULA chief executive Mark Peller said before the flight that those engines had been retrofitted for the oxygen-valve problem behind a New Glenn ground-test explosion in May. The six boosters appeared to perform normally and burned out in less than two minutes. The anomaly came during the burn of the Centaur upper stage, which carries two RL10 engines made by L3Harris. GeekWire, citing Spaceflight Now, reported that the first stage appeared to burn longer than planned and that a telemetry animation showed the Centaur making unusual orientation adjustments early in its burn. Liftoff was at 12:40 p.m. Eastern after two days of delays and a countdown hold at 20 seconds for a technical issue; it is not known whether that issue played any role. Leadership on the rocket side already turned over once: longtime ULA chief Tory Bruno left last December for Blue Origin, and Peller, who led Vulcan’s development, was named chief executive in August.

What changes for Amazon is the order of the remaining book, not a new design of the satellite. New Glenn, the other Bezos-linked rocket, has 24 Leo launches reserved and has been grounded since that May explosion, so it is not a spare engine sitting on the pad. Ariane 6 and SpaceX’s Falcon 9 are also on the manifest. The next dated ride is an Ariane 6 targeted for November 23 at the earliest, carrying 36 satellites. Until ULA names a cause, the heavier Vulcan cadence Amazon bought as its primary workhorse stays in the hangar, and every other rocket in that book has to absorb a schedule written for a vehicle that just failed its first flight in nine months. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-loses-40-leo-satellites-as-ula-vulcan-launch-failure-deals-setback-to-tech-giants-starlink-rival/)

### On the Calendar
An Ariane 6 mission carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites is targeted for November 23 at the earliest. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-loses-40-leo-satellites-as-ula-vulcan-launch-failure-deals-setback-to-tech-giants-starlink-rival/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **5,248 Nvidia employees joined a petition past 100,000 names to reinstate Jensen Huang.**

**What You Need to Know:** A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang passed 100,000 signatures on Saturday, including 5,248 people who said they are current Nvidia employees, and by Saturday afternoon the count was above 115,000. Italy’s data-protection authority fined Meta €805 million ($887 million) for accessing Android users’ gallery photos and videos without explicit consent. Apple Intelligence is approved for iPad and Mac in China ahead of a December rollout, and Firmus is seeking $3 billion privately with prepayments from Nvidia and Meta.

### Top News
**Thousands of Nvidia staff sign to bring Huang back: The Information**
A petition urging Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang passed 100,000 signatures on Saturday, The Information reported, including 5,248 people who said they are current employees. Signers named there include Elon Musk, Epic Games’ Tim Sweeney and Y Combinator’s Garry Tan. By Saturday afternoon TechCrunch put the total above 115,000, with the petition site listing 5,965 current employees, 1,108 former employees and 63,063 shareholders, plus Replit CEO Amjad Masad among notable supporters. The text says signers are concerned Huang was removed without meaningful due process, demands that the board bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, and says he deserves due process, not mob justice. Huang resigned Thursday, four days after confessing to an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy, and he has agreed to testify before Congress. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/thousands-nvidia-staff-sign-petition-bring-back-huang) Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/14/elon-musk-other-tech-execs-sign-petition-calling-on-nvidia-to-reinstate-jensen-huang/)

**Italy fines Meta €805 million over Android galleries: Bloomberg**
The Italian Data Protection Authority fined Meta Platforms €805 million ($887 million) for accessing photos and videos in Android users’ galleries without their explicit consent, Bloomberg reported. Reuters carried the same fine as $887 million over Android users’ data access. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-14/italy-fines-meta-805-million-over-access-to-users-photos) Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/italy-fines-meta-887-million-over-android-users-data-access-2026-11-14/)

### The Thread: A capacity upgrade, then a thundering herd
Microsoft’s Microsoft 365 failure lasted about 30 hours, and the company now says the break was introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade, then showed up after a more recent network change. GeekWire, reading Microsoft’s incident log, puts the disruption at about 30 hours across more than 70 countries. TechXplore puts products offline in at least 74 countries and territories in the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa. The services named were Outlook, Teams and Copilot. Microsoft called it a technical issue, not cyber and not related to AI or agents, and on Saturday said the remaining customers and regions had service again.

Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, said cascading failures and thundering herds at the network perimeter made recovery harder than normal. In his account a thundering herd is huge numbers of devices reconnecting at once and overwhelming systems as they return. Microsoft told customers a preliminary post-incident report would come within two business days and a final report within five. He said the write-up would include a step-by-step timeline and many repair items, and that the company would be very specific.

The load on that perimeter is a January number Microsoft reported: more than 450 million paid commercial Microsoft 365 seats. GeekWire’s reading is roughly one seat for every 18 people on Earth. Unity Health Toronto declared a Code Grey and said patient care continued. Pennsylvania lawmakers went about 18 hours without email. A Colorado jail could not take online bond payments. Business Upturn, citing Nikkei, said securities firms and asset managers in Japan fell back on fax machines when trade-confirmation email stopped. New York’s Emergency Management office warned of delays reaching city agencies. In Singapore some government systems, including email, were disrupted. In London the UK Supreme Court was not receiving email.

It was at least the fourth significant outage of this kind this year. A January outage lasted nearly 10 hours. In July a bug in Microsoft’s automated network maintenance system disrupted Azure and Microsoft 365 for hours. On August 31 an Exchange Online outage also hit Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint. GeekWire sets those failures next to earlier incidents at Amazon Web Services: a second cloud operator, the same class of customer dependence. Friday’s FAA ground stop was not part of the Microsoft incident. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no connection, and Microsoft said it had no indication the ground stop involved any Microsoft service. Federal officials blamed aging FAA telecom gear.

What the two companies share is the reconnect problem, not this week’s fault. The incident account gives Amazon no role in the upgrade. Customers still treat both perimeters as one risk, because a network change at either can drop mail, chat and an assistant together, then worsen as devices rush back. Microsoft owes the specific repair list its Copilot executive already promised. Amazon inherits the comparison buyers will use the next time its own change window fails. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/i-hope-this-email-finds-you-microsoft-declares-outage-over-as-the-world-digs-out-of-its-inbox/) Source: [techxplore.com](https://techxplore.com/news/2026-11-microsoft-global-outage.html)

The company blamed an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a recent network change, and described it as a technical fault not related to cyber or AI agents. The Federal reported that Teams chats and meetings returned before some Exchange Online calendar features, that OpenAI and Anthropic's Microsoft 365 connectors were affected, that IndiGo and Akasa Air reported email problems while Air India rerouted email and flights continued, and that NHS staff in the UK turned to paper records. Microsoft said it had no indication the ground stop was related to its disruption and that a full post-incident report will follow the review. Source: [thefederal.com](https://thefederal.com/category/business/microsoft-fixes-global-outage-affecting-microsoft-365-and-copilot-across-74-countries-262900) Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/dhs-chief-sees-no-microsoft-link-to-faa-ground-stop-says-possible-ai-role-being-investigated/)

The endpoint predicts joint 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, small-molecule ligands and the complexes they form, and it runs with network isolation so sequences stay in the customer's account. A real-time SageMaker request is capped at 60 seconds, so this model uses asynchronous inference with an invocation timeout of up to one hour, and the endpoint can scale to zero instances when the queue is empty. The lease guarantee is a commitment already written; the funding behaviour around Nvidia is what founders are marking down. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/13/jensen-huangs-departure-blasts-big-hole-in-ai-startup-funding-vcs-and-founders-say/)

### The Thread: Cost per solved task
NVIDIA server version 0.3.0 of NeMo Switchyard is the open-source library Amazon's sample uses to choose which Amazon Bedrock model answers a coding agent. The sample installs switchyard-server 0.3.0 from crates.io and runs LiteLLM image version 1.102.0, both in one container on Amazon Elastic Container Service on AWS Fargate in private subnets. Amazon says NVIDIA documents that server release as a demo and evaluation component, and Amazon calls the integration experimental sample code, not a production deployment.

A coding agent works in tasks. The developer asks for a change; the agent reads files, edits code, and runs tests until the work is done. One task can take a few model calls or dozens. Token price does not equal task price, because the bill depends on how many turns a model needs, how much history each turn replays, and how often a run is retried or never finishes. Every attempt is paid, including attempts that never finish. Amazon's score is cost per solved task: total cost of the runs divided by the number of runs whose tests pass.

The library supports two strategies through LiteLLM. Stage routing reads recent tool activity and results in the history, so the agent must send the full conversation, then picks between a capable model and a lower-cost efficient model. Random routing picks from the configured models, with optional weights, for splits and comparisons. Neither strategy calls a judge model. LiteLLM has also shipped a native Switchyard stage router as an auto-router. Deployment in the sample uses the AWS Cloud Development Kit, and Amazon tells customers to clear the design with security and legal teams and to test it in a non-production account first.

Amazon hosts the gateway and the models; NVIDIA supplies the chooser. The agent sends an OpenAI-compatible request with the model field set to switchyard and a shared gateway key. Only the IPv4 range the deployer allows can reach the hostname, which sits on a load balancer with an AWS Certificate Manager certificate. AWS WAF applies IP-reputation, known-bad-input, and per-IP rate limits. The load balancer forwards only three paths, chat completions, models, and a health check, and returns 404 for every other path. LiteLLM checks the key, the plugin picks the model, and the call goes out through the Bedrock Converse or ConverseStream API on the task's own identity role, via a runtime interface endpoint so the traffic stays on Amazon's network. The header x-litellm-model-name names the model that answered.

The split of work is the change. Amazon gets a harness that compares a routed group with single-model baselines on a customer's own workloads, which is how the post says to judge the router. NVIDIA gets its library in the request path of agents that already speak a common format, without operating the gateway or the capacity those agents consume. The benchmark runners in the sample are the step the post actually specifies for deciding whether that split is worth keeping. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/route-coding-agent-requests-to-the-right-model-on-amazon-bedrock-with-nvidia-nemo-switchyard/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Gemini 4 Hydrogen scores 51, one point ahead of Google's larger Argon.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, one point ahead of the larger Argon model, and is rolling into Search and the Gemini app. Apple is selling HomeView and a new Apple TV 4K at 299 dollars each, with HomeView kept out of the European Union. Nvidia's board has Jensen Huang's resignation and finance chief Colette Kress as interim chief executive.

### Top News
**Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Mashable**
Koray Kavukcuoglu, senior vice president at Google DeepMind, announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon for speed, and said that at its default high thinking level it surpasses frontier model Gemini 4 Argon. Analytics India Magazine reported a score of 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at that default, against 50 for Argon, rising to 54 at a new extra-high setting. Google said Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at the default high level and scored 57 percent on Terminal-Bench 4.1, against 18.2 percent for Flash. The price is 1.50 dollars per million input tokens and 7.50 dollars per million output tokens across a context window of up to 1 million tokens, and the model is rolling out in Search, the Gemini app, the Gemini API, Google AI Studio and Gemini for business. Kavukcuoglu framed it for code, tests and everyday work, or as the fast engine beside Carbon and Argon; Orchestrator in Google Antigravity switches among the models and, on Terminal-Bench 4.0, landed near Carbon's success rate while using 24 percent less quota and finishing 19 percent faster. Google also said Hydrogen is two times less likely than 3.8 Flash to step past permission boundaries, and that it still hallucinates. Source: [mashable.com](https://mashable.com/tech/google-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-launch) Source: [analyticsindiamag.com](https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-for-faster-coding-and-ai-workflows)

**Apple Launches Two Products Today: MacRumors**
Apple is selling HomeView and a fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, each priced at 299 dollars, after pre-orders that opened in mid-October. HomeView is a smart-home display running Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, in tabletop and wall-mounted models, and it can recognize up to six users by face, each with a personalized Home Screen. The Apple TV 4K adds Siri AI, the A19 chip, an updated Siri Remote with Find My, 128GB of storage and four-speaker surround sound with HomePod mini 2. Both were announced on October 13 alongside HomePod mini 2, which launched on October 30. HomeView is not sold in the European Union because Siri AI is unavailable on iOS there under current regulatory constraints; Apple said it is "working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward." Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/13/apple-launches-two-products-today/)

**Nvidia announces CEO change as Jensen Huang resigns: Verdict**
Nvidia's board said Jensen Huang resigned immediately as president, chief executive and director. The board that was already looking for a chief executive now has that resignation in hand, with Colette Kress — finance chief since September 2013, after nearly 25 years in finance roles at Microsoft and Cisco — as interim chief executive while she keeps the finance job, and a formal search of internal and external candidates underway. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993; the exit followed reports of an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and The Information reported that general counsel Tim Teter asked him at home whether that report was true and that Huang said it was. The board named Harvey Jones, former chief executive and executive chairman of Synopsys, Nvidia's first chair; Jones said the board expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to continue without interruption. Bloomberg, citing documents it reviewed, reported that a Chinese company founded by Alice Huang procured smuggled AI chips that were installed at a Shanghai data center with links to Megaspeed. The Financial Times reported that Huang had supported keeping sales of Nvidia chips open to China. Source: [verdict.co.uk](https://www.verdict.co.uk/nvidia-jensen-huang-resigns-ceo-change/) Source: [info-reader-production.herokuapp.com](https://info-reader-production.herokuapp.com/articles/sex-lies-ai-chips-jensen-huangs-last-days-nvidia-ceo) Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-13/banned-nvidia-chips-installed-at-china-data-center-linked-to-alice-huang) Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/0d4e93e4-895e-4ae0-a01b-833a3ed440a8?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

By Friday Microsoft said a configuration patch on upstream authentication and routing had improved server stability, and engineers were widening that fix toward regions entering peak business hours. Copilot executive Charles Lamanna said there was no indication the incident was malicious or cyber activity. Source: [coinpaper.com](https://coinpaper.com/38790/microsoft-365-outage-hits-130-000-users-as-outlook-teams-and-copilot-services-fail-worldwide) Source: [itpro.com](https://www.itpro.com/software/microsoft/microsoft-365-outage-disruption-continues-with-issues-spanning-copilot-exchange-and-sharepoint)

### Company Desk

### The Counterpoint
**Free accounts still land on Flash-Lite: Notebookcheck**
The 51-point score does not mean a free user can choose Hydrogen. Notebookcheck, citing Google, says free users get it only through automatic model selection when Google judges the prompt suitable, that most prompts still go to Flash-Lite, and that turning auto selection off sends every reply to Flash-Lite. On Google's plans page, Google AI Plus at 4.99 dollars a month now lists Hydrogen as its headline model, with twice the free tier's usage limits, and the Pro model starts on Google AI Pro at 19.99 dollars, which also includes Argon. Google's help page on Gemini models still lists Pro under AI Plus, so the two pages disagree. Source: [notebookcheck.net](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Gemini-4-Hydrogen-What-free-users-and-Google-AI-Plus-get.1449493.0.html)

### The Thread: The mail server under the assistant
Nearly 130,000 Outlook problem reports showed up on Downdetector in the United States shortly after 1 p.m. Eastern on November 12. Microsoft 365 drew more than 38,000 additional reports and Teams about 4,500, Coinpaper said — user submissions, not a verified customer count. La Veu Lliure put the broader Downdetector tally near 200,000 reports in more than 70 countries. UC Today clocked the Exchange incident from 16:17 GMT Thursday to a 07:25 GMT Friday update that still had the suite in service degradation, more than 15 hours on. At 17:54 GMT Microsoft described an Americas impact; at 18:07 GMT it said users in any region could be hit; at 18:26 GMT it opened a suite-wide incident.

The load was not extra traffic. By 19:18 GMT Microsoft had concluded that many servers failed automated health checks and dropped out, so the machines still up took the work. A process that sets up secure connections became overwhelmed, and those servers stopped processing requests. At 19:06 GMT the company paused deployments and configuration changes, then started reverting a network change that correlated with the start of the impact. Machines brought back online failed again once traffic returned. At 04:10 GMT Friday, steps in some regions were not producing a sustained recovery. At 05:01 GMT the mitigations had driven a surge of calls from routing services onto backend servers, and some machines were stuck in a bad state, blocking a force-sync of the network change. At 06:56 GMT Microsoft reported only marginal success from patching and rebooting.

Teams split on that Exchange line. Joining calls and meetings, group chats, channel messages and standard channels largely kept working. Calendars, scheduling, invites, meeting edits, Live and Virtual events, contact sync, and creating or deleting private or shared channels did not. SharePoint sharing with people outside an organization broke, while files stored in SharePoint stayed available. A separate North America Teams incident, from 15:40 to 17:09 GMT Thursday, was fully resolved. The public Azure status page showed no Azure issues. A Dynamics 365 contact-center incident locked agents out for just under eight hours; Microsoft restored that access at 00:57 GMT Friday, while email, the usual overflow channel, was already impaired.

OpenAI said new Microsoft 365 connections may be broken and tools are not working as expected. Anthropic said mail, calendar and search in its Microsoft 365 connector were failing for most requests, and that Claude for Outlook was affected. Those assistants do not run the mail system; they call it, so a fault in Exchange reaches products Microsoft does not own. Verdict, in its account of the Nvidia leadership change, also noted that earlier this month Microsoft and Nvidia introduced Frontier Launchpad, a support programme for AI software companies in the UK and Ireland.

> **Hundreds of agents wrote AWS Emulator, and Amazon's engineers never reviewed the code.**

**What You Need to Know:** Amazon says autonomous agents wrote AWS Emulator, a free local stand-in for AWS, and its engineers neither wrote nor reviewed the code. Google is putting Gemini on Apple CarPlay without a wake word, and the Commerce Department is finishing a rule to block remote access to advanced AI chips. Meta is hiring a longtime AWS infrastructure executive to run its own build.

### Top News
**AWS Emulator: Open-source tool for testing AWS apps locally, built by autonomous AI agents: Help Net Security**
Amazon Web Services has released AWS Emulator, a free tool that simulates AWS services on a laptop, a development server, or in a continuous-integration pipeline, Help Net Security reported. The company says autonomous agents wrote it entirely. Senior principal engineer Matthew Goldberg said, "The emulator was written entirely by autonomous agents. Our team hasn’t written or reviewed any of the code," because guardrails kept the agents inside set lines. Three agent teams divide the work: one builds tests from public API specifications and checks them against real AWS, one runs those tests on the emulator and groups failures, and one fixes a single problem per agent. Hundreds of agents fix thousands of issues a day against a library of tens of thousands of tests, and a change enters the main codebase only after build checks and agent reviews for coding standards, security, and fidelity. Developers can start it through an AI coding agent, a Linux package, Docker, or an embedded mode inside a Rust test process. There is no extra service fee — users pay for AWS resources when they deploy — and the code and fidelity tests are on GitHub under a CC0 public-domain dedication, with per-service fidelity scores published at each release. Source: [helpnetsecurity.com](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/12/aws-ai-agents-built-emulator/) Source: [cloudcomputing-news.net](https://www.cloudcomputing-news.net/news/aws-cloud-emulator-ai-agents/)

**Google’s Gemini AI Assistant Now Works On Apple CarPlay: Yahoo Autos**
Google is rolling Gemini out on Apple CarPlay so an iPhone user can open the app from the car screen and continue a conversation, Yahoo Autos reported, and The Mac Observer dates the global start to November 11. The driver has to tap the icon. Gemini does not wake on a voice command, because Apple does not allow third-party wake phrases or an always-on microphone. Only Siri has that privilege, though a driver can ask Siri to launch Gemini. Once it is open it runs full screen, so the navigation route is not visible during the chat, and the driver can interrupt, change subject, or pause. With permissions it can read Gmail and Google Calendar, and CarPlay chats sync back to the Gemini app on the phone. The app is free, covers supported Gemini Live languages, and appears after the latest Gemini app is installed, the microphone is allowed, and Gemini Live has been used at least once on the phone. Last month Google also put Gemini into the CarPlay mode of Google Maps. Apple opened the door to third-party conversational apps in iOS 26.4 without letting them replace Siri or take over vehicle functions. Source: [autos.yahoo.com](https://autos.yahoo.com/ev-and-future-tech/articles/google-gemini-ai-assistant-now-074246913.html) Source: [autoevolution.com](https://www.autoevolution.com/news/google-gemini-now-available-on-carplay-apple-still-blocking-the-feature-everybody-needs-278295.html) Source: [macobserver.com](https://www.macobserver.com/news/google-gemini-now-available-on-apple-carplay/)

**Commerce Department Finalizing Long-Awaited AI Remote Access Rule: The Information**
The Commerce Department is finalizing a rule to stop Chinese AI firms from remotely using advanced AI chips through data centers in other countries, The Information reported, citing two people familiar with the process. The rule would expand existing semiconductor controls at the Bureau of Industry and Security to seven more countries, including Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand, to block remote access and chip smuggling into China. Commerce is still consulting other agencies before it can be finished. The Information said the step could answer criticism that the department has been slow on limits that influential companies, including Nvidia, have opposed. ### The Counterpoint
**The emulator will not tell you whether a permission holds: Help Net Security**
AWS Emulator is the wrong tool for the question that matters in a real account: whether a person or a policy is allowed to touch a resource. Help Net Security reported that it does not evaluate AWS Identity and Access Management or resource-based policies the way AWS does, so it should not be used to test security, and it is not intended for production workloads. Fidelity varies by service and feature. Behavior is checked against AWS in US West (Oregon), except global services, which are checked in US East (N. Virginia). All emulated resources sit in memory and disappear when the emulator stops. AWS has not tested it for long-running use or load testing, and the documentation says to use one region and one account because the emulator does not keep resources separate by region or account. Source: [helpnetsecurity.com](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/12/aws-ai-agents-built-emulator/)

### The Thread: The AWS operator Meta wants on its own machines
Santosh Janardhan joined Facebook in October 2009. More than seventeen years later, Meta is taking him off day-to-day leadership of infrastructure and installing Dave Brown, who spent nearly twenty years at Amazon Web Services, with Brown assuming that organization in early 2027. Citybiz reported the change from a Bloomberg account of an internal employee memo. Janardhan helped oversee the computing systems behind Meta’s global operations, including its data centers, networking infrastructure, engineering platforms, and custom-designed chips. He remains through the first quarter of 2027 to assist the transition, then becomes chief technology officer of Meta Compute, where he will advise on technical strategy and maintain relationships with key technology partners. Brown joined Meta earlier in 2026 as vice president of infrastructure. At AWS he most recently served as senior vice president responsible for compute and machine-learning services.

Under chief executive Mark Zuckerberg, Meta is committing hundreds of billions of dollars to data centers, advanced processors, networking equipment, and engineering talent. In the memo, Janardhan described the infrastructure organization as having evolved from a supporting technology function into a competitive advantage. During his tenure Meta expanded its global data center network and invested in proprietary silicon, advanced networking technology, and systems designed to improve computing efficiency. The stated aim is capacity for more sophisticated models and for AI-powered services across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and the wider ecosystem. The appointment runs through Amazon and Meta because the executive who managed large-scale compute and machine-learning services at AWS is the person Meta is placing over its own build. Amazon is the company that developed that operating experience inside the cloud business that rents capacity. Meta is recruiting it while it designs its own chips and grows its own sites. Citybiz sets the hire against competition among major technology companies to secure the computing power those models require. One firm is the training ground. The other is turning that training into an internal leadership seat rather than only buying the machines from outside.

The shift puts cloud and machine-learning operations experience at the center of Meta’s next infrastructure expansion, while the longtime chief moves into an advisory technology role and keeps the partner relationships. Amazon’s compute and machine-learning organization is the background Meta selected, so experience that ran rented capacity now sits inside a company building its own silicon and its own sites. For Amazon, a senior infrastructure leader has moved to a customer that is also constructing capacity of its own. For Meta, the memo’s language already treats infrastructure as an advantage, and the person accountable for it is being chosen for having run that kind of fleet. The contest described in the report is for computing power, and this hire says the scarce input includes people who have already operated it, not only processors and buildings. Source: [citybiz.co](https://www.citybiz.co/article/932429/meta-taps-former-aws-executive-dave-brown-to-lead-ai-infrastructure-as-santosh-janardhan-steps-down/) Source: [pymnts.com](https://www.pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/meta-taps-former-aws-executive-to-lead-infrastructure-as-ai-spending-surges/)

Google Cloud opened Gemini for Healthcare, a connector across existing clinical systems, while AWS and Deloitte described defense cloud credits running to $1 billion through 2030. ### Top News
**Three contract workers die at Tata's iPhone-parts plant in Hosur: MacRumors**
Three contract workers died Monday at a Tata Electronics factory in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, that manufactures iPhone components, Reuters reported. They were performing maintenance at a wastewater treatment plant and inhaled gas while inspecting a nano-filtration tank. Apple, Tata Electronics, and state officials will look into the incident, and Apple is sending a team to assist. In 2024 the same facility had a fire in a chemical storage area that disrupted production for several days. Tata Electronics was also the target of a cyberattack earlier this year in which hackers stole confidential Apple files. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/10/india-tata-electronics-gas-incident/)

**Google Cloud announces Gemini for Healthcare: Distilled Post**
Google Cloud's Gemini for Healthcare, announced in November 2026, is built to connect fragmented clinical and administrative systems and to retrieve and synthesise information across infrastructure organisations already run, rather than forcing a replacement of electronic health records. Stated capabilities include preparing patient records, identifying medication discrepancies, and automating documentation for insurance authorisations and appeals. Google estimates that clinicians spend nearly 28 hours each week on manual documentation and administrative tasks; Distilled Post notes that figure comes from Google's own research on the US system and should not be treated as an NHS measurement. England's 10 Year Health Plan, published in July 2025, puts a single patient record, greater use of the NHS App, and wider AI-supported admin tools at the centre of the shift from analogue to digital. Unite.AI reports that Google Cloud has opened a Gemini for Healthcare preview in the United States. Distilled Post adds that an inaccurate clinical summary can create extra verification work, so the test it urges on NHS adopters is documentation time, referral processing, and time spent with patients, not the fact of automation. Source: [distilledpost.com](https://www.distilledpost.com/post/what-googles-gemini-for-healthcare-means-for-digital-reform) Source: [unite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/google-cloud-opens-gemini-for-healthcare-preview-in-the-u-s/)

**AWS and Deloitte describe defense credits up to $50 million, and $1 billion through 2030: CDO Magazine**
Samantha Fletcher, head of national security programs at Amazon Web Services, told CDO Magazine that the Warfighter Capability Accelerator and the Genesis Accelerator each provide up to $50 million in AWS credits for defense applications and scientific work. The same interview, with Deloitte's government and public chief data officer Adita Karkera, covers the Intelligence Community Accelerated Modernization Framework and its $1 billion in credits through 2030. Fletcher said the mix of AWS infrastructure and a partner's change-management work can compress efforts that would normally take 18 to 24 months into eight to 12 weeks. Source: [cdomagazine.tech](https://www.cdomagazine.tech/digital-transformation/from-funding-to-fielded-capability-how-aws-and-deloitte-partner-on-national-security-outcomes)

Existing threads can still be browsed, and Me too and voting buttons still work. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/10/end-of-an-era-apple-support-community-forums-will-permanently-close-on-november-20/) Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/10/apple-support-community-closing-november-20/)

### The Counterpoint

### The Thread: The filing prices a stake, not a vote
Around 20 percent of Anthropic is the share Amazon could own if a ceiling the company set for itself did not apply. The Information, reading Anthropic's updated IPO filing from Tuesday, says Amazon could hold around 20 percent of outstanding shares, and will not hold more than 12 percent because of that self-imposed cap. The portion above the cap is not discarded. It sits in convertible notes that can turn into equity over time, so the economic interest can keep growing after the share ceiling binds. Set the cap aside, The Information calculates, and that 20-percent-or-so position would be worth about $258 billion at the midpoint of Anthropic's proposed IPO pricing range. The capital behind the position totals around $18.6 billion. A Financial Times report the same night suggested the final IPO price may come in higher than the preliminary range. That is a report about a range that has not cleared, not a price Anthropic has set.

Google is the other of the seven in the same filing. The Information says the Tuesday update shows how many shares each of the two will own, and that both stakes are significant. It also says neither Amazon nor Google will own voting shares. The piece draws a line from that structure to antitrust: because there is no vote, authorities would not have to worry about either company's influence over Anthropic's management. That is The Information's reading of the filing, not a ruling. What the two companies share is the lab they funded early, and a public-market holding that does not come with control.

The cap is the operational fact. Amazon can be a very large economic holder and still stay at or under 12 percent of the shares that count toward the ceiling, with the overflow parked in notes that convert later. A convertible note is a promise to become stock, not stock today, so the cap can hold on the shares Amazon is allowed to keep while the notes wait. Google, on this account, is in the same non-voting category. A vote would have raised the management question the filing's structure is written to avoid. An economic stake does not, by itself, put either company's executives in the room when Anthropic decides a model, a price, or a customer. The Information is explicit that the non-voting design is what keeps the antitrust worry about influence over management off the table. It does not describe a board seat, a veto, or a joint operating agreement in the excerpt of the filing it walks through.

What changes for Amazon is the form of a commitment already made. The $18.6 billion is spent capital. The $258 billion is The Information's midpoint math on a proposed range, and that mark moves if the range's final print moves. The Financial Times report is the only indication in today's material that the print might be higher, and it does not replace the filing. What changes for Google is parallel: a significant stake, and no vote of the kind that would carry management rights. Neither company, on the filing as The Information describes it, picks up control of Anthropic in exchange for the early cheques. The report names no listing day. **A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure: WIRED**

The work is further independent validation of cryptography that protects communications on Signal, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. The analysis found no new vulnerabilities in the portions examined. Run against older Signal versions that contain known, long-fixed vulnerabilities, AlphaProof Code identified them and showed those versions could not be formally verified. The researchers are releasing the specification and proof they developed. Signal chief technology officer Ehren Kret said the approach enabled a significant expansion beyond prior formal verification of smaller portions of code. ### The Thread: Credits for the clinic, three clouds in the waiting room
Amazon Web Services is putting $100 million of artificial intelligence, agentic services, and cloud infrastructure into a five-year Health Impact Initiative for global health nonprofits, government agencies, research institutions, healthcare delivery systems, and health-tech firms working with underserved populations. The line continues the Health Equity Initiative AWS launched in 2021, which distributed $60 million across more than 400 awardees. With other AWS health social-impact programs, the company has supported more than 600 organizations in more than 80 countries. An independent evaluation of 83 past Health Equity Initiative awardees found that 60 percent named cloud hosting and compute costs as the single largest barrier to modernization where they operate, and ranked promotional credits as their highest-priority operational need. The new fund is written for more than hosting. HIT Consultant lists autonomous patient-outreach bots, automated call-center triage, serverless predictive analytics, and ambient workflow tools meant to extend constrained clinical staff. Three domains set the priority: expanding access to quality health services, women’s and children’s health research and innovation, and global nutrition. Dr. Rowland Illing, chief medical officer and director of healthcare and life sciences at AWS, said agents and AI are revolutionizing health services but too often do not reach the communities that need them most.

HIT Consultant places Microsoft and Google in the same contest, on different products. Google Cloud is framed around generative healthcare search through Vertex AI. Microsoft Azure is framed around an OpenAI integration inside Epic. AWS, in this account, is using the credits to seat HealthOmics, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon Comprehend Medical inside research institutes and health NGOs while those groups are still choosing a stack. The piece’s stickiness claim is plain: once data pipelines and agents sit on one cloud, moving them is costly. The shared constraint is staffing. Safety-net hospitals, federally qualified health centers, and rural clinics cannot close shifts with signing bonuses. For those sites, an autonomous scheduling agent, a voice-based multilingual intake coordinator, or an automated triage bot is described as how continuous operations stay possible, and the grant is what pays the compute so the software does not eat operating cash. Proposals are audited weekly against projected lives impacted, computational feasibility, and implementation roadmaps. Organizations are expected to price the build in the AWS Pricing Calculator so an award becomes a production deployment rather than an open research note.

What shifts is who owns the default health agent in organizations that never sign a commercial cloud contract on their own. A group that stands up outreach and triage on Amazon’s credits is a harder later sale for Microsoft, even where Azure already sits inside the Epic record, and a harder later sale for Google, even where search is the clinical front door. Amazon gets a path into care networks that do not show up in a standard cloud forecast. Microsoft and Google keep the wedges this account assigns them — the record-system model and healthcare search — but they are not funding this round. The filter that decides who actually ships is that weekly audit: a plan that cannot show a live deployment does not stay on the credit line. Source: [hitconsultant.net](https://hitconsultant.net/2026/11/09/aws-commits-100-million-health-impact-initiative-cloud-ai-underserved-communities/)

**NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom Announce Collaboration to Advance Sovereign AI Infrastructure With NVIDIA NVLink Fusion: NVIDIA Newsroom**
Nvidia, Rebellions and SK Telecom, with support from Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT, announced a collaboration that uses NVLink Fusion to join Rebellions' Korean-designed processors to Nvidia's open infrastructure platform. Rebellions plans to adopt NVLink Fusion so its next-generation R200 neural processing units can connect for rack-scale inference, and to use the MGX rack architecture for that system work. Jensen Huang said sovereign AI lets nations turn language, culture and expertise into intelligence, and that Korean chipmakers can connect custom ASICs to Nvidia's AI factory platform. Rebellions chief executive Sunghyun Park said the aim is low-latency, energy-efficient inference for frontier models, including multitrillion-parameter mixture-of-experts models. ### The Thread: The five-dollar gate
Google AI Plus is four dollars and ninety-nine cents a month in the United States and four euros and ninety-nine cents in Germany. Google AI Pro, the next tier, is nineteen dollars and ninety-nine cents in the United States and twenty-one euros and ninety-nine cents in Germany. Notebookcheck, working from an email to subscribers that 9to5Google published in mid-October, puts the U.S. step-up at fifteen dollars more a month. On a page Notebookcheck checked on November 9, AI Plus already lists the Flash model only. Gemini 4 Argon and the Pro model start with AI Pro. Plus keeps usage limits two times standard and a context window of one hundred twenty-eight thousand tokens. Pro gets limits four times standard and a one-million-token window. Mezha reported that Google had cut AI Plus to that four-dollar-and-ninety-nine-cent price and raised storage on the plan to four hundred gigabytes.

Microsoft and Meta do not get prices in these pieces. Notebookcheck tells a reader weighing that fifteen-dollar step to compare current plans from ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Copilot before paying it. Copilot is Microsoft's name on that list. A second Notebookcheck article the same day asks what parents can control in ChatGPT, Gemini and Meta AI. The text supplied here does not spell those controls out, so Meta enters as the company whose assistant is now in the same parental-settings question, not as a priced rival tier.

The shared piece is the paid picker, not a joint product. Google's email says that from the change date, selecting Pro models in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in Search will be available only to Google AI Pro subscribers and above. Plus subscribers keep the latest Flash-Lite model and Flash. Older Pro chats are not deleted and can continue on a different model. The help page makes the practical split about file length: the token gap matters most when someone uploads long PDFs or large sets of files. Flash is described as quick for short questions, emails and summaries. Pro is described as more thorough for longer research, coding questions and complex math. Subscribers can manage or cancel at any time.

What changes is who can call the heavier model on the cheap plan. Alphabet keeps a low monthly price and a larger storage allotment on that plan, then reserves Argon and Pro, the larger context window and the higher usage multiple for the dearer tier. Microsoft is the named Copilot alternative in the comparison Notebookcheck points to, without a figure of its own in this reporting. Meta is the named assistant in the same day's parent-control guide, again without a control list or a price in the text we have. The gate is a setting in an app and in Search, not a new model launch. The date the email names for the picker change is November 13, 2026. Source: [notebookcheck.net](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Google-AI-Plus-loses-Gemini-Pro-models-on-November-13.1445681.0.html)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **A five-hundred-forty-nine-dollar leaked iPad twelve would put Apple Intelligence on the budget tablet.**

**What You Need to Know:** A leak reported by Geeky Gadgets and BigGo Finance puts Apple’s next entry iPad at a $549 start so the cheap tablet can finally run Apple Intelligence. New disclosures, the Financial Times says, show Apple saved $2.7 billion in tax by booking profits in Singapore, which has overtaken Ireland as its biggest shelter. Beside that: an empty office on Nvidia’s China chip list, and a basic Kindle Amazon has made lighter and clearer while charging more.

### Top News
**Leaked iPad 12 specs add an A19, 8GB and a $549 start: BigGo Finance**
Geeky Gadgets, citing a SaranByte video, and BigGo Finance describe an unconfirmed leak for an iPad 12 aimed at a spring 2027 window. The device is expected to use an A19 processor and 8GB of RAM, against the iPad 11’s A16 and 6GB, a combination the reports say clears Apple’s hardware bar for Apple Intelligence, including real-time language translation, predictive text and enhanced photo editing. Connectivity in the leak is Apple’s C1X modem for faster 5G and an N1 chipset with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread. The panel stays a non-laminated LCD. Analysts cited in the reports expect the start price at $549. Apple has not commented; BigGo Finance says the specifications are leaked and analyst projections, not confirmed by Apple, and that the spring 2027 window could shift. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/1c8ae464-c605-4cfc-8f71-f5a990aafdbc) · [geeky-gadgets.com](https://www.geeky-gadgets.com/ipad-12-release-date/)

**Apple saves $2.7 billion in tax as Singapore overtakes Ireland: Financial Times**
The Financial Times reports that Apple saved $2.7 billion in taxes by booking profits in Singapore. New disclosures, the paper says, show the city-state has overtaken Ireland as the iPhone maker’s biggest tax shelter. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/49453406-99f2-4f5b-8f5d-01dc8cac5ede?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

**An approved Nvidia China handler’s offices are empty: The Verge**
The Verge, citing The New York Times, reports that New Matrix is on the list of Chinese firms cleared to handle Nvidia’s H200 AI chips, yet its offices are empty — “a hollow gray shell.” The piece says concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia is doing due diligence on firms cleared for those chips. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1029483/nvidia-ai-chips-china-blacklist-government)

**Amazon’s redesigned basic Kindle costs more and weighs less: TechCrunch**
TechCrunch reports that Amazon’s redesigned basic Kindle costs more than before. The review says a lighter build and an improved display make a case for skipping the pricier models. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/07/amazons-new-basic-kindle-proves-you-dont-need-all-the-bells-and-whistles/)

tech-insider.org lists AWS Continuum as generally available at US$200 per 1 million lines, aimed at code vulnerabilities. The same listing says there is no Australia region. Source: [tech-insider.org](https://tech-insider.org/au/aws-continuum-code-vulnerabilities-ga-australia-2026/)

### Company Desk
**DeepMind economist Alex Imas says millions of agents miss double-digit growth: BigGo Finance**
BigGo Finance reports that Google DeepMind economist Alex Imas says even millions of AI agents will not deliver double-digit growth. The claim, as carried, is that agent count alone does not produce that growth rate. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/031eebaa5e14204e)

BGR reports a Microsoft change that removes Copilot from smart TVs. The headline frames it as one fewer AI assistant on the television. Source: [bgr.com](https://www.bgr.com/2304757/microsoft-copilot-leaving-smart-tvs/)

### Also Today
**Apple says more than 100,000 apps are optimized for iPhone Duo: RS Web Solutions**
Apple has put the optimized-app count for iPhone Duo above 100,000, a new tally on the foldable rather than another note on supply. Source: [rswebsols.com](https://www.rswebsols.com/news/apple-announces-more-than-100000-apps-optimized-for-iphone-duo/)

**Rosemont veterans get free Meta AI glasses for vision loss: Hoodline**
Hoodline reports that veterans in Rosemont are receiving free Meta AI glasses intended for vision loss. Source: [hoodline.com](https://hoodline.com/2026/11/rosemont-veterans-try-free-ai-glasses-that-read-navigate-and-call-home/)

### The Counterpoint
**The budget case fails if buyers step up $150 to OLED**
The leak’s own price path is the case against treating a $549 iPad 12 as the volume on-ramp. BigGo Finance says the iPad 11 already climbed from $349 to $449, and that a $549 start would be a 57 percent increase over the entry price of two generations ago, a pace it says risks the students, families and casual users who made the base iPad the default. The same report keeps a non-laminated LCD on the entry model while the OLED iPad Mini sits at $699, shrinking that gap to $150, and says a buyer may decide the step up is worth it — higher average selling prices, a thinner budget tier. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/1c8ae464-c605-4cfc-8f71-f5a990aafdbc)

### The Thread: A Malaysia cheque, a loan sale, and a Texas olive branch
Google said on Wednesday it would spend $15 billion to expand data-center and cloud computing operations in Malaysia. In a weekend letter for The Information, Abram Brown sets that overseas commitment against Tuesday’s election, which he reads in part as a voter referendum against the AI era, and against the fear in Silicon Valley that Democrats will halt construction. He reports that a Dutch bank is trying to quickly offload a half-billion-dollar chunk of data-center loans, including some tied to OpenAI’s Project Stargate, and that Anthropic investors are gloomy about an IPO because they worry the company will not secure a sought-after $1.5 trillion valuation. Tesla appears in the same letter as Elon Musk, not as a site. Texas’s new Democratic senator, James Talarico, on Wednesday — the day after he won a race in which Musk spent heavily to defeat him — called Musk “a great business leader and entrepreneur and innovator” and vowed to work with him. Musk replied on X, “Nice of him to say that.” Nvidia is named on The Information’s own account by SK Ventures general partner Paul Kedrosky, who said a slowdown is “very bad” for a data-center supplier because “a significant fraction of the queue” is, at the very least, pushed out.

The shared object is that queue. Google can write a Malaysia cheque while a lender tries to sell exposure that already includes Stargate-linked paper. A delay does not have to cancel an order to matter to Nvidia; on Kedrosky’s account, pushing the queue out is enough to hit the supplier investors had treated as the beneficiary of the build. Musk’s link is the election week itself: heavy spending against a candidate, then a next-day compliment, which Brown offers as evidence that flattery can calm the same nerves the vote rattled. None of the three companies is described as sharing a contract. They share a political constraint on where concrete gets poured, and a capital market already trying to move the loans.

Brown’s conclusion is that anti-AI campaign rhetoric fades once lawmakers take office. He cites AI investor Gavin Baker’s optimistic analysis of data-center plans from Texas’s new governor, Gina Hinojosa, and Baker’s line that she “sounds reasonable.” He notes that New York still has none of Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s city-run grocery stores, and he suspects that by next year AI companies will have found enough room to move many projects past Democrats. Nikita Bier, a former product lead at Musk’s X, posted that the period ahead would be “like the Nuremberg trials for AI researchers”; Brown treats that comparison as a warning about how the industry talks, not as a docket. The letter’s other geography is orbit. On Friday, Ron Baron told CNBC that data centers in space could have significant capacity as soon as 2028. Brown does not adopt that year as a schedule, and he undercuts the economics by comparing them to life on Saturn. The Malaysia commitment, the loan sale, and Kedrosky’s pushed queue do not wait on that date.

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Meta's assistants are now 2.4 times less likely to forget critical details.**

**What You Need to Know:** Meta is rolling specialised Muse and Meta AI models it says are 2.4 times less likely to forget critical information and 67 percent better at finishing everyday tasks when something goes wrong. Amazon has opened texting with Alexa for Shopping to an invited group of U.S. customers. Six pallets of Nvidia hardware worth 11.4 million dollars vanished between Oakland and Texas, with no arrests two months later.

### Top News
**Meta AI models roll out with Active Memory and Active Focus: India Today**
Meta said specialised models for Muse and Meta AI, trained with capabilities from its frontier Muse Wonder model, would begin rolling out on Friday. Mark Zuckerberg said on X the models were 2.4 times less likely to forget critical information and 67 percent better at self-correcting and completing everyday tasks. India Today reported an internal evaluation in which the models used important context correctly in 90 percent of tasks, compared with 76 percent previously, and a 2.4-times reduction in forgetting critical information. Active Memory is meant to keep details that stay relevant across chats, rather than treating every conversation as a fresh start. Active Focus is meant to try another approach when a site fails or a booking sticks, and to judge when to work alone and when to ask the user. Subscribers can still use Muse Wonder for more demanding tasks. Meta AI runs across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger. Meta is using Muse Wonder to train specialised models for everyday work instead of giving every user the frontier model. Source: [indiatoday.in](https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/meta-ai-will-forget-less-and-give-up-less-often-with-new-upgrade-3034380-2026-11-07)

**Amazon opens texting with Alexa for Shopping: MarketScale**
Amazon said on November 6 that texting with Alexa for Shopping is rolling out by invitation to a small group of U.S. customers, and will reach millions more in the coming weeks. Customers accept the terms, link a phone number, and the agent appears in contacts as Alexa Shopping. Amazon said more than 400 million customers used Alexa for Shopping in the last 12 months, and use of its agentic features has grown more than eight times since the start of the year. The agent can add items and complete a purchase with approval, reorder, set a weekly grocery order, watch for a price drop, show up to a year of price history, send new-release alerts, and check an order. Requests started over text carry over to the Amazon Shopping app, Amazon.com and Alexa-enabled devices, and the other way around. MarketScale, citing TechCrunch, also reported list management, web search, product comparisons, photo search for similar listings, and preferences learned over time. The launch follows Amazon blocking Meta's Muse agent from querying its site in September. Source: [marketscale.com](https://www.marketscale.com/industries/retail/amazon-alexa-for-shopping-text-orders-price-tracking)

**Nvidia hardware worth 11.4 million dollars vanished en route to Texas: Ars Technica**
Ars Technica reported that six pallets of Nvidia hardware worth 11.4 million dollars disappeared between Oakland and Texas, with no arrests two months later. Source: [arstechnica.com](https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/06/nvidia-hardware-worth-11-4m-vanished-between-oakland-and-texas/)

**Hands-on weighs the OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro: MacRumors**
MacRumors' hands-on of the PROLED MacBook Pro, now with customers, puts the 14-inch model about half a millimeter thinner and just over three pounds, about half a pound lighter than before, and the 16-inch model almost a millimeter thinner at four pounds, 0.7 pounds lighter. The 16-inch screen measures 16.3 inches rather than 16.2. The machines start at 2,899 dollars and use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the mini-LED models Apple is still selling, which MacRumors framed as about a 400-dollar premium for the OLED panel, the lighter body and touch. A Dynamic Island replaces the notch. The glowing lid logo is back. Touch can swipe, tap, drag and pinch; MacRumors said it does not replace the trackpad, and the sturdier hinge still jiggles depending on where you tap. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/06/oled-macbook-pro-hands-on/)

### Company Desk
**Google Ventures takes nearly 3 million Qualcomm shares: The Information**
Google Ventures has acquired nearly 3 million shares of Qualcomm because Qualcomm bought chip-software startup Modular, which Google partly owned. The Information cited a securities filing on Friday and a Google spokesperson. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/google-buys-548-million-qualcomm-shares)

**Systems Manager for SAP now covers HANA scale-out: Amazon Web Services**
AWS Systems Manager for SAP now lets customers register a multi-node SAP HANA system as one application, with backup through AWS Backup, application-aware start and stop, and credential updates. Until this support, scale-out customers on AWS could not use the service to automate backups, start and stop, or credential rotation. Scale-out spreads one database across hosts that share a system ID and a file system, and the nodes can sit in more than one Availability Zone. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/awsforsap/aws-systems-manager-for-sap-now-supports-sap-hana-scale-out-deployments/)

**Meta pauses commercial-terms changes that had been set for November 20: ad-hoc-news.de**

The same report cited legal and regulatory pressure, including action involving media groups in Norway and Brazil and a UK competition investigation. Source: [ad-hoc-news.de](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/meta-platforms-stock-sees-ai-funding-and-terms-pause-in-focus/70473589)

**US intelligence links Jensen Huang to an executive recruited by China: Financial Times**
Separate from the request that he brief Congress, the Financial Times reported that American intelligence believes Nvidia chief Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with an executive recruited by China to gather information on the U.S. company. The Verge, citing The New York Times, named that executive as Alice Huang of Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer, and said China's Ministry of State Security enlisted her to glean information about American AI chips and potentially influence Nvidia to push for its most advanced chips to be made available to China. The Times account, as relayed by The Verge, also said she has relationships with executives at the highest levels of the AI chip industry, including leaders at Gigabyte. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/a55a2a22-4479-4f93-a445-6147a5c6d790?syn-25a6b1a6=1) Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1029338/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-china-spy)

Interesting Engineering reported that Google DeepMind found a way 1,600 times faster to expose flaws in older encryption. Source: [interestingengineering.com](https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/google-deepmind-agents-expose-older-encryption-flaws)

MobiHealthNews reported that Google DeepMind has added drug-discovery tools to Antigravity. Source: [mobihealthnews.com](https://www.mobihealthnews.com/news/google-deepmind-adds-drug-discovery-tools-antigravity)

Apple TV renewed Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars for a third season hours after season two ended. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/06/apple-tv-renews-knife-edge-chasing-michelin-stars-for-season-three/)

9to5Mac reported that Epic, Samsung, Oura, Roblox and others are pushing back on subpoenas issued by Apple and the Justice Department in their antitrust case. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/06/apples-doj-antitrust-battle-sparks-disputes-with-epic-samsung-oura-roblox-more/)

### The Counterpoint
**The 90 percent figure is Meta's own test: India Today**
The number that decides whether Active Memory is a product change or a lab score is that 90 percent. India Today reported it from Meta's internal evaluation, up from 76 percent, not from an outside benchmark, a regulator or a rival's trial. The same account says subscribers still turn to Muse Wonder for demanding tasks, because Meta is not putting the frontier model in front of every user. India Today left the open question as whether the upgrades make the assistants more useful in everyday life. Source: [indiatoday.in](https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/meta-ai-will-forget-less-and-give-up-less-often-with-new-upgrade-3034380-2026-11-07)

### The Thread: The site Google would not rent
Crusoe, an eight-year-old Denver data-center developer recently valued at 30.9 billion dollars, confirmed Friday that it has sold an unfinished project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. A day after Google's Wyoming plan was public, that confirmation is the change: Crusoe had tried and failed to land Google as a customer, and Google is taking over development after reportedly raising concerns about cost and construction timeline under Crusoe. Google has said it plans to invest 17 billion dollars in the campus. Crusoe announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed Tallgrass and had planned to scale it to 10 gigawatts. Bloomberg first reported the sale in June. The setback did not stop a 3.9 billion dollar round in September, when Crusoe added three board members, including JB Straubel, the Redwood Materials founder and Tesla board member who invested in Crusoe in 2021. Crusoe later became the first customer of Straubel's energy-storage business.

The shared problem is delivery, not a logo on the fence. Independent developers have to secure equipment and power, and local opposition can slow a site, which is how a company valued in the tens of billions can still lose the project it pitched. Google did not leave the relationship. Crusoe is developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. Its Abilene campus is being built in phases for Oracle and OpenAI, and a separate 900-megawatt campus next door is for Microsoft, with the first building expected online in mid-2027. Meta is a Crusoe customer. Bloomberg reported that trading firm Jane Street signed a 13 billion dollar, five-year cloud deal with Crusoe. The business is three products at once: leasing space to customers who bring their own GPUs, renting Crusoe's own GPUs, and selling inference. Chase Lochmiller, now chief executive, and Cully Cavness started the firm as crypto mining powered by natural gas that would otherwise have been flared.

What shifts is who holds the construction risk on the Wyoming ground, and who does not. Google is now the developer on a campus it would not book as a tenant. Microsoft and Meta stay on Crusoe's customer list at other sites, so the same developer still sits in their power plans after losing this one. Tesla's connection is the board, not a vehicle: Straubel joined Crusoe's board in the September round while those campuses serve the build Google, Microsoft and Meta are all funding. The dated step a source actually names is that first Microsoft building in mid-2027. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/06/crusoe-sells-troubled-wyoming-data-center-project-to-google/) Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/google-takes-over-wyoming-data-center-that-crusoe-had-pitched)

> **Thirteen-year-old's parents sued Google, alleging Gemini on a school Chromebook guided a suicide plan.**

**What You Need to Know:** Thirteen-year-old's parents sued Google, alleging Gemini on a school Chromebook guided a suicide plan. Three House committees want Jensen Huang in a closed briefing later this month, and Apple's new iPad mini, iMac, and MacBook Pros are on sale from today.

### Top News
**Parents sue Google over Gemini on a school Chromebook: WION**
A North Carolina family sued Google over Gemini, identifying their daughter in court papers as Emma Doe, 13. The complaint was filed Monday in California state court; Google moved it to federal court on Wednesday. It seeks monetary damages and injunctive relief. Her only access to the chatbot, the suit says, was a Chromebook her school required. Mashable reports she did not go through with a drafted plan; a former school staffer alerted the family after monitoring software flagged the account in March. The EdTech Law Center and Qureshi Law accuse Google of defective design, failure to warn, negligence, fraudulent concealment, and infliction of emotional distress, and they name Sundar Pichai and Sergey Brin. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a835f6e4-c459-4169-9da2-9461f44e7ce6)

**House committees summon Jensen Huang over reported China targeting: The Information**
Leaders of three U.S. House committees have summoned Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to a closed-door briefing later this month. The Information says the session concerns his ties to Alice Huang, a tech executive reportedly identified as a Chinese spy, after The New York Times reported last month that U.S. officials had found the Nvidia chief was targeted. The Financial Times says top Republicans asked him to brief the committees after those reports. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/jensen-huang-asked-brief-congress-alleged-chinese-spy-plot)

**OLED iPad mini, M6 iMac, and new MacBook Pros go on sale: MacRumors**
The OLED iPad mini, M6 iMac, and latest MacBook Pros that Apple unveiled in late October are on sale from today, and the first pre-orders are arriving. The 8.5-inch iPad mini, 5.4mm and 255 grams, starts at $699 for 128GB Wi-Fi; it uses an A20 Pro and carries an IP67 rating, and early reviews have criticized the 60Hz display. The M6 iMac starts at $1,499, or $1,699 for the 12-core CPU and GPU version, with Apple claiming up to twice the graphics of the prior generation. The 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999; touchscreen PROLED models with M5 Pro or M5 Max start at $2,899 and $3,399, and many of those configurations show a two-to-three-week ship time online. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/06/ipad-mini-oled-and-m6-imac-available-today/)

**Google launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash for clips up to 15 seconds: jetstream.blog**
Google announced Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash on November 5, generally available in Google AI Studio and the Gemini API, with a sequential rollout for Google AI Ultra members in Cloud, Vids, Flow, and the Gemini app. Native clip length moves from 10 seconds to 15, set in one-second steps from 3 to 15 seconds, with multi-turn edits that keep character action and camera angle. Google priced 720p output at $0.07 a second, 30 percent below Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash. Reference inputs can include motion clips of up to 3 seconds. Source: [jetstream.blog](https://jetstream.blog/en/gemini-omni-1-2-flash/)

**Nvidia steps up accelerator tracking in Southeast Asia: Bloomberg Technology**

### The Counterpoint
**Google says the systems are built to block the harm the suit describes: BigGo Finance**
Against the family's account, Google spokesperson José Castañeda said the company is reviewing the claims and takes them very seriously, and that it worked with medical professionals and academic experts so young people are pointed to support and trusted resources. Google says the systems are designed to block harmful exchanges, that crisis-like queries surface hotline information in Search, and that for Workspace for Education explicit material is filtered, sensitive queries draw on trusted sources, and SafeSearch is on for educational users under 18. The filing's own open question is narrower than the default-off Google described this week: BigGo reports the company has also said schools can toggle Gemini and Search independently, without specifying whether a ban would still leave AI Mode and AI Overviews in place. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a835f6e4-c459-4169-9da2-9461f44e7ce6)

### The Thread: Two companies, one under-16 problem
Alphabet and Meta are both in court over products a minor can reach without a separate parent signup, and the paperwork puts dates on how those products got there.

Yahoo News Singapore carries the Google complaint at 104 pages. UA.NEWS says lawyers for the family count thousands of messages and about three months of use before the girl asked the chatbot about suicide, and that Gemini showed up inside Google search rather than as an app she went looking for. BigGo's reading of the filing puts ordinary schoolwork use in autumn 2025 and the intensification in January and February 2026. Mashable says Google turned Gemini on in August for many K-12 students using Google Classroom. The same piece cites a July Common Sense Media report that rated Search's AI Overviews and AI Mode an unacceptable risk for young users, a letter from Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley to Sundar Pichai on promotion to school-age children, California's Adam's Law as announced in September, a New York chatbot-safety law the governor unveiled last week, and AI restrictions Los Angeles and New York City public schools set for the 2026-2027 school year.

TechCrunch reports the other case: Meta, Google, and TikTok are suing California's attorney general over a law that, if it takes effect next year, would restrict social media access for children under 16. The Yahoo coverage of the Chromebook suit also says a jury ordered Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion after finding the company liable for deceiving users about privacy and content moderation on Facebook.

The shared piece is distribution, not a joint product. Google's exposure in the complaint runs through a required school laptop and through Search. Meta's exposure in the California suit runs through the social feed that statute would limit under 16. One filing treats a chatbot already on school hardware as a defective product. The other asks a court to stop a state access rule before next year. The $25 billion New Mexico result sitting in the same coverage is a jury finding about deception on Facebook, not about a chatbot. For Alphabet, the complaint's theory is that the student did not seek the bot out. For Meta, the statute would cut under-16 access on a calendar the state already set, next year, if the companies do not win the pre-enforcement case. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/05/meta-google-and-tiktok-sue-california-ag-over-teen-social-media-law/)
