# MAG 7 Daily
> **Hon Hai's October sales rose 46 percent on resilient Nvidia server demand.**

**What You Need to Know:** Hon Hai's October sales rose 46 percent on resilient Nvidia server demand. Amazon turned Hive-to-Iceberg migration into a managed S3 Tables job, and Apple turned on cancellation-flow offers for App Store subscriptions. Delhi Police have an FIR over alleged child sexual abuse material on Meta's Facebook and Instagram.

### Top News
**Nvidia Partner Hon Hai’s Sales Rise 46% Thanks to AI Demand: Bloomberg Technology**
Hon Hai Precision Industry reported a 46 percent jump in October sales. Bloomberg tied that jump to resilient demand for the Nvidia servers at the center of the global AI infrastructure build-out. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-05/nvidia-partner-hon-hai-s-sales-rise-46-thanks-to-ai-demand)

**Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg: Amazon Web Services**
Amazon S3 Tables now run a managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg for Parquet tables in Amazon S3 that are registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. AWS says the path needs no pipelines to build and no compute to provision, and that production workloads keep running. Before any copy, S3 Tables identify every source object in scope and generate a compatibility report, then handle validation, compatibility checks, type conversions, file recompression, and compaction. Syncs can run as often as needed without stopping writes to the source, except for a few minutes at cutover. The destination stays read-only during migration and becomes read-write once migration is completed. Customers pay only for data copied, with no charge for the Hive-to-Iceberg conversion, and source objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering stay in their current access tier. It is available in US East (Northern Virginia and Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Singapore, Sydney, and Tokyo), and Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, and Stockholm), for Glue-registered Parquet Hive tables in the same account and Region. Query paths named in the post include Amazon Athena and Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/amazon-s3-tables-now-offer-managed-migration-of-apache-hive-tables-to-apache-iceberg/)

**Apple now lets developers offer discounts when users move to cancel subscriptions: 9to5Mac**
Apple has turned on Retention Messaging, a subscription tool it announced at WWDC earlier this year. Messages appear in the cancellation flow and can include text, images, or a special offer, configured in App Store Connect with subscriber eligibility and a wait time between messages. A Retention Messaging API, access by request, lets a developer pick which message a subscriber sees from that subscriber's details. Developers can create up to 10 retention messages per app, each tied to one or more subscriptions. This is not the 2024 Win-Back Offers, which discounted former subscribers after a cancel or expiry. These messages reach people before the cancellation is finished. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/04/apple-now-lets-developers-offer-discounts-when-users-move-to-cancel-subscriptions/)

**Delhi Police registers FIR over alleged circulation of child sexual abuse material on Meta platforms: The Hindu**
Delhi Police's Special Cell registered an FIR on October 8 over suspected child sexual abuse material on Meta platforms, including Facebook and Instagram. The Hindu reported the FIR under Sections 67 and 67B of the Information Technology Act, 2000, after a complaint flagged approximately 10 links. Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations Additional CP Sanjay Bhatia said police opened an investigation to verify the allegations. NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo said on X that Delhi Police registered the FIR on the commission's directions. Anadolu Ajansı and NDTV also reported the investigation. Source: [thehindu.com](https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/delhi-police-registers-fir-over-alleged-circulation-of-child-sexual-abuse-material-on-meta-platforms/article71668968.ece)

**Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones: Ars Technica**
Ars Technica reported that hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones. Researchers say the group may have been Kremlin-sponsored and was searching for diplomatic targets. Source: [arstechnica.com](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11/hackers-exploited-ios-and-android-flaws-to-infect-phones/)

### Company Desk
**Google brings Gemini to AT&T home security with smarter alerts and 24/7 recording: Digital Trends**
Google is bringing Gemini to AT&T home security. Digital Trends reported smarter alerts and 24/7 recording on AT&T's connected-life system. Source: [digitaltrends.com](https://www.digitaltrends.com/home/google-adds-gemini-to-att-connected-life-home-security/)

The Financial Times reported that Big Tech's $600 million midterm campaign fell flat. Elon Musk was rebuked, the paper said, as anger at AI and Silicon Valley fueled support for Democrats. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/3e65138f-068f-465f-a1ae-a9c61ea1afc4?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

### Also Today

Dataconomy reported that Google is allowing Gmail and Photos data to be used for personalised ads in Search and Gemini. Source: [dataconomy.com](https://dataconomy.com/2026/11/05/google-allows-gmail-and-photos-data-for-personalised-ads/)

AWS is bringing OpenAI's Daybreak Red to GovCloud for cybersecurity work, TokenPost reported. Source: [tokenpost.com](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/technology/49202)

India Today reported that Mark Zuckerberg is done with fruit names and that Meta's AI models will get more serious names. Source: [indiatoday.in](https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/mark-zuckerberg-done-with-fruits-meta-ai-models-to-get-more-serious-names-3032724-2026-11-05)

PPC Land reported that Microsoft Clarity is putting Shopify and WooCommerce products into Copilot and Bing. Source: [ppc.land](https://ppc.land/microsoft-clarity-puts-shopify-and-woocommerce-products-in-copilot-and-bing/)

CRN reported that Microsoft has again delayed making usage-based billing the default for Copilot, citing partner feedback. Source: [crn.com](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2026/microsoft-delays-default-copilot-usage-based-billing-again-after-partner-feedback)

A local family is fighting Entergy in court over land for power running to a Meta AI data center, the Ouachita Citizen reported. Source: [hannapub.com](https://www.hannapub.com/ouachitacitizen/news/local_state_headlines/local-family-fights-entergy-in-court-lawsuit-over-land-running-power-to-meta-ai-data/article_5a7b0881-0e5f-4002-b6a0-a910b363e5c6.html)

### The Counterpoint
**The sales jump is not a return: The Verge**
Hon Hai's October print is demand for Nvidia servers, not evidence that the buyers' build is paying off. After four of the biggest competitors in the AI race held quarterly earnings calls late last month, The Verge's reading was that Big Tech is not done spending record amounts on the data-center buildout, and that the buildout is not any closer to the returns it promised. The number that decides the Hon Hai story is still that missing return, not the 46 percent at the assembler. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1027344/amazon-microsoft-alphabet-google-meta-data-centers-earnings-q3)

### The Thread: Debt taken, a Texas option refused
Meta's first euro bonds drew €53 billion in investor orders, TokenPost reported, record demand for that debut euro sale. Bloomberg, on the first day of trading, said the freshly minted euro bonds were being quoted above face value after a sale that drew record investor orders for a corporate bond in Europe. Yesterday the sale was the news. Today the paper is already above par, and the order book has a published size.

Microsoft made the opposite capital call. The Financial Times reported that Microsoft rejected a multibillion-dollar AI deal with the UK start-up Nscale, turning down an option to more than double a Texas data-centre contract. The paper called it a fresh blow ahead of the start-up's IPO. One of the seven is raising a new currency of debt into the build. Another is leaving a doubling option on the table in Texas rather than taking the extra hall.

Amazon and Meta show up again as the customers a phone-chip company wants next. On Qualcomm's fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call, The Verge reported, the company laid out a push into AI data centers through partnerships with companies including Amazon and Meta. The same piece said smartphone sales were tanking by around 20 percent compared with 2025. The data-center pitch is the replacement story for a phone market that shrank by about a fifth in a year.

The chip-shipment tally points the same way, and it pulls Apple in. Counterpoint Research, as reported by 9to5Mac, found Apple and Samsung were the only major smartphone-chip vendors to gain share in the third quarter of 2026, while global shipments declined 21 percent year over year. Share gained inside a falling total is not a larger phone market. It is a reshuffle while Qualcomm talks up halls instead of handsets.

What is shared is the bill for AI sites and the slump in the phone business that used to fund these suppliers. Meta is paying for the build with euro debt that buyers bid to a record and then marked above par on day one. Microsoft is choosing which contracted expansion not to take, and that choice hits Nscale before an IPO rather than adding a doubled Texas site to Microsoft's own book. Amazon and Meta are named partners for a chip vendor whose phone sales are down hard against last year. Apple's gain is mix: more of a smaller shipment pool, not a phone cycle that rescues the old line.

What changes, without treating the assembler print as the payoff, is who holds the next constraint. Meta has a euro curve it did not have. Microsoft's refusal means the extra Texas capacity in that option is not Microsoft's to switch on. Amazon and Meta become the design-in targets for a vendor exiting a weak phone year. Apple can take vendor share and still sit in a market whose units fell. None of these filings dates the quarter when the data-center spend The Verge called unrewarded starts to throw off the returns the earnings calls promised. Source: [tokenpost.com](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/business/48986) Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-05/meta-s-euro-bonds-jump-on-first-day-of-trading-after-record-sale) Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/668e6ef8-88a1-4bef-8664-8f495baf09f8?syn-25a6b1a6=1) Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1026867/qualcomm-earnings-data-centers) Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/04/report-apple-and-samsung-outperform-rivals-as-smartphone-chip-shipments-tumble-21/)

### On the Calendar
US buyers who received an iPhone Duo on the October 23 launch day have until November 6 to return it under Apple's 14-day policy, MacRumors reported. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/05/iphone-duo-launch-day-nov-6-last-chance-return/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Google will switch off Search for students aged five to eighteen unless schools opt in.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google will switch off Search, with Gemini, for students aged five to eighteen unless a school administrator opts in. Apple put GitHub Copilot inside the Xcode 27.3 beta and testers got the iOS 27.3 build, including a China Apple Intelligence beta. A funding scrap for AI capacity runs through a Malaysian build, a first euro bond, and a thin Nvidia allocation to China.

### Top News
**Google will turn student Search and Gemini off unless schools opt in: The SOFX Report**
Starting next year, Google will leave Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search off for student accounts aged five to eighteen unless an administrator turns a service on. Chris Phillips, vice president of education, told The New York Times that Search and AI are deeply integrated, and that a school which bans AI will not have access to Search. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Google is trying to use monopoly power to force AI into public schools. Former Federal Trade Commission chair Lina Khan said Google is using its search monopoly to coerce schools into adopting AI, and that it will punish those who do not fall in line. The Decoder put the Search consequence in 2027. Google said schools should get more information on the change in the coming months. Source: [sofx.com](https://www.sofx.com/google-to-block-search-access-for-schools-that-disable-ai-features/) · [cybernews.com](https://cybernews.com/tech/google-search-ai-schools/) · [the-decoder.com](https://the-decoder.com/schools-that-turn-off-googles-ai-will-lose-search-too-starting-in-2027/) · [sfist.com](https://sfist.com/2026/11/03/google-playing-hardball-with-schools-says-if-they-disable-ai-tools-they-cant-use-search/)

**Xcode 27.3 beta adds GitHub Copilot to Apple’s coding assistant: 9to5Mac**
Apple released Xcode 27.3 beta 1 with GitHub Copilot added to the coding assistant built into Xcode. Dataconomy reported the same beta addition. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/03/xcode-27-3-adds-github-copilot-to-its-built-in-coding-assistant/) · [dataconomy.com](https://dataconomy.com/2026/11/04/apple-adds-github-copilot-to-xcode-273-beta/)

**Jailbreak demo holds through Lockdown Mode and an update: MacRumors**
Hacker team Calif showed a jailbroken iPhone 18 Pro with Lockdown Mode on, then installed iOS 27.2, and the jailbreak was still in place. The video shows a malicious PDF sent by AirDrop and accepted by the user. Apple told TechCrunch earlier this year it was not aware of any successful mercenary spyware attack on an iPhone in Lockdown Mode. Calif said it is disclosing the vulnerabilities to Apple and does not plan to release a jailbreak tool for end users. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/03/iphone-jailbreak-lockdown-mode/)

**Thai opposition leaders demand a spyware answer after Apple alerts: Bloomberg Technology**
Two Thai opposition leaders want the government to disclose whether state agencies targeted political leaders with spyware, after Apple software flagged attempted attacks on their phones. The demand comes ahead of a December no-confidence debate. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-04/thai-spyware-alerts-on-opposition-leaders-phones-prompt-demands-for-probe)

### Company Desk
**Washington notice lists 95 Amazon Stores cuts, not a new round: GeekWire**
A notice made public Tuesday lists about 95 Amazon job cuts in Washington state, and a spokesperson told GeekWire they are part of previously reported Stores layoffs, not a new round. The filing names software engineers, product managers, and program managers, mostly in Seattle, with others in Bellevue, Redmond, Sumner, Pasco, or remote. Reuters had reported fewer than 1,000 corporate cuts, mainly in Stores, affecting the United States, India, and the United Kingdom. Amazon eliminated about 14,000 corporate roles globally in October 2025, including 2,303 in Washington, then a January round that included 2,198 Washington employees. Spokesperson Brad Glasser said the company adjusted parts of Stores so the structure would better match its priorities. Separately, Amazon announced roughly 300,000 seasonal openings in U.S. operations, with health coverage from January 1, 2027, for seasonal employees working at least 30 hours a week, plans starting at $5 a week with $5 copays, after a September announcement of more than $1.5 billion in additional pay for U.S. operations employees. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/filing-amazons-previously-announced-layoffs-include-95-jobs-in-washington-state/) · [mynorthwest.com](https://mynorthwest.com/local/amazon-layoffs-washington-95/4294326)

**iOS 27.3 beta opens, with Qwen in the China Apple Intelligence set: MacRumors**
After Apple had already set the iOS 27.3 beta window, testers now have the build: Apple Intelligence features are in the China set, and Siri AI is not. TechNode reported the China developer beta integrates Qwen; Free Malaysia Today described the China arrival as coming after a two-year delay. The same beta adds a developer preview so any app can bring actions into Siri AI through App Intents, and it expands Siri AI to Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/guide/ios-27-3-beta-features/) · [technode.com](https://technode.com/2026/11/04/apple-intelligence-enters-developer-beta-in-china-with-qwen-integration/) · [freemalaysiatoday.com](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/business/2026/11/04/apple-ai-tools-come-to-china-after-2-year-delay)

**Musk and Zuckerberg structures aimed at investor suits: Financial Times Technology**
The Financial Times reported that a SpaceX-Tesla merger and Meta’s new share class are expected to fend off legal challenges after shareholder rights were diminished in Delaware and Texas. The piece frames both moves as the latest in decade-long efforts by Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg to repel investor lawsuits. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/e8d40d03-4d86-46ca-aab5-68f7ea69f364?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

### Also Today
**GovTech teams with Google DeepMind on on-device scam detection: Computer Weekly**
Singapore’s GovTech is working with Google DeepMind to use on-device AI to detect scams. Source: [computerweekly.com](https://www.computerweekly.com/news/366653612/GovTech-teams-up-with-Google-DeepMind-to-use-on-device-AI-to-detect-scams)

**Worldwide Express unfreezes $10 million with AWS AI agents: PYMNTS.com**
PYMNTS reported that Worldwide Express unfroze $10 million using AWS AI agents. Source: [pymnts.com](https://www.pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/worldwide-express-unfreezes-10-million-with-aws-ai-agents/)

### The Counterpoint
**Google says schools can switch Search on without taking every AI service: The SOFX Report**
Against the reading that a school which refuses AI loses Search, Google’s news account said the day’s changes give schools more choice, not less: Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search start off, and administrators can turn on one, two, or all three individually. The same post said AI Mode and AI Overviews in school Search will offer step-by-step guided learning so students do not get quick answers to schoolwork. That clarification is the fact that decides whether Phillips’s “deeply integrated” line still means Search cannot be separated from Gemini. Source: [sofx.com](https://www.sofx.com/google-to-block-search-access-for-schools-that-disable-ai-features/)

### The Thread: Cheques, sites, and a chip book that will not fill
Alphabet’s Google plans to spend $15 billion to expand data-center and cloud operations in Malaysia, Bloomberg reported, with the AI boom cited as the demand pulling that infrastructure. The same country, the same day, got a different Amazon move: BusinessToday said AWS launched Semarak AI Malaysia, a program with three pillars to drive AI adoption. One figure is a construction budget. The other is an adoption program, and the launch line does not attach a dollar total to those three pillars.

Meta is raising money rather than breaking ground in that story. Bloomberg said Meta has started its first euro-denominated bond sale and is set to pay generous yields, after a $15 billion dollar deal. The wire put that debut inside a race in which the biggest technology companies are financing trillions of dollars of investment in artificial intelligence. The euro sale does not add a Malaysian hall. It adds a second currency after the dollar raise, and it prices the funding at a yield Bloomberg called generous.

Nvidia’s bind is production. Yesterday the company told cloud clients to take on less China business. Today Bloomberg reported that Chinese AI developers expect to receive 1 percent of the $70 billion in advanced RTX chips they have ordered over the next several months, because Nvidia is struggling to lift output against soaring demand. AMD, which the same wire called a key challenger to Nvidia in AI chips, forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $17 billion, plus or minus 3 percent. Bloomberg read that outlook as fresh evidence that data-center processor demand is still strong. The AMD figure is a rival’s sales line, not a count of Nvidia boxes landing in China.

On the U.S. side of the land rush, MyNorthwest identified AWS as the buyer behind a $264 million data-center land deal in West Richland, Washington. That is a site purchase. It is not a switched-on cluster, and it is not the Malaysian program.

The shared constraint is the AI capacity race: power and buildings on one side, chips and the debt that pays for both on the other. Google is committing owned cloud capacity in Malaysia. Amazon is buying land in Washington and, separately, wrapping an adoption push around Malaysia. Meta is testing whether euro investors will fund the same build after the dollar deal. Nvidia cannot turn the China slice of that RTX order book into shipments at anything like the order size, even as a challenger’s quarterly outlook says buyers who can get processors are still spending.

What changes is the queue, not a single campus opening. Malaysian capacity becomes a Google spend. Euro bond buyers become a new price on Meta’s AI funding. Chinese developers holding RTX orders are the customers for whom almost the whole book does not convert on this run. Amazon’s West Richland outlay secures dirt, not racks. No source today dates a ribbon-cutting on either site. The clock a wire actually set is the delivery window on those fractional Nvidia shipments. # MAG 7 Daily
> **Nvidia told cloud clients a majority of their customers must be non-Chinese.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia told cloud clients a majority of their customers must be non-Chinese, a client-mix rule that would narrow one route China's AI developers use to reach advanced computing. Apple guided holiday-quarter revenue growth of 7% to 10%, above the 6% estimate in a Financial Times report, and a gross margin of 45% to 46%, below that report's 47% estimate, with John Ternus calling memory costs unprecedented. An adviser to Europe's highest court said Gemini's reuse of press articles may infringe publisher rights in some cases, while training itself stays inside the text-and-data-mining exception.

### Top News
**Nvidia tells cloud clients a majority of customers must be non-Chinese: Financial Times**
The Financial Times reported that Nvidia told cloud computing providers a majority of their clients must be non-Chinese. The Information, citing three people familiar with the matter, said Nvidia recently told some cloud customers to reduce exposure to Chinese companies, in part narrowing a key route for China's AI developers to advanced computing power. Bloomberg reported the same Financial Times account, citing unidentified people, as an instruction to scale back that exposure. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/1902df70-1380-4588-bad5-171352b575f2?syn-25a6b1a6=1) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/nvidia-tells-cloud-clients-take-less-china-business) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-03/nvidia-tells-data-center-clients-to-trim-china-business-ft-says)

**Apple guides holiday growth of 7% to 10% as memory costs cut the margin: MacRumors**
On his first earnings call as chief executive, John Ternus, with chief financial officer Kevan Parekh and chief operating officer Sabih Khan, guided December-quarter revenue growth of 7% to 10%, above the 6% estimate carried in the Financial Times report, and a gross margin of 45% to 46%, below that report's 47% estimate. The Information reported September-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% from a year earlier, and called it the year's slowest sales growth; MacRumors put September gross margin at 47.9%. Ternus said memory pricing is "unprecedented," that memory purchase prices keep rising beyond the December quarter, and that the holiday margin also takes Siri AI costs. Inventory more than doubled year over year to $14.5 billion, and Ternus said manufacturing purchase obligations rose $33 billion from June to the September quarter. Khan said iPhone Duo is constrained and that it is hard to predict when supply and demand balance; Ternus told Reuters Apple is not able to predict that balance, and he said a very small percentage of units were returned over display issues. Greater China revenue rose 21% to a quarterly record, driven by iPhone and Mac, while Bloomberg reported Chinese revenue still fell short of estimates. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Techmeme/status/2117566404958576819) · [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/02/apple-q4-2026-earnings-takeaways/) · [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/02/apple-memory-costs-increase-december/) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/apple-sales-cool) · [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/02/apple-says-its-hard-to-predict-when-iphone-duo-constraints-will-improve/) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-03/apple-sets-new-sales-highs-in-china-even-as-increased-costs-bite)

**EU court adviser says Gemini's use of press may infringe publisher rights: Reuters**
Advocate General Maciej Szpunar told Europe's highest court on Tuesday that Google's Gemini may infringe press publishers' rights in certain circumstances. He said the right may be infringed when an LLM-driven chatbot retrieves a publication from a press publisher's website, reuses it to generate an answer, and gives that answer to the user. Copyright, he said, does not protect the mere facts in a news report, only the specific form of expression. Use of copyrighted material to train large language models is, in his view, freely permitted under the text and data mining exception. He was advising in a case brought by Hungarian site operator Like Company against Google, and advocate-general opinions are usually followed by the judges. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/googles-use-press-by-ai-chatbot-may-infringe-copyright-rules-eu-court-adviser-2026-11-03/) · [thestandard.com.hk](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/world/article/347365/Googles-use-of-press-by-AI-chatbot-may-infringe-copyright-rules-EU-court-adviser-says)

### The Counterpoint
**The majority rule and the "some customers" account are not the same size of constraint: The Information**
The number that decides how hard Nvidia's instruction bites is whether a majority-of-clients rule is what was actually imposed. The Information's account, from three people familiar with the matter, is that some cloud customers were told to reduce Chinese-company exposure, which would narrow one route to advanced compute without stating a client-mix quota. Bloomberg's retelling, from unidentified people, is an instruction to scale back exposure. ### The Thread: The September scoreboard under the memory bid
Apple's iPhone business booked $57.6 billion in the September quarter, up 17% and a new September-quarter record, and that line is only the start of a split that also runs through Amazon's cloud, across the seven only where the same memory and compute bid shows up. Mac revenue was $10.8 billion, up from $8.7 billion, despite supply constraints. Full-year Mac revenue was $37.9 billion, up from $33.7 billion in 2025, and Ternus said Apple has never sold more Macs in a fiscal year than it did in 2026. iPad revenue fell to $6.2 billion from $7 billion, which Apple tied to supply constraints and a difficult compare with last year's A16 iPad. Services revenue was $31.6 billion, up from $28.8 billion, a new all-time record, and $123.3 billion for the full year of 2026. The App Store saw nearly a billion average weekly visitors, and the number of users paying for at least one service grew. Wearables, Home and Accessories were $8.3 billion, down 8%, against the prior-year launches of Apple Watch SE 3 and AirPods Pro 3. The new Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini and Apple HomeView did not ship in the September quarter. The installed base is more than 2.5 billion active devices.

The foldable sits on the same constrained shelf. The Verge reported the iPhone Duo launched last month at $1,999, with a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner screen, that preorders sold out, that some shipments are expected in 2027, and that a limited number were available in stores at launch. TechCrunch reported Apple is deepening a partnership with Perryman, a titanium producer, for materials for the foldable, and that Verizon has been offering gift cards while apologizing for the delays. An October Financial Times report, cited there, quoted Apple calling Duo demand nothing short of extraordinary after the device sold out on Apple's site within hours.

The shared constraint is memory, and TechCrunch tied it to soaring demand for memory chips from the AI industry, which has pushed component costs up for hardware makers across the board. Parekh said Apple's price increases were done reluctantly. Those June and September increases on iPads, Macs and iPhones, plus lower prices on some non-memory parts and memory bought earlier, offset part of the September pressure. Ternus said the benefit of that pre-bought memory declines over time. Khan said iPhone, iPad and Mac were constrained in the September quarter by demand plus limited availability of the advanced nodes the processors are made on, and that those node constraints are easing as more of the lineup moves to 2-nanometer chips. Mac and iPad supplies are expected to stay constrained in the December quarter, primarily because of memory, with demand higher than expected. Services revenue in that quarter is expected to grow 8% to 9%, and Apple expects the quarter to be the largest for revenue in its history.

Amazon is the other named side of the compute bid. BankInfoSecurity reported that AWS posted its fastest growth in five years, and attributed that pace to demand for AI agents. That is a separate measurement from Apple's device mix, not a figure Apple put on its own bill. What changes for Apple is which lines already show the squeeze: iPhone and Mac set records, iPad and wearables did not, and December is the quarter Apple named memory as the main constraint on Mac and iPad. What changes for Amazon is that agent demand is the workload a trade report credits for the fastest AWS growth in five years, the same class of compute demand TechCrunch says is bidding up the memory device makers now have to buy. The next dated window in these reports is that December quarter. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/02/apple-q4-2026-earnings-takeaways/) · [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1024915/apple-iphone-duo-supply-chain-constraints) · [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/02/apple-says-its-hard-to-predict-when-iphone-duo-constraints-will-improve/) · [bankinfosecurity.com](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/aws-posts-fastest-growth-in-five-years-on-ai-agent-demand-a-33255)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Space data centers could cost one hundred times Earth builds, Google's energy chief said.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google's head of data center energy said orbital data centers could cost up to one hundred times sites on Earth, even as Google tests AI server chips in orbit. Microsoft is opening Copilot to McGraw Hill's licensed curriculum, and Apple's unreleased HomeView software lists a HomeKit Secure Video camera mode ahead of a November 13 launch. Gemini can now rewrite a whole Google Slides deck from one prompt.

### Top News
**Google energy chief says space data centers could cost up to 100 times Earth sites: The Information**
Data centers in space could cost up to 100 times as much as those on Earth, Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's head of data center energy, said at The Information's WTF summit. The remark is a cost check from a company that is itself testing AI server chips in orbit. Corio's line was to explore terrestrial options before going extraterrestrial. The Information tied the comment to SpaceX orbital data-center plans that underpin part of a roughly $1.8 trillion market capitalization. Yesterday's coverage had her planning sites for 2031 or later; today's figure is the multiple on leaving the ground. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-energy-chief-space-data-centers-cost-100-times-earth)

**McGraw Hill will plug licensed course content into Microsoft Copilot: EdTech Innovation Hub**
McGraw Hill plans a Microsoft 365 Copilot plugin that connects K–12, higher education, and professional learning content through Model Context Protocol, so educators and students can summarize, translate, or adapt licensed materials into lesson plans and study aids. A limited beta is set for early 2027, only for eligible McGraw Hill higher-education and school-district customers who already hold Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses. Dave Cortese, McGraw Hill's chief digital information officer, said the collaboration expands into new channels "while maintaining control over how our content is used and valued." Deirdre Quarnstrom, vice president of Microsoft Education Experiences, said bringing those strengths into Copilot can help educators create more relevant learning experiences "while giving institutions a secure, governed way to adopt AI responsibly." The plugin sits beside McGraw Hill's own tools, including AI Reader, Sharpen, Learning Studio, Writing Assistant, and Teacher Assistant. McGraw Hill has also selected Copilot as its enterprise AI productivity tool. Interested institutions can register through the publisher's AI connector beta program. Source: [edtechinnovationhub.com](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/mcgraw-hill-to-bring-licensed-education-content-into-microsoft-copilot-through-new-ai-plugin)

**Gemini can edit an entire Google Slides deck from one prompt: MIXED News**
Google is rolling out a Gemini update that can edit multiple slides, or a whole presentation, from a single prompt in Google Slides, changing content, visual style, or matching another deck used as a style reference. Edits land on editable slides, not a flattened image, and the side panel then summarizes what changed, so undo and version history still apply. Suggested jobs include consistent title styles, removing page numbers, recoloring a deck, expanding or simplifying text from Drive files, condensing slides, or adding slides. Gemini chooses which slides to touch, so the result still needs review. The update is in English, on an extended rollout that began October 29, and can take longer than 15 days. Eligible plans are Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, Google AI Pro for Education, and personal Google AI Pro and Ultra. Workspace customers get promotional access to higher multi-slide creation limits through at least December 1, 2026. This is separate from the editor inside the Gemini chat app. Source: [mixed-news.com](https://mixed-news.com/en/google-slides-gemini-edit-entire-presentation-one-prompt/)

**A Gemini Gmail suit is refiled after a judge found no concrete harm: PPC Land**
PPC Land reported that Google faces a refiled suit over Gemini and Gmail after a judge found no concrete harm. Source: [ppc.land](https://ppc.land/google-faces-refiled-gemini-gmail-suit-after-judge-found-no-concrete-harm/)

**Trump administration withholds AI testing framework records: The Information**
The Trump administration declined to produce key documents on its voluntary AI testing framework, despite a September agreement with the nonprofit Protect Democracy Project after a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit. The Information reported that the refusal came in a letter sent to the nonprofit on Friday. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/trump-administration-refuses-release-information-ai-testing-framework)

### Company Desk
**HomeView software lists a HomeKit camera mode and ships on version 26.5: MacRumors**
Code sleuth pdfu found settings strings in HomeView Software 27.2 for four camera modes — Off, Detect Activity, Stream, and "Stream & Allow Recording" — plus schedules for home, away, or asleep, and a HomeView-specific 1080p/30fps path with microphone input that the software selects for HomeKit Secure Video sessions. Other strings limit streams and recordings to home members, show a green light and play a sound when a stream is viewed or recording starts, and notify users when camera settings change. An away schedule is listed, but the strings suggest streaming and recording can be enabled from the HomeView itself only while people are home. HomeView launches Friday, November 13, starting at 299. ### The Thread: Fifty million agents, Meta's Muse on Microsoft's container
Microsoft's quarter ended September 30, 2026, is the bill for the layer Satya Nadella is calling an operating system for work. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $63.9 billion, up 30 percent from a year earlier. Total revenue was $92.3 billion, up 19 percent. Operating income was $45.9 billion, up 21 percent. Azure revenue rose 48 percent. Reported net income was $36.6 billion, up 32 percent. Adjusted net income, removing the impact of investments in OpenAI, was $36.4 billion, up 18 percent. EdTech Innovation Hub carried those figures from the quarter and from Nadella's LinkedIn post on the same results.

Copilot daily users increased nearly 50 percent from the previous quarter and more than fivefold from a year earlier. Customers with more than 50,000 Copilot seats increased eightfold year over year. Nadella also reported a nearly 20 percent quarterly improvement in user satisfaction; the post did not say how that measure was calculated. The latest Copilot update brings Chat, Cowork, Autopilot, and Code into one experience. Dynamics 365 capabilities are being pulled into Copilot so employees can reach business processes through the assistant. On GitHub Copilot Fusion, which coordinates multiple models, he wrote that it delivers frontier-level quality at up to 77 percent lower cost. Foundry revenue more than tripled from a year earlier. Customers building with multiple AI models increased fivefold. Revenue from open-source models grew tenfold. Nearly 60,000 customers were accessing context through Microsoft IQ, up 25 percent from the previous quarter. More than 50 million agents were registered in Agent 365, up 30 percent quarter over quarter.

The shared machine is Microsoft Execution Containers, MXC, which links Windows and Agent 365 so an agent has a controlled environment on a device. Nadella named Meta Muse among the agents adopting it, next to OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code. Meta is not the landlord. Muse is a guest on Microsoft's runtime. Perception, Microsoft's security tools, sits outside the model and governs identity, permissions, and which actions an agent is authorized to take.

That split changes the spend and the product. Microsoft's quarterly capital expenditure was $45.2 billion. Cash from operations rose 29 percent to $58 billion. Free cash flow after property and equipment was $18.6 billion. For the following quarter Microsoft expects revenue of $96 billion to $97.1 billion, and Azure growth of 49 to 50 percent excluding currency, with demand still ahead of supply. Nadella's stated priority is maximizing intelligence per task while optimizing cost and performance. For Meta, Muse on MXC is a shopping assistant that can run inside another company's device container, not only inside Meta's own apps. For Microsoft, a named Meta agent on the adoption list is evidence the container is a platform, not only a Copilot feature. No source today dates the next MXC release.

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Thousands of UK publishers now face a CMA case over Meta's AI content terms.**

**What You Need to Know:** Thousands of UK publishers now face a CMA case over Meta's AI content terms. The watchdog is asking whether Meta can take website content for its own products, including AI, from businesses that use its services. The CMA board is due to consider its next strategic-market-status proposals in spring 2027.

### Top News
**CMA opens a Meta investigation over publisher content for AI: The Next Web**
The UK Competition and Markets Authority on Friday opened a Competition Act 1998 investigation into whether Meta holds a dominant position and is imposing terms that let it collect content from the websites of businesses and publishers that use its services, then use that content in its own products, including AI, without those businesses choosing whether or how it is used. Sarah Cardell, the CMA's chief executive, said digital platforms help UK businesses reach millions of customers, but a company with a dominant position must not use it to impose unfair terms. The watchdog said the terms could be an unlawful imposition of unfair trading conditions on thousands of UK businesses, and it acted on concerns from the News Media Association and the Movement for an Open Web. Meta had planned the terms for 30 October, pushed them to 20 November after talks with the CMA, and on 28 October paused the rollout until it has consulted industry groups. In Norway, a court earlier in the week temporarily banned Meta from enforcing the new terms after 10 media outlets argued the terms threatened their rights to their content. Separately, the CMA is asking Meta for information about Meta One, its business subscription, after the Federation of Small Businesses raised concerns about small firms posting external links on Facebook and Instagram without paying; the regulator has not decided on formal action, and that question sits outside the new investigation. Source: [thenextweb.com](https://thenextweb.com/news/cma-meta-investigation-publishers-ai-terms)

**Meta builds a 106-pound humanoid with Fourier: The Information**
Meta has built a prototype humanoid with Chinese robotics company Fourier and is already working on a second version, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the initiative. The roughly 106-pound machine, known internally as Max, was built in three months. The goal was to help Meta's robotics arm develop a more polished future product for people's homes that it could eventually release. No launch target had been set. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/meta-built-humanoid-prototype-chinese-startup-ramp-robotics-push)

**Google's data-center energy chief is planning sites for 2031 or later: The Information**
Google's data center energy chief is planning for facilities that will not come online until 2031 or later. The Information, drawing on the WTF Summit, said that timeline exposes a widening gap between AI chip development and power availability. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/everyones-using-ai-divisions-growing-wtf-highlights)

**Apple Maps starts blurring NASA, Space Force and Air Force bases: 9to5Mac**
Apple Maps has begun blurring NASA, Space Force and Air Force bases. The change blocks views of fighters on tarmacs and rockets on launch pads. Source: [spaceexplored.com](https://spaceexplored.com/2026/10/30/apple-maps-begins-blurring-nasa-space-force-and-air-force-bases/)

### Company Desk
**EU label puts the iPad mini 8 battery at 4,900 mAh: MacRumors**
Apple's EU energy label for the iPad mini 8 lists a battery capacity of 4,900 mAh, or 18.9 watt-hours, against 5,034 mAh and 19.3 watt-hours on the previous model. Apple's site lists the same battery-life estimates for both, which MacRumors ties to the A20 Pro's efficiency and to the new OLED panel, where black pixels turn fully off. The mini has an 8.5-inch OLED display, an Acoustic Display audio system instead of speaker holes, Wi-Fi 7, and a design Apple describes as 15 percent thinner and lighter. It is available to pre-order and launches on Friday, November 6, with US pricing starting at $699. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/31/ipad-mini-8-battery-capacity-mah-wh/)

**Microsoft's new buyout drops the age and tenure bar: GeekWire**
Microsoft is offering buyouts to about 60,000 employees, about a quarter of its workforce, including some executives. Unlike the retirement program it offered in the spring, this offer has no age or tenure requirement, and business leaders decide whether their groups take part. GeekWire also noted $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI, more than Microsoft made from Xbox or Bing. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/microsofts-big-buyout-amazons-trillion-dollar-future-and-an-ai-wearable-reviews-our-show/)

**Nvidia shows OOI optical packaging, with prototype samples in hand: BigGo Finance**
Nvidia has unveiled an optical packaging architecture it calls OOI, in which the optical engine sits directly on the silicon interposer. BigGo Finance reported that prototype samples are in hand. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/25fb0763-dca8-46e5-9a4d-7fd23359e200)

### Also Today
**Gemini's in-chat file editor is live for a free account: Notebookcheck**
Notebookcheck tested Gemini on November 1 with a free Google account in Germany and found the in-chat editor already live on the web, after Google said on October 29 that generated documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets and code can be edited in the conversation for all users, with no subscription, while the Android and iOS apps can edit only PDFs. Source: [notebookcheck.net](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Google-Gemini-now-lets-free-users-edit-generated-PDFs-in-chat.1439329.0.html)

**AWS releases File Mover Express for S3 transfers: InfoQ**
AWS has released File Mover Express, an open-source tool for S3 file transfers. Source: [infoq.com](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-s3-file-transfer/)

**A Gemini tool cut UK planners' assessment time 58 percent: FourWeekMBA**
FourWeekMBA reported that a Google Gemini tool cut UK planners' assessment time by 58 percent. Source: [fourweekmba.com](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-googles-gemini-tool-cut-uk-planners-assessment-time-58/)

### The Counterpoint
**Meta says the publisher case has no grounds: The Next Web**
Meta said there were "no grounds" for an investigation. A spokesperson said the company has already committed not to change its terms without consulting publishers and other stakeholders, and that it welcomes the chance to explain its approach to the CMA. The regulator itself said no decision has been made on whether Meta broke the law, and the case first has to decide whether Meta holds a dominant position in a relevant UK market. Meta has not been designated with strategic market status under the UK's newer digital-markets regime, the designation that would give the CMA wider powers. Source: [thenextweb.com](https://thenextweb.com/news/cma-meta-investigation-publishers-ai-terms)

### The Thread: Two backlogs, one cash test
Google Cloud's backlog climbed 256 percent to $561 billion. Amazon Web Services' backlog rose 189 percent to $578 billion. Together those stocks of contracted work are about $1.14 trillion, the figure Goldman Sachs strategists Mark Wilson and Tony Pasquariello are split on, TokenPost reported.

Google Cloud revenue increased 103 percent year over year. AWS revenue grew 39 percent. Wilson argues that the growth rates and the backlogs show AI demand remains strong and that returns are beginning to materialize at the large cloud providers. He also treats the figures as an answer to doubts about whether AI investment is paying off. Pasquariello argues the other side of the same print. Cloud growth, he says, may conceal weakness in other core businesses. Rising capital spending at technology companies has not, in his view, demonstrated comparable earnings-growth potential. He points to slower upward revisions to forward earnings-per-share estimates, and to signs that S&P 500 earnings growth may have peaked.

The cash number sitting next to the backlog is Alphabet's, not a blended cloud total. Alphabet recorded a $910 million free cash flow outflow for the quarter, compared with market expectations for a $3.5 billion inflow. Goldman Sachs strategist Rich Privorotsky framed the industry question as which companies in AI will capture the profits, and what financing costs they will face. In October, the S&P 500 excluding AI stocks outperformed technology shares. Both strategists described market volatility as unusual. They differed on whether the AI rally would continue.

The shared object is the backlog: work customers have committed to that has not yet been recognized as revenue. Both clouds are using that stock to show that AI capacity has buyers lined up, and both are still in the build. They are not the same shape of business. Alphabet's cloud revenue is the faster of the two, up 103 percent, and its backlog of $561 billion is the one that jumped 256 percent. Amazon's cloud grew 39 percent, and its backlog is the larger pile, $578 billion, up 189 percent. The $1.14 trillion sum is the joint claim. What it changes for Alphabet is already a cash result: an outflow of $910 million in a quarter when market expectations had been an inflow of $3.5 billion. What it changes for Amazon is that a $578 billion backlog now has to be read against Pasquariello's warning that cloud strength can hide slower earnings momentum elsewhere, while capital spending still runs ahead of the profit it is supposed to produce. Wilson reads the combined figure as returns starting to form. Pasquariello reads it as a mask. Privorotsky's financing-cost question hangs over both, because a backlog is a delivery promise, and delivery on this scale is being built with other people's capital as well as the cloud providers' own cash.

HomeView, priced at $299 in the US, launches on Friday, November 13. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/31/apple-homeview-software-tour/)

Jules is headed for shutdown on December 31. Source: [testingcatalog.com](https://www.testingcatalog.com/google-tests-new-gemini-4-carbon-checkpoint-arena/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **More than fifty apps now run inside Gemini and Search, and Google bars their ads.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google’s Connected Apps preview puts outside tools inside Gemini and Search and forbids those partners from serving third-party ads. Apple set a November 4 developer beta for the first Apple Intelligence features in mainland China, with Alibaba’s Qwen handling some requests. Counterpoint Research measured the iPhone 18 Pro launch as a China-led gain against declines in the United States and Japan.

### Top News
**Google Opens Gemini and Search to Apps, Bars Their Ads: FourWeekMBA**
Google said on October 28 it is launching a preview of the Connected Apps Platform so developers can bring capabilities into Gemini and Search, with more than 50 Connected Apps already live between the two. Developers integrate a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, register through the Google Connected Console, and choose before review whether an app goes live in Search, the Gemini app, or both; a remote MCP server reaches Gemini and Search on web, Android, and iOS, while Android MCP reaches Gemini users on Android. The category chosen at registration cannot be changed later, developers must list at least three capabilities, and Google reviews each app, requiring test accounts with sample data where sign-in is needed. The Connected Apps Policy says partners must not serve any third-party advertising or promotional material, must offer direct utility free of advertising, and may still include their own brand elements; an app also must not use overly broad or deceptive capability descriptions to get the model to select it over another app, and Google can reject the app, suspend it, remove it, or suspend or terminate the developer account. Adobe, Experian, Localiza, and Peloton are live in Gemini, with those apps coming to Search in the coming weeks, plus a new Calm integration on both; Search’s AI Mode connected apps in the United States, in English, include Instacart, Canva, YouTube Music, Yahoo Fantasy Football, and Sleeper, and AI Mode may default to the last app used for a task. Sundar Pichai’s figure this week was one billion Gemini app users, and Google said it is opening access in phases, adding developers, markets, and Google products over the coming months, with live apps able to track traffic, latency, and error rates. Source: [fourweekmba.com](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-google-opens-gemini-and-search-to-apps-bars-their-ads/) | https://www.searchenginejournal.com/google-connected-apps-preview-ai-mode-gemini/595268/

**Apple Confirms iOS 27.3 Beta Release Date With Apple Intelligence in China: The Mac Observer**
After Apple Intelligence stayed off iPhones sold in mainland China, Apple said testing of the first wave starts November 4, 2026, with the latest iOS developer beta, and the public release comes with iOS 27.3 in December 2026. The package includes Writing Tools, Live Translation in Messages, FaceTime, Phone, and supported AirPods, Visual Intelligence, Genmoji, Photos Clean Up, notification summaries, and related Mail and Notes tools, on the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, iPhone 16 and later, iPhone Air, and iPhone Duo, with the device and Siri set to English or Simplified Chinese. Apple has partnered with Alibaba so Siri, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence can hand some requests to Qwen, including questions about photos and documents; access uses a Qwen account or Sign in with Apple. Alibaba said Apple asks for consent before a question, document, or image is sent to Qwen, that the integration is opt-in, and that user requests and generated replies will not be used to train Alibaba’s models. Siri AI, Image Playground, and the other next-generation Apple Intelligence features from WWDC 2026 stay out of this release, and iPad, Mac, and other devices wait on further approvals. Outside mainland China, Apple Intelligence and the ChatGPT option stay as they are. Source: [macobserver.com](https://www.macobserver.com/news/apple-confirms-ios-27-3-beta-release-date-with-apple-intelligence-in-china/) | https://www.martincid.com/technology-sv/apple-intelligence-china-ios-27-3-qwen-siri/ | https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202610/1373351.shtml

**iPhone 18 Pro Sales Surge in China, Offsetting Decline in U.S. and Japan: MacRumors**
Counterpoint Research said combined global sales of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max rose 3.1 percent in their first three weeks versus the equivalent launch period last year. China sales increased 29 percent, which Counterpoint attributed to better initial supply and higher prices for competing Android flagships, while U.S. sales fell 4 percent and Japan fell 27 percent. In the United States, Counterpoint said buyers perceived insufficient changes to features and design despite additions such as the variable aperture camera. Apple raised starting prices by 100 dollars in the U.S., bringing the Pro to 1,199 dollars and the Pro Max to 1,299 dollars, and Counterpoint said exchange rates compounded price increases in Japan. The Pro Max share of sales slipped from 57 percent to 56 percent, with growth in India and Southeast Asia favoring the smaller model. The tracking period predates the iPhone Duo’s launch on October 23. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/31/iphone-18-pro-sales-surge-in-china/)

**HomeView Software 27.2: Wallpapers, Control Center, and More: MacRumors**
Apple released HomeView Software 27.2, build 24V514, for the HomeView hub that launches November 13 and is priced at 299 dollars, with pre-orders open. The update includes 20 default wallpapers in light and dark variations, and users will also likely be able to set their own photo wallpaper. Unlike iOS, HomeView does not use SpringBoard; its launcher is called BreadBoard, and the Control Center UI process is called CupBoard. The software shows a Hello screen at startup, Control Center in a setup animation, automatic Light and Dark Mode, and Snoopy animations on the Snoopy face. A hidden HomeView Software 26 graphic adds to evidence that Apple had planned an earlier launch. HomeView launches alongside the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K on November 13. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/30/homeview-software-27-2/) | https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/30/download-all-20-apple-homeview-wallpapers-in-light-and-dark-mode-here/

### Company Desk
**Washington governor rips Microsoft over TV ad in leaked audio: GeekWire**
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson criticized Microsoft for funding a PAC whose TV ad, aired during Seahawks games, says “Olympia is broken.” Microsoft has given the group, Washington Needs to Compete, more than 5 million dollars of the 13.8 million dollars it has raised. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/washington-governor-rips-microsoft-over-tv-ad-in-leaked-audio/)

### The Counterpoint
**Google is expanding its own AI Mode ads while partner apps cannot carry any: FourWeekMBA**
The same week Google barred Connected Apps from third-party advertising, Alphabet said on its October 29 earnings call that it is expanding ads in AI Mode into international markets, alongside multi-turn ads in AI Mode in the U.S. On that call the company also said strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization it was seeing in AI Mode. The apps sit at the moment of intent; the ad inventory Google is adding is Google’s, and the queries driving the new surface are the ones Alphabet said monetize less. Source: [fourweekmba.com](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-google-opens-gemini-and-search-to-apps-bars-their-ads/)

### The Thread: The flash shelf flipped
Two years ago Apple bought nearly twice the flash storage of Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Google combined, according to TechInsights estimates in a Wall Street Journal report carried by MacRumors. Hyperscalers are now buying double Apple’s share. That is the shared component under iPhones and under the data centers those four companies are filling.

As the iPhone took off, Apple became the world’s largest buyer of flash storage and used the leverage. The Journal account says that after ordering flash at rock-bottom prices, Apple would refuse delivery at times if prices were falling, leaving suppliers holding unsold chips, including ones custom-made for Apple. Kioxia, previously Toshiba Memory, had executives who joked they felt like Charlie Brown trying to kick the football. Apple is also said to have pressed flash makers to open their books so it could monitor sales and check that no one else got a better deal. Around the end of 2015, Sandisk refused requests for additional supply because it already had customers willing to pay more. Tony Blevins, then head of procurement, threatened a Sandisk salesman and said he would have Sandisk’s chief executive, Sanjay Mehrotra, crawl on his knees back to Apple, according to a person familiar with the call. SK Hynix and Samsung were not in those examples.

The AI data-center build is what reversed the table. Flash storage and RAM now go into those centers in volume, and the buyers on the other side of TechInsights’ old comparison — Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Google — are the hyperscalers whose combined purchases have passed Apple. Apple has raised prices on more than a dozen products this year, including iPhones, iPads, Macs, HomePods, and the Apple TV, and attributed the increases to the memory chip shortage. Former CEO Tim Cook said the price increases were unavoidable. An Apple spokesperson told the Journal that Apple has worked with many suppliers for decades, values the partnership, and looks forward to continuing the work.

The margin on the upgrade customers actually buy is already thinner. TechInsights estimated that Apple makes a gross profit of 134 dollars when a customer spends 200 dollars to move an iPhone 18 Pro from 256 gigabytes to 512 gigabytes, down from 185 dollars on the equivalent upgrade for the iPhone 17 Pro last year. Higher shelf prices can mean lower demand, so Apple is not fully insulated from the shortage it is passing on. On an earnings call this week, SK Hynix forecast that the memory chip shortage will persist through 2030. MacRumors read that as the bargaining pendulum staying away from Apple for at least four more years. The dated marker in the supplier’s own forecast is 2030. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/30/apple-flash-storage-suppliers-revenge-report/)

### On the Calendar
Developer testing of the first Apple Intelligence features in mainland China starts November 4, 2026, with the public iOS 27.3 release set for December 2026. Source: [macobserver.com](https://www.macobserver.com/news/apple-confirms-ios-27-3-beta-release-date-with-apple-intelligence-in-china/)

HomeView, priced at 299 dollars, launches November 13 alongside the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/30/homeview-software-27-2/)

Adobe, Experian, Localiza, and Peloton apps that are live in Gemini come to Search in the coming weeks. Source: [fourweekmba.com](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-google-opens-gemini-and-search-to-apps-bars-their-ads/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Two senators set a November 25 deadline for Meta to account for glasses footage.**

**What You Need to Know:** Two senators set a November 25 deadline for Meta to account for glasses footage. Amazon’s cloud sales reached $46 billion in the quarter, up 39.3 percent, with 2026 cash capital spending still about $220 billion. Nvidia is in talks to back debt for an Nscale data-centre site that Anthropic plans to use.

### Top News
**Senators question Meta on AI glasses privacy: Tech Times**
Senators Ron Wyden and Edward Markey wrote to chief executive Mark Zuckerberg after human reviewers reportedly watched people undressing, using the bathroom, and engaging in sexual activity in footage from Meta’s AI glasses, including people who did not know they were being filmed. They want Meta to explain privacy checks before launch, how captured imagery is used, and whether people can have data deleted. An earlier investigation by two Swedish news outlets, as reported via Gizmodo, found third-party data labellers in Kenya viewed sexual content recorded through the glasses; the senators’ letter says contractors described that footage. Meta disclosures cited by the senators state that imagery processed through the glasses’ visual AI features may be retained and used to train AI systems, including with human reviewers. A wearer option, reported via VitalLaw, lets owners stop visual data from being retained for AI training. The senators write that “individuals captured without their consent have no corresponding control over the processing of their images or data,” and they asked Zuckerberg to respond by 25 November. Source: [techtimes.co.uk](https://www.techtimes.co.uk/senators-question-meta-privacy-ai-smart-glasses-1809567)

**Amazon Q3 sales rise 12% to $201.9B as AWS growth hits 39%: Türkiye Today**
Amazon reported third-quarter net sales of $201.9 billion, up 12 percent from $180.2 billion, or 13 percent excluding a $900 million unfavorable foreign-exchange impact. Operating income rose 61 percent to $28.1 billion from $17.4 billion, and the operating margin reached a record 13.9 percent. AWS net sales rose 39.3 percent to $46 billion, the fastest pace in nearly five years, with an annualized run rate of $184 billion; AWS operating income rose 56 percent to $17.8 billion from $11.4 billion. North America sales grew 6 percent to $112.9 billion; international sales rose 5 percent to $43.1 billion, or 8 percent excluding currency. Net income slipped 2 percent to $20.7 billion, or $1.89 per diluted share, from $21.2 billion, or $1.95, primarily because the year-ago quarter included a $9.5 billion pre-tax gain on Anthropic. NewsCord’s comparison of outlets says earnings per share of $1.89 missed a FactSet consensus of $1.97, and that free cash flow was negative $42.4 billion for the 12 months through September, against positive $14.8 billion a year earlier, with net cash outlays for property and equipment up $94.8 billion. Andy Jassy said AWS growth is projected above 40 percent in both 2027 and 2028, that no business has reached a trillion dollars of annual revenue, and that Amazon may have two such businesses in five to ten years. Fourth-quarter net sales are guided at $240 billion to $247 billion, growth of 12 percent to 16 percent, and operating income at $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion, against $25 billion a year earlier. Cash capital expenditure for 2026 remains about $220 billion. Jassy also cited a contracted backlog of $578 billion and said 2027 capital spending will be meaningfully higher; GeekWire, via that same roundup, reported CFO Brian Olsavsky saying Amazon Leo satellite costs are weighing on the fourth-quarter profit forecast. The Register reported that AWS is installing an AI accelerator every 14 seconds. Source: [turkiyetoday.com](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/business/amazon-q3-sales-rise-12-to-2019b-as-aws-growth-hits-39-3231326) Source: [newscord.org](https://newscord.org/article/amazon-misses-earnings-aws-revenue-jumps-39-as-shares-drop-more-than-7--Story_20261029_Amazonreportedboomin5195d6ef) Source: [theregister.com](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/10/30/aws-installs-an-ai-accelerator-every-14-seconds-and-eyes-1-trillion-annual-revenue/5306547)

**Nvidia in talks to backstop Nscale’s Anthropic site: Bloomberg**
Nvidia is in discussions to provide credit guarantees for an Nscale data-centre facility that Anthropic plans to use, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg. The Information reports talks to provide billions of dollars in credit guarantees for debt on a 460-megawatt centre tied to a $45 billion Anthropic project; the deal is not signed, and terms could change. The same report frames the talks as further support for neoclouds including Nscale, CoreWeave, and Firmus. The Financial Times describes Nscale, a Nvidia-backed neocloud seeking a $35 billion IPO, as betting on a West Virginia campus hit by construction issues, local opposition, and financing risks. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-29/nvidia-in-talks-to-offer-credit-support-for-nscale-project) Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/nvidia-talks-provide-billions-credit-support-cloud-providers-45-billion-anthropic-deal) Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/ee86c4b6-1fe4-467e-8f18-9c08df288aff?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

**Reddit’s CEO says Google’s AI Mode does not drive traffic: The Verge**
On Reddit’s third-quarter 2026 earnings call, chief executive Steve Huffman said Google’s AI-powered search modes do not help traffic to the platform. Reddit said search traffic in October has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1022848/reddit-ceo-google-ai-mode-traffic)

**Meta raises equity and preferred for an AI buildout: Simply Wall St**
Simply Wall St reports that Meta Platforms raised $25 billion in a follow-on Class A share sale and $12.5 billion of preferred stock, tied to AI infrastructure, Muse products, and expanded work with Nvidia and AMD on chips, networking, and software. The same account says 2026 AI capital expenditure is $130 billion to $145 billion, that free cash flow has turned negative, and that legal costs include a $25 billion New Mexico penalty. Meta reports millions of AMD EPYC processors in use, AMD Helios rack-scale systems in testing toward broader deployment, and AMD Instinct GPUs already in production for training and recommendation engines, with day-zero support for Muse Spark Open and Muse Glimmer on AMD GPUs, Ryzen AI PCs, and Radeon cards. Those two steps sit on contractor access and on whether a clip is made at all; they do not answer the November 25 request for deletion rights for people who never wore the device. The number that still decides the letter is whether Zuckerberg’s reply, due 25 November, gives bystanders a deletion path the wearer toggle does not. Source: [techtimes.co.uk](https://www.techtimes.co.uk/senators-question-meta-privacy-ai-smart-glasses-1809567)

### The Thread: One inference bill, Meta and Nvidia on the customer list
AWS signed new agreements this quarter with Meta and with NVIDIA, on a list that also names OpenAI, Salesforce, Oracle, Qualcomm, Verizon, ADP, Stripe, and NATO. The product those names sit on is Amazon Bedrock, not a new campus announcement.

Fortune 500 companies spent nearly 7 times more on Bedrock year over year. Total Bedrock token volume grew nearly 17 times year over year. The quarter’s model additions on Bedrock include OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, and GPT-6.1 Sol; Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5; Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3; SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7; Z.ai’s GLM 5.3; and two purpose-built cybersecurity models from OpenAI. Built-in web search for OpenAI models on Bedrock is meant to ground answers in current information without a customer-built retrieval pipeline. Bedrock Managed Agents, a public preview powered by OpenAI, is the managed path Amazon is offering for production agents.

Strands harness, released as open source, starts with a single line of code and can run locally, on Bedrock AgentCore, or on another provider. AWS says it lowers the cost of agent tasks by 32 percent through token efficiency versus other harnesses on the same frontier models, with equal or better accuracy. Strands Box, in preview, is an open-source sandbox for rules on agent behavior and access, meant to hold on a desktop, in AgentCore, or elsewhere.

AgentCore is in use by tens of thousands of customers, who deployed 2 times more agents in the third quarter than in the prior three quarters combined. Lambda topped a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate; named users include Samsung, Volkswagen, United Airlines, Mercedes-Benz, and Booking.com. Lambda Web Functions adds web apps on that same serverless base, with Lambda handling scaling, multi-region distribution, and active CPU billing.

AWS Continuum, which discovers, prioritizes, validates, and remediates software vulnerabilities at machine speed, is generally available, and AWS is bringing it into Anthropic’s Claude Code, OpenAI’s Codex, and AWS’s Kiro. Named users include Capital One, IBM, Infor, Luminate, and Robinhood. Amazon Quick now reaches Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, and can keep running when a laptop is closed.

The shared dependency is the runtime, not the chip invoice. Meta and NVIDIA appear here as AWS customers in the same quarter they show up elsewhere as infrastructure partners and suppliers. Amazon’s measurable claim in this release is usage: 7 times the Fortune 500 Bedrock spend, 17 times the tokens, a 32 percent cut in agent-task cost, twice the agents versus the prior three quarters combined, and a $1 billion Lambda run rate. Meta gets a contracted inference path beside its own buildout. NVIDIA is on the buyer side of AWS while still selling accelerators into everyone else’s factories. The About Amazon note names no next dated step for these agreements. Source: [aboutamazon.com](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview?utm_source=rss)
