# MAG 7 Daily
> **Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59, ahead of Claude and GPT-6, for cyber teams first.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon posts 59 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, just ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, and the first copies go to cyber defenders rather than the open Gemini app. Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro is on a November 6 launch, and Amazon put five new Alexa devices on sale the same week it confirmed device-unit job cuts.

### Top News
**Google's Gemini 4 Carbon promises a leap in coding and cyber defence: Engadget**
Google released Gemini 4 Carbon on top of Gemini 4 Argon, which it launched two weeks earlier, and Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, called Carbon the company’s strongest model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon work. Access starts this week with selected cyber-defence teams, then trusted partners through the Fairwind programme, while Google says it is in the US government’s voluntary pre-release testing process; Argon is already in the Gemini app and AI search mode, and no wide Carbon date was set. Google says Carbon scored 59 on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and GPT-6 Astra at 57, up from Argon’s 50. On tests Google cited, Carbon scored 88.2 percent on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8 percent on ExploitGym and 71.0 percent on CWE-bench, with secure-code success more than double Argon’s and the Chrome team reporting patch quality more than ten times that of another lab’s large frontier model. Introductory pricing matches Argon at 2 dollars per million input tokens and 10 dollars per million output tokens, cached input 95 percent below the standard input rate, and Basic Tutorials reported those rates later rise to 4 dollars and 20 dollars. Source: [engadget.com](https://www.engadget.com/2300677/google-gemini-carbon-promises-significant-leap-in-ai-coding-and-cybersecurity/) · [itbrief.asia](https://itbrief.asia/story/google-unveils-gemini-4-carbon-with-cyber-focus) · [basic-tutorials.com](https://basic-tutorials.com/news/gemini-4-carbon-googles-new-flagship-ai-model-for-cybersecurity-and-coding/)

**Apple unveils touchscreen MacBook Pro: Bangkok Post**
Apple unveiled the MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display and Touch, its first touchscreen Mac and the first Mac with OLED, in 14-inch and 16-inch models with Dynamic Island, tandem OLED and a touch sensor built into the panel. Apple lists up to 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, a 120Hz refresh that can drop to 10Hz, P3 and Adobe RGB coverage, up to 24 hours of battery life, a 1.36–1.81 kg design, M5 Pro and M5 Max, up to 128GB of unified memory, up to 16TB of storage, a six-speaker system with 50 percent deeper bass, Thunderbolt 5 and a 12MP Centre Stage camera. NewsCord put the 14-inch at 2,899 dollars, the 16-inch at 3,399 dollars and a fully loaded configuration at 14,549 dollars; The Information said the latest MacBook Pro without a touchscreen starts at 1,999 dollars, and MacRumors said the OLED models carry a 400-dollar premium over comparable mini-LED models. NewsCord said pre-orders open October 30 and the machines launch November 6. Johny Srouji called the machine a monumental step forward for the Mac, John Ternus introduced it after taking over from Tim Cook last month, and NewsCord recalled Steve Jobs calling touchscreen Macs ergonomically terrible — “your arm wants to fall off” — and Tim Cook comparing a laptop-tablet combination to a refrigerator and a toaster. Source: [bangkokpost.com](https://www.bangkokpost.com/life/tech/3345780/apple-unveils-touchscreen-macbook-pro) · [newscord.org](https://newscord.org/article/apple-unveils-touchscreen-macbook-pro-with-proled-xdr-display-starting-at-us2899--Story_20261028_ApplestouchscreenMac377849b6) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-cloud-closes-azure-microsoft-wins-day-investors) · [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/28/apple-announcements-october-2026/)

**Amazon launches Alexa gadgets and cuts device jobs: Silicon UK**
Amazon on Wednesday launched five devices for its updated Alexa service: Echo Show 16, a 16-inch display with built-in Fire TV and a night-vision camera, from 499.99 dollars; a refreshed Echo Studio at 249.99 dollars with a camera; an Echo Dot at 99.99 dollars with a smart-home hub and Wi-Fi extender; Echo Time at 199.99 dollars, which uses sleep sensing to time a wake-up without a wearable; and Alexa Photo Frame from 199.99 dollars, syncing pictures from Amazon Photos. Amazon confirmed to Silicon UK that it cut a “small number” of roles and said the cuts would improve efficiency; a Reuters report, citing an unnamed person familiar with the matter, put the devices-and-services reduction at up to 250 people, mostly in software development, after about 1,000 core-retail cuts earlier this month. Marketscreener set the nearby Apple hardware at 299 dollars for HomeView and 149 dollars for HomePod mini 2, both on the latest Siri, and noted OpenAI is developing its own hardware. Source: [silicon.co.uk](https://www.silicon.co.uk/cloud/ai/amazon-alexa-cuts-632095) · [marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AMAZON-COM-INC-12864605/news/Amazon-launches-five-new-Alexa-devices-to-strengthen-its-position-in-the-smart-home-54588203/)

### Company Desk
**Microsoft pulls Copilot as AI on smart TVs fails to take off: FlatpanelsHD**
FlatpanelsHD reported that Microsoft is pulling Copilot after AI on smart TVs failed to take off. KuCoin reported that LG is discontinuing the Microsoft Copilot AI service on its TVs. Source: [flatpanelshd.com](https://www.flatpanelshd.com/news.php?subaction) · [kucoin.com](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/lg-announces-microsoft-copilot-ai-service-to-be-discontinued-on-tvs)

### Also Today
**Russia now requires Apple to store user communications: 9to5Mac**
Bloomberg, as reported by 9to5Mac, says Apple and Microsoft are now under Russian rules that require companies to store users’ communications and hand them to security agencies if requested. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/28/russia-now-requires-apple-to-store-user-communications-and-hand-them-over-if-requested/)

**Apple and OpenAI trade-secrets lawsuit now has a trial date: 9to5Mac**
Judge Edward Davila set the schedule, including a trial date, in Apple’s trade-secrets case against two former employees, OpenAI and io Products. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/28/apple-and-openai-trade-secrets-lawsuit-now-has-an-official-trial-date/)

**Meta delays update amid concern about scraping websites for AI training: PCMag**
PCMag reported that Meta delayed an update amid concern about scraping websites for potential AI training. Source: [pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/news/meta-delays-update-alarm-over-scraping-websites-for-potential-ai-training)

**Nvidia unveils DSX POD server racks: TradingView**
Nvidia unveiled DSX POD server racks intended to speed AI factory buildouts. Source: [tradingview.com](https://www.tradingview.com/news/cryptobriefing:87028f528094b:0-nvidia-unveils-dsx-pod-server-racks-to-speed-up-ai-factory-buildouts/)

**Google DeepMind and Google Cloud deploy AI across Singapore’s health system: TradingView**
Google DeepMind and Google Cloud are deploying AI across Singapore’s health system. Source: [tradingview.com](https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:7c6b26218094b:0-google-deepmind-and-google-cloud-deploy-ai-across-singapore-s-health-system/)

### The Counterpoint
**First on the composite index, second or worse on several jobs that buyers actually run: BigGo Finance**
BigGo Finance’s read of the same launch cuts the “near sweep” claim: paired with Google’s Antigravity tool, Carbon scored 59 on an agentic-coding index, short of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 at 62, and on FrontierSWE 2, GPT-6 Astra led at 65.5 percent against Carbon’s 61.2 percent. On the Vals Index, covering finance, coding, legal and tax tasks, Carbon ranked second at 70.36 percent, behind Sonnet 5.5 at 70.85 percent, and on WebDev Arena it placed fourth. The three headline cyber scores, including 54.8 percent on a 10-hour ExploitGym test, were measured without safety guardrails enabled, so the defensive chain Google is selling was not scored in the configuration customers would actually be allowed to run. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/d80ab5e2-0f44-436e-93d7-ddfd9619cbe5)

### The Thread: Two cloud lines, one September quarter
Google Cloud revenue more than doubled in the September quarter, to over 30 billion dollars, and that unit’s operating income tripled to 11.12 billion dollars. Azure revenue in the same period was 33 billion dollars, up 48 percent. Yesterday the open question on this show was still the growth rate; those two lines are the answer, and they leave the long-time number-three cloud business a few billion dollars from Azure.

Alphabet reported a 25 percent rise in company revenue to 127.58 billion dollars, slightly short of Wall Street forecasts, The Information wrote. Free cash flow turned negative by more than 9 billion dollars, against positive free cash flow of more than 24 billion dollars a year earlier. Search advertising grew 12 percent to 63.35 billion dollars, the softest growth in that business since the second quarter of 2025. Sundar Pichai said year-over-year search-query growth is the highest in five years, and he credited AI investment. Philipp Schindler told analysts that strong growth in AI Mode queries weighed on the result because monetization there is lower: Google is not showing as many ads in AI Mode as it does in ordinary search.

The cloud comparison is not a pure hosting match. Google Cloud’s revenue includes tensor-processing-unit systems that customers install in their own data centres. It did call those sales a meaningful contributor to revenue growth. Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud’s chief executive, said the company is seeing extraordinary demand, and executives told analysts to expect TPU sales to count for even more of Google Cloud next year.

Microsoft’s September-quarter revenue rose 19 percent to 92.3 billion dollars, one percentage point faster than the growth rate reported for the prior quarter, a figure Digitimes also carried. Microsoft 365 Commercial Cloud, the line that includes Copilot and the broader Office suite, rose 17 percent to 27.7 billion dollars, a slight acceleration from the June quarter. What Microsoft did not repeat was the paid Copilot seat count it had published before: 30 million at the end of June, up from 15 million at the end of 2025, each paying 30 dollars a month on top of the application fees. Satya Nadella said the number of customers paying for usage-based Copilot features grew 75 percent in the September quarter. CFO Amy Hood said average revenue per user rose because of that pay-as-you-go use. Late last month Microsoft folded Copilot features into one application, in part to steer people toward agents and usage billing, including tools set against Meta’s Muse.

Both companies are funding the same kind of build, and the quarter shows different proofs. Google’s cash flow went negative while cloud operating income tripled, and part of the cloud line is now chip hardware leaving the building. Microsoft kept commercial-cloud growth in the teens and stopped publishing the seat count that had been the simple evidence subscriptions were absorbing the spend. The next marker Kurian gave analysts is next year, when TPU sales are expected to weigh more on Google Cloud. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-cloud-closes-azure-microsoft-wins-day-investors) · [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261029VL215/microsoft-azure-copilot-revenue-growth-2027.html)

### On the Calendar
NewsCord said pre-orders for the touchscreen MacBook Pro open on October 30, with the official launch on November 6. Source: [newscord.org](https://newscord.org/article/apple-unveils-touchscreen-macbook-pro-with-proled-xdr-display-starting-at-us2899--Story_20261028_ApplestouchscreenMac377849b6)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Two-minute simulated worlds with live audio now let Genie 4 testers direct scenes.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google DeepMind's Genie 4, released in research preview, lets trusted testers run interactive worlds and change them while they run, with sound generated in the same pass. Apple has unveiled an M6 iMac from $1,499, with deliveries on November 6, and the FIA has named AWS its AI and cloud partner from club racing through Formula 1. OpenAI plans to buy Google's chips, and a Meta AI director has left to build a workspace aimed at Office and Google Workspace.

### Top News
**Google DeepMind Releases Genie 4 World Model With Real-Time Editing and Audio: AI Insider**
Google DeepMind has released Genie 4 in research preview for trusted testers. Users steer with keyboard controls and plain-language prompts, including mid-simulation changes to weather, camera, people and objects, and the model generates ambient sound, music and dialogue with the picture. MarkTechPost reports scene consistency of up to two minutes, double Genie 3, which it says ran at 720p and 24 frames per second with visual memory of about one minute after an August 2025 announcement. Gemini Omni anchors look and behavior; Gemini 3.8 Flash breaks a goal into steps, checks frames and replans if the user intervenes, and in one demo Gemini 4 Argon split a checkers task into steps that Genie 4 simulated with Apptronik's Apollo humanoid. Research director Tejas Kulkarni said future world models will be hybrids, with Gemini writing code and text while Genie simulates reality. All Genie 4 video and audio will carry SynthID watermarks; a waitlist is open, Google AI Ultra subscribers are due to get it in Project Genie, and early-access Gemini API and Google AI Studio partners follow, with The Hindu listing uses from creative direction and historical scenes to simulation after internal safety evaluations. Source: [theaiinsider.tech](https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/10/28/google-deepmind-releases-genie-4-world-model-with-real-time-editing-and-audio/)
Source: [marktechpost.com](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/28/google-deepmind-genie-4-world-model/)
Source: [thehindu.com](https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/technology/google-unveils-genie-4-world-model-powered-by-gemini-ai-models/article71634624.ece)

**Apple Unveils M6 iMac With Faster AI Performance, Starts at $1,499: Techeconomy**
Apple has unveiled a 24-inch iMac with the M6 chip, starting at $1,499, with pre-orders from Wednesday, October 28, in 35 countries and regions and deliveries from November 6. Apple says on-device AI is up to five times the M4 iMac, graphics up to twice the M4 model, performance up to 18 times the most popular Intel-based iMac, and LM Studio prompt processing up to 12 times the M1 iMac, with memory bandwidth of 170GB per second and SSD speeds up to twice the prior generation. A 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU model starts at $1,499; a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU model, two more cores than the previous generation, starts at $1,699, with education pricing of $1,449 and $1,599. The 4.5K Retina display is rated at 500 nits in seven colors, with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, macOS 27, a 12-megapixel Centre Stage camera, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports and support for two 6K external displays. A 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 and is due November 6, and 9to5Mac reports that iMac and that MacBook Pro keep the previous generation's prices. MacRumors says those pre-orders open at 10:10 a.m. Pacific Time, and Bloomberg, via MacRumors, expects still-unannounced OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros to be announced at today's "Pro and tell" event in Los Angeles, with expected prices from $2,899 for 14-inch and at least $3,399 for 16-inch; the already unveiled OLED iPad mini, from $699, opens for pre-order on the same clock. Source: [techeconomy.ng](https://techeconomy.ng/apple-m6-imac-macbook-pro-ai-performance)
Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/28/apple-open-pre-orders-five-new-products-today/)
Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/27/new-m6-macs-buck-apples-second-wave-of-price-hikes/)

**FIA Partners with AWS to Drive Innovation Across Global Motor Sport: Federation Internationale de l'Automobile**
The FIA has named Amazon Web Services its official partner for artificial intelligence, cloud computing, machine learning and cloud infrastructure, from club racing through Formula 1. AWS will help shape technical rules for the next generation of Formula 1 cars; the FIA already runs aerodynamic simulations on AWS high-performance computing so engineers can test airflow without building parts, and AWS will give technical teams AI tools for rules on safety, performance and sustainability. The deal extends the Digital Licensing Platform AWS developed and hosts, which The Next Web says launched in 2025, now reaching more national sporting authorities with more languages, FIA University links and licence renewals, with event management for volunteers and officials planned next. More business applications are set to move to AWS, work the FIA ties to doubling global motor sport participation, and AWS becomes an official partner of the FIA Awards and the FIA Sustainable Innovation Series. The agreement is separate from AWS's deal with Formula 1's commercial rights holder, cloud provider since 2018. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said the partnership can make it simpler for drivers, officials and volunteers to take part. Source: [fia.com](https://www.fia.com/news/fia-partners-aws-drive-innovation-across-global-motor-sport)
Source: [thenextweb.com](https://thenextweb.com/news/fia-aws-ai-cloud-partner)

**OpenAI Plans to Buy Google's Chips as Part of Its AI Build-Out: Bloomberg Technology**
OpenAI plans to buy artificial intelligence chips from Alphabet's Google, Bloomberg and The Information report, each citing a person familiar with the matter. Financial terms and other details of the tensor processing unit purchase could not be learned. The Information says OpenAI has been one of Nvidia's most valuable customers, and that Nvidia has invested tens of billions of dollars in the startup. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-28/openai-plans-to-buy-google-s-chips-as-part-of-its-ai-build-out)
Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/openai-longtime-nvidia-customer-plans-buy-googles-ai-chips)

**Meta AI director Rohit Patel quits after eight years to take on Microsoft Office and Google Workspace: Indian Television Dot Com**
Rohit Patel, a director at Meta Superintelligence Labs, is leaving after eight years to found Ndoc, aimed at replacing Microsoft Office and Google Workspace with one AI-native workspace. Three tabs split the work: Stage for decks, dashboards and mini apps, Narrative for analysis and citations, and Model for datasets and Python scripts, and users can ask the assistant to explain any script or formula. Ndoc is built on fine-tuned open-source models, keeps context across people, documents, teams and companies, and Patel plans to open-source a .ndoc.html format, which he tied to leaving rather than seeking consensus from hundreds of people at Meta. The startup has a team of three, has not raised outside funding, is in an enterprise pilot and limited alpha, and has connectors to import data from existing apps, with a beta expected in the coming weeks and a full launch in 2027. The exit follows Joel Kaplan, Andrew Tulloch and Emily Dalton Smith; OpenAI launched Space, a shared workspace inside ChatGPT, in September. Source: [indiantelevision.com](https://indiantelevision.com/mam/meta-ai-director-rohit-patel-quits-after-eight-years-to-take-on-microsoft-office-and-google-workspace/)

### The Thread: A prospectus, a reseller, and next year's TPU revenue
The Information reports that Anthropic's IPO prospectus records a plan to spend $114.5 billion with Google Cloud, and the filing does not split out how much of that sum is tensor processing unit compute. The same prospectus estimates a further $125 billion to $150 billion on TPUs with Google and other providers, and $161.2 billion for TPU compute with Broadcom, which co-designs the chips with Google. TPUs began as chips Google used only internally, starting more than a decade ago. Outside customers first reached them through Google Cloud in 2018.

Oracle is the new reseller in that stack. The Information says Google has said Oracle will be the first major cloud provider besides Google itself to offer TPUs to customers from Oracle's own data centers. Google began recognizing revenue from selling TPUs into outside data centers last quarter. Chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi said on that earnings call that only a small portion of revenue from those agreements showed up in the quarter, and that the vast majority kicks in next year.

John Blackledge of TD Cowen, in a report The Information cites from earlier this month, estimates TPU sales of $9.4 billion in the second half of this year, about 13 percent of the roughly $70 billion he forecasts for Google Cloud in that half. By 2028 he thinks TPUs could be a $138 billion business, 34 percent of his Google Cloud revenue estimate for that year. Analysts, on average, expect Nvidia to report $692 billion of revenue in the fiscal year ending January 2028. The Information notes that Blackledge's 2028 TPU figure would still be a fraction of that Nvidia total. Those are his estimate and the analysts' average, not figures Google or Nvidia have booked.

Meta is already a tenant on the same chip. The Information says it reported earlier this year that Meta struck a deal to rent TPUs from Google. Alphabet therefore has three commercial paths in one piece of reporting: a cloud commitment from Anthropic at prospectus scale, a sale channel through other companies' data centers with most of that revenue still ahead, and an existing rental with Meta. Nvidia's side of the comparison is the analyst revenue number, not a new chip announcement in this article. Oracle's role is to put Google silicon in a second cloud's buildings. The next dated marker the source names is next year, when Ashkenazi said the vast majority of outside-data-center TPU agreement revenue is due to be recognized. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-tpu-moment)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Nvidia will invest three billion dollars in Meta to scale Muse agents.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia will invest three billion dollars in Meta’s equity offering and the two companies are expanding work on Muse, including more Vera Rubin hardware. Microsoft opened a voluntary exit to about 60,000 eligible employees in four countries. Apple unveiled the iPad mini that had circulated as an OLED rumor, now with a shipping design, chip and price.

### Top News
**Nvidia puts $3 billion into Meta and expands the Muse partnership: NVIDIA Newsroom**
Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering, a planned commitment rather than a completed sale, as the companies expand work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve training and inference and to cut the cost of running those systems. Meta intends to expand deployment of Nvidia Vera Rubin systems and Vera CPUs for next-generation agents, plus Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4. The companies are also considering Nvidia’s OpenShell Reference Architecture for safer agent deployment and Sentry for monitoring agent behavior. Jensen Huang said agents are a new computing paradigm and that the partnership is meant to optimize infrastructure so Muse can serve billions of people. Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is how Meta brings personal superintelligence to everyone. Nvidia said Muse models and agents on its infrastructure have delivered frontier-level benchmark performance and surging consumer downloads since launch. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-meta-to-expand-collaboration-on-muse-and-muse-family-of-models-amid-robust-growth) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/nvidia-invests-3-billion-meta-deeper-ai-partnership) · [grafa.com](https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/nvidia-meta-3-billion-investment-ai-partnership)

**Microsoft opens a voluntary exit to about 60,000 employees: Instant Gaming News**
An internal memo from chief people officer Amy Coleman launched a time-limited voluntary separation programme for eligible employees at level 70 and below on participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States, about 60,000 people, roughly a quarter of the workforce. Coleman said it lets people who want a future outside Microsoft leave with support and gives participating organizations another way to match staffing to changing needs; some organizations are not offering it, and it builds on a voluntary programme earlier this year. Eligible people were to get an email with the terms. In India, where Microsoft has about 23,000 employees and eligibility was not broken out, the decision deadline is December 1, and the package is understood to match standard severance: one month of base salary per completed year, plus health insurance and career-transition services. A Microsoft spokesperson said the company is backing India’s AI ambitions with $20.5 billion committed from 2025 through 2029 and is on track to equip 20 million people in India with AI skills by 2030. Source: [news.instant-gaming.com](https://news.instant-gaming.com/en/articles/22684-microsoft-announces-a-voluntary-buyout-to-60-000-employees) · [hdfcsky.com](https://hdfcsky.com/news/microsoft-announces-voluntary-exit-offer-for-employees-in-india-3-other-countries)

**Apple unveils the iPad mini that had been an OLED rumor: The Hindu**
Apple unveiled the new iPad mini, calling it the biggest update ever: 5.4 millimetres thin, with an 8.5-inch OLED display, peak brightness of 1,200 nits, 600 nits full-screen for SDR and HDR, a 1-nit minimum and a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. It runs the A20 Pro with a 7-core GPU and neural accelerators in each GPU core; IOL reported the CPU up to 60 percent faster and the GPU about 2.7 times the prior model, with doubled memory bandwidth, and a 512GB model that adds a core on the CPU and dual 16-core Neural Engines. The tablet is IP67, rated for 1 metre for 30 minutes, with a 12-megapixel landscape front camera, a 12-megapixel wide back camera, Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 frames per second. Storage is 128GB, 256GB and 512GB, in Midnight and Starlight; the US price starts at $699, and in India Wi-Fi starts at ₹82,900, Wi-Fi plus cellular at ₹1,00,900, and education pricing at ₹76,900. Pre-orders open October 28 and sales begin November 6. Battery life is up to 10 hours, with a 50 percent charge in about 30 minutes on a 35-watt or higher adapter. Dave Pakula, vice president of Hardware Engineering, called it a huge leap for a full iPad in the palm of the hand. Siri AI arrives in beta with iPadOS 27. Source: [thehindu.com](https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/technology/apple-unveils-new-ipad-mini-with-thinner-design/article71630115.ece) · [iol.co.za](https://iol.co.za/technology/gadgets/2026-10-27-apple-unveils-redesigned-thinner-ipad-mini-with-oled-display/)

### Company Desk
**Apple ships iOS 27.2 with Siri recall and more than 160 fixes: MacRumors**
Apple released iOS 27.2, the first major iOS 27 update, putting the iPhone Duo and other iPhones on the same version. Siri AI can recall past conversations and draw on photos attached to Messages, calendar-event attendees and voicemails, with better results from Safari history and Reading List; it requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later, remains unavailable in the EU and mainland China, and adds French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish. The Times of India reported the sale is structured so Mark Zuckerberg can raise money without surrendering voting control, and that Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom are interested in buying shares. Source: [telecompaper.com](https://www.telecompaper.com/news/meta-announces-plans-to-sell-up-to-usd-95-billion-in-new-shares-to-fund-ai-plans--1586818) · [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/meta-plans-to-raise-up-to-95-billion-for-its-ai-expansion-through-two-stock-offerings-with-nvidia-amd-and-broadcom-interested-in-buying-shares-as-mark-zuckerberg-seeks-new-funding-without-surrendering-voting-control/articleshow/135226925.cms)

**Xero connects live books to Gemini: The Fintech Times**

**Google Classroom adds Gemini visibility for teachers: EdTech Innovation Hub**
Google is adding Gemini app publishing and teacher insights that let teachers see students’ Gemini notebook conversations. Source: [edtechinnovationhub.com](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/google-classroom-now-lets-teachers-see-students-gemini-notebook-conversations)

**DeepMind promotes Iason Gabriel: EdTech Innovation Hub**
Google DeepMind promoted Iason Gabriel to principal scientist and director at the DeepMind Institute. Source: [edtechinnovationhub.com](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/google-deepmind-promotes-iason-gabriel-to-principal-scientist-and-director-at-deepmind-institute)

### The Counterpoint
**Suppliers buying the customer is the circular-capital problem: The Times of India**
The same fundraising that Nvidia is joining is the one The Times of India flags as circular capital: silicon suppliers are eyeing a $5 billion stake while Meta sells shares to fund AI expansion, and Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom are among those interested in buying. A supplier writing a cheque into the customer that then buys that supplier’s systems is not an outside test of demand, and the Times framed Zuckerberg’s aim as new money without giving up voting control. Source: [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/meta-plans-to-raise-up-to-95-billion-for-its-ai-expansion-through-two-stock-offerings-with-nvidia-amd-and-broadcom-interested-in-buying-shares-as-mark-zuckerberg-seeks-new-funding-without-surrendering-voting-control/articleshow/135226925.cms)

### The Thread: Three cheques, one crowded shelf
Almost a quarter of a trillion dollars is the sum The Information put on three fundraising plans unveiled the same Monday, from Anthropic, SpaceX and Meta. SpaceX signed a $40 billion financing agreement with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management to lease graphics processors, which SpaceX called the largest GPU financing in history. Colleague Alex Eichenstein reported that the money is expected to run through a special purpose vehicle kept off SpaceX’s balance sheet, a structure that could limit any hit to its credit rating. Meta’s board committee, in a filing last week, said timing mattered so the company could secure capital before competitors saturate funding options, and it named a congested pipeline that includes Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI. Microsoft is the other of the seven in that piece, and the new number is take-up rather than eligibility: the global workforce is 223,000, an earlier voluntary offer went to 9,000 people and about a third accepted, and Microsoft is expected to see a smaller share this time, fewer than 20,000.

The shared constraint is the funding shelf, not a shared product. Meta’s directors treated Alphabet’s deals as occupying the same equity and debt options Meta wants to use before they fill up. Microsoft is offering exits while that window is still described as open. The Apollo lease is the article’s exhibit that a company with Elon Musk’s platform is choosing an off-balance-sheet GPU structure rather than a plain borrowing. Musk, in a post on X that The Information quotes, said debt markets in recent weeks have closed to firms whose revenue is only from AI data centers, and that more than 200 neoclouds face what he called guppy-level death and consolidation. The Information notes that the argument is self-serving: fewer neoclouds could leave more capital for SpaceX and other large names later. Apollo’s chief economist, Torsten Slok, wrote over the weekend that despite the investment and the hype, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech.

For Meta, the filing turns the raise into a race against other people’s calendars, including Alphabet’s, rather than a quiet registration. For Microsoft, the buyout math is the operational twin of the same squeeze: on the take-up the company is expected to see, the offer does not empty a quarter of a 223,000-person company. The risk the piece leaves on the table is Slok’s zero, and Musk’s warning that investor disfavor could spread from neoclouds to larger AI companies if customers keep seeing no payoff. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/anthropic-spacex-meta-cash-grabs)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Unilever cut order handling from twenty minutes to ninety seconds for retailers.**

**What You Need to Know:** Unilever cut order handling from twenty minutes to ninety seconds for retailers, using a Microsoft-built agent system now running in production. NVIDIA published a full reference architecture for containing enterprise agents, Mazda put Gemini in a Canadian CX-5, and a New Mexico order plus a California tax arrangement landed on Meta the same week Apple blocked a set of weak web certificates.

### Top News
**Unilever’s multi-agent creating customer value at global scale: Microsoft UK Stories**
Unilever has launched NOVA, five AI agents built with Microsoft on Foundry, to read, check and enter customer orders that still arrive as emails, PDFs, spreadsheets or photos. Microsoft UK Stories reports that about 300,000 direct customers are served, and that 3.7 billion people use a Unilever product every day. Four agents read the message and extract the order; a fifth checks the work. Francis Castro, head of technology for customer operations, says orders in the pilots are eight times faster than before, refund claims are processed twice as fast, and new-customer onboarding has been reduced by 90 percent. Microsoft engineers joined Unilever to build and test claims validation in less than eight weeks. NOVA has already processed thousands of orders in production. Source: [ukstories.microsoft.com](https://ukstories.microsoft.com/features/unilevers-multi-agent-creating-customer-value-at-global-scale/)

**NVIDIA unveils architecture for secure enterprise AI agents: Engineering.com**
NVIDIA today announced the OpenShell Reference Architecture for building, containing and enforcing safe agents, extending the OpenShell secure runtime it had already set out. Engineering.com reports that Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are said to deliver 30 times higher throughput per megawatt on agentic workloads, while Vera CPUs are said to deliver twice the performance of x86 processors and to run the OpenShell boundary. BlueField-4 runs NVIDIA Sentry, which quarantines an agent that leaves its software boundary in milliseconds and boosts agent capacity by up to 20 percent. ServiceNow said Arc, a personal long-running agent, is generally available, with policies carried to OpenShell and Sentry so access can be revoked across software and hardware within seconds. The stack is described as able to run on Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, including Microsoft Windows via Microsoft Execution Containers, and to host agents from builders including Google, Meta and OpenAI. Source: [engineering.com](https://www.engineering.com/nvidia-unveils-architecture-for-secure-enterprise-ai-agents/)

**Google Gemini Enhances the Connected Driving Experience in the All-New Mazda CX-5: Chinook Observer**
Mazda Canada said on October 26 that Google Gemini is available to eligible users in the all-new CX-5 equipped with Google built-in. Drivers can use everyday language, including follow-up requests, for navigation, Google Maps traffic and recommendations, Spotify and YouTube Music, hands-free messages, and supported vehicle functions such as climate. Tasks started on a smartphone can continue in the car through compatible Google services. Amy Fleming, president and CEO of Mazda Canada, said the aim is technology that stays in the background so the driver stays on the road. Mazda Canada’s retail network is 163 stores. Source: [pr.chinookobserver.com](https://pr.chinookobserver.com/article/Google-Gemini-Enhances-the-Connected-Driving-Experience-in-the-All-New-Mazda-CX-5/6adf095adba4ed9cc76d96b2)

**Apple Addresses Web Security Threat, Working on macOS Update With Additional Fix: MacRumors**
Apple has been blocking eMudhra’s compromised TLS certificates since October 19 in Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple’s networking and security frameworks, MacRumors reports from Apple’s support document. A researcher found that private keys on eight of the Indian firm’s intermediate certificate-authority certificates were weak; those keys could have allowed impersonation of legitimate sites, and Apple says there is currently no evidence of malicious exploitation. The block is automatic and does not require a software update for most devices. macOS command-line tools can still accept the certificates until a macOS update changes the default /etc/ssl/cert.pem file; until then, administrators can remove the root CA certificates from that file. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/25/apple-blocks-compromised-emudhra-certificates/)

**Meta loses $124bn in value as AI spending plans hit US tech shares: Business Matters**
A New Mexico judge on Wednesday ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over its handling of Facebook user data, and Meta plans to appeal, Business Matters reports. Separately, the board plans to award Mark Zuckerberg, 42, Class C non-voting shares he could sell to pay a possible California billionaire wealth tax without giving up control. He owns about 13 percent of Meta and controls about 61 percent of its votes; he told the board that selling existing shares to pay the tax would cut his voting power to 53 percent. He has pledged to remain living in California for the next eight years. The proposed tax is a one-off 5 percent levy on the assets of any billionaire living in the state on January 1, 2026. A special committee said its negotiations with him were protracted and, at several points, contentious, and concluded that his presence at headquarters in Menlo Park was critical. Source: [bmmagazine.co.uk](https://bmmagazine.co.uk/ai/meta-ai-spending-tech-sell-off/)

### Company Desk
**Springer Nature and Google DeepMind partner on AI peer review assistant: Research Information**
Springer Nature and Google DeepMind have announced a research partnership to build an AI peer-review assistant that helps reviewers navigate manuscripts, charts and figures without replacing human judgement. Research Information reports that a prototype is in test, built with Google’s open-source Agent Development Kit and run inside Springer Nature’s private Gemini Enterprise environment so manuscripts used in development stay on Springer Nature’s infrastructure. The project builds on Google tools including ScholarPeer and Deep Review, and on Springer Nature’s in-house platform Snapp. Saskia Steinacker, chief product officer at Springer Nature, said reviewer expertise remains fundamental and that innovation and trust have to move together. Seshu Ajjarapu, senior director of applied AI at Google DeepMind, said the aim is a review experience that keeps pace with submission volume while holding journal standards. Source: [researchinformation.info](https://www.researchinformation.info/news/springer-nature-and-google-deepmind-partner-on-ai-peer-review-assistant/)

**Apple Display Veterans Step Back as New Leaders Take Over: MacRumors**
Victor Yin now oversees much of Apple’s display development, after years of preparation under Wei Chen and John Zhong, MacRumors reports from Mark Gurman. Chen and Zhong, each with about 30 years at Apple, are moving to more limited roles as advisers, in a succession Gurman describes as underway for several years. October promotions made Rajesh Ambati, Louie Sanguinetti and Derek Shaeffer vice presidents, covering connectivity hardware and software. The shifts follow Apple’s expansion of Johny Srouji’s role to chief hardware officer, putting hardware engineering and hardware technologies under him. Gurman also reports that some hardware program managers have been laid off in recent weeks as Srouji and CEO John Ternus remove management layers. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/26/apple-display-veterans-step-back/)

### The Counterpoint
**The ninety-second cut is still a pilot: Microsoft UK Stories**
The time cut is Castro’s figure for 11 pilot markets, not for the order book as a whole. Unilever still takes about two million orders a year in non-standard formats, out of about 20 million, and those are the ones NOVA is built to catch. The plan is to expand past 50 markets. In the pilots, orders are 95 percent touchless, with people still stepping in on exceptions, and Deepalok Roy Chowdhury said there was apprehension when the work started. Whether ninety seconds survives contact with the other markets is the number that decides it: the touchless rate once those 50 are in production, not the rate inside the 11. Source: [ukstories.microsoft.com](https://ukstories.microsoft.com/features/unilevers-multi-agent-creating-customer-value-at-global-scale/)

### The Thread: Two clouds inside one Korean bank
More than 2,000 servers and more than 100 services already run in Amazon Web Services for KB Financial Group. In 2020 the group became the first South Korean financial group to sign a corporate contract for AWS financial cloud, Seoul Economic Daily reports, and AWS has now invited AI executives from the group and from KB Kookmin Bank to its Executive Briefing Center.

Alphabet is already inside the same group. In July, KB worked with Google Cloud on KB Davis, a Gemini-based data analytics AI, and on KB Star Byeoli, a customer consultation AI. As internal AI services multiply, KB Kookmin Bank is trying to link AWS, Google Cloud and its own AI systems so the data those tools need can move between them.

The 2020 contract was a diversification, not a swap. KB wanted more than one cloud so a single provider could not become a single point of failure, and it wanted AWS technologies in financial services faster. The practical result was a parallel estate: AWS was added to the group platform Cleon, and the group now runs that estate of more than 2,000 servers and more than 100 services beside whatever it already had.

The newer layer is models, not racks. Amazon Bedrock lets a financial firm call an outside model, including Anthropic’s Claude, inside AWS security and management controls, without training the model itself. KB is tying internal systems to Bedrock at individual affiliates. The named ones are an AI investment-product information service at KB Asset Management, an AI development and operations platform for employees at KB Securities, and a customized real-estate information service at KB Kookmin Bank.

The sharpest build is the KB AI Dev Center, a dedicated AI software unit the bank opened in July this year. Developers describe the function they want in ordinary language. AI then supports design, coding and testing. AWS provided technical support for that development environment and for its monitoring framework, according to the paper’s sources. That is Amazon inside the bank’s software factory, not only inside its data center.

Google’s July work sits on the other side of the same factory. Davis is analytics. Star Byeoli is the customer conversation. Neither replaces Bedrock, and Bedrock does not replace them. The bank’s stated problem is the join: an environment in which AWS, Google Cloud and internal systems can share the data a given service needs. A deeper AWS briefing, which the paper says AWS proposed after taking an interest in how KB built its AI development framework, is a contest for the next workload between two suppliers the group already pays.

What changes for Amazon is a flagship financial account moving from a 2020 infrastructure contract into agent-style development, on an invitation AWS itself extended. What changes for Alphabet is that two named Gemini tools are already in the group, so any new AWS scope is won against an incumbent, not into an empty seat. What changes for KB is operational: more of the design-to-test loop sits with a vendor runtime, and the data path between the two clouds becomes the constraint on how far either assistant can go.

A KB Financial official said being invited to speak directly with senior AWS officials is itself meaningful, and that the group will look at further technical support and at how overseas financial firms use AI. The Seoul Economic Daily account is by Do Hye-won and was AI-translated from Korean; the paper warns that quotes from foreign sources may not match the original wording. The cooperation the official described is the scope still open: global practice, and more technical support for a framework that already spans both clouds. Source: [en.sedaily.com](https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/10/26/kb-financial-group-deepens-aws-tie-up-to-speed-ai-banking)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **IP68 failed: dust killed the iPhone Duo's inner display.**

**What You Need to Know:** Dust entered the iPhone Duo's hinge in JerryRigEverything's test and left the inner display unresponsive, despite the phone's IP68 rating. Teardowns the same day put the two battery cells at a combined 4,883 mAh. Sweden's Government Offices will block ChatGPT and Claude on staff computers from October 26 and leave Microsoft Copilot as the only approved assistant.

### Top News
**iPhone Duo fails a dusty durability test: MacRumors**
JerryRigEverything's test got dust into the iPhone Duo hinge through several ingress points, and the dust overwhelmed the magnets that hold the phone shut. The bend test then left a permanent green line across the inner display, and the screen became unresponsive. The outer screen, with Ceramic Shield 2, scratched at level 7 on the Mohs scale. The inner screen managed level 2, though its matte nano-texture coating made marks disappear. Nelson, who said he has been testing folding phones since the first generation seven years ago and that most survive, said the iPhone Duo did not. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/24/iphone-duo-fails-jerryrigeverything-test/)

**iPhone Duo teardowns show two batteries and a repair path: MacRumors**
REWA Technology and Phone Repair Guru posted the first teardown videos. The phone has two battery cells that come out with electrically activated adhesive: a larger cell rated 2,962 mAh (11.56 Wh) and a smaller one rated 1,921 mAh (7.5 Wh), for 4,883 mAh in total. REWA's labeled logic board shows Apple's A20 Pro chip and C2 cellular modem. Phone Repair Guru found the Touch ID button can be removed for repair, but called the process difficult, and said the USB-C port is fully modular. The Duo is eSIM-only worldwide. Apple has published its repair manual, and iFixit is expected to post a fuller teardown in the coming days. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/24/iphone-duo-teardown-videos/)

**Sweden blocks ChatGPT and Claude, keeps Microsoft Copilot: Decrypt**
Sweden's Government Offices will block ChatGPT and Claude on staff computers from Monday, October 26, and direct civil servants to Microsoft Copilot as the only approved assistant, Sveriges Radio reported. Mikael Wettercrantz, the offices' director of digitalisation, wrote on the staff intranet that using AI services without a formal contract can have consequences for information security, citing both the sensitivity of information entered and how AI-generated responses were handled. Consumer tools without a formal agreement send queries to external company servers, and U.S. law can compel those companies to hand data over. Copilot cleared a review in which the offices raised its security settings; ChatGPT and Claude did not get that treatment. Some employees can still reach both blocked tools through an internal platform the offices built. The Tax Agency and the National Board of Institutional Care have already banned consumer AI tools. The Enforcement Authority is preparing its own decision. A Transport Administration audit found roughly 10 AI services in use in a widespread and risky way. In February the European Parliament disabled ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot on parliamentary devices. Microsoft added Claude models to Copilot in early 2026; in the EU those Anthropic models default to off unless an administrator enables them, and the Government Offices have not confirmed whether Claude is switched on in their Copilot. Source: [decrypt.co](https://decrypt.co/381763/sweden-government-offices-block-chatgpt-claude)
Source: [kucoin.com](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/sweden-bans-chatgpt-and-claude-approves-microsoft-copilot-for-government-use)
Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/bbaca341-1519-4ceb-80a0-019739082f0a)

The Information reports that Meta is a CoreWeave customer to the tune of $35 billion. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/neoclouds-gathering-storm)

### The Counterpoint
**The outer glass held at Mohs 7: MacRumors**
The same JerryRigEverything write-up that records the hinge failure also credits the outer display. Ceramic Shield 2 on that outer screen scratched only at level 7 on the Mohs scale, and the inner panel's matte nano-texture made marks disappear. Those two results cut against reading the test as a soft phone from edge to edge. They do not clear the device: the inner screen still stopped at level 2, the bend test left a permanent green line, and Nelson's verdict was that the Duo did not survive. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/24/iphone-duo-fails-jerryrigeverything-test/)

### The Thread: Version 66.0 lands on Apple TV
Version 66.0 is the build number Apple's TV-specific release metadata assigns to Instagram, and that metadata dates the build to October 23. That is the first day Instagram is on Apple TV. An archived App Store listing from October 19 still showed compatibility with only the iPhone and the iPad. The app plays Reels, longer videos, and live shows. Users can watch content from creators they follow, discover videos, and resume watching across devices. Instagram describes the app as a way to watch together with friends and family, which puts a feed built for a phone onto a screen a room can share.

Meta did not start that television job on Apple's hardware. Instagram first began testing its TV app on Amazon Fire TV devices in the United States in December 2025, before expanding to Google TV in February 2026 and to Samsung smart TVs in June. The initial experience focused on Reels organized into channels based on viewers' interests, with videos playing automatically. In June, Meta outlined plans to expand beyond short videos with longer creator content, episodic series, and live broadcasts. The Apple TV app's description lists longer videos and live shows alongside Reels, which means the June plan is the list that reached Apple's store. The release follows Instagram's dedicated iPad app, which arrived in September 2025 after years of requests for an interface designed for Apple's tablets. The Apple TV app requires tvOS 26.0 or later, and it is on the Apple TV App Store.

The dependency is the store and the operating system, not a shared balance sheet. Meta can reach Apple's streaming device only if Apple lists the app and only on tvOS 26.0 or later. Apple's box, in turn, now carries a Meta catalog — Reels, longer videos, and live shows — next to the shows Apple sells under its own TV brand. Resume-across-devices is the practical link: a video started on an iPhone can continue on Apple TV, so Meta's account and Apple's screen are in the same session. The earlier dates show a platform tour, not a one-company launch. December 2025 was a test on Amazon's Fire TV, in the United States. February 2026 was Google TV. June was Samsung, and June was also when Meta said the product would leave short video behind. October 19 is the last listing in today's record that still stopped at iPhone and iPad. October 23 is version 66.0 on Apple TV. September 2025 is the tablet step that came before the television step on Apple's own hardware. No article here states a price for the app, a user count, or a date for a following version. What changed, with dates attached, is availability: from a test on Amazon's living-room device, through Google TV and Samsung, to a shipping app on Apple's. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/25/instagram-launches-apple-tv-app/)
